resetByChannel.description: Provides channel-specific reset overrides keyed by provider/channel id for fine-grained behavior control. Use this only when one channel needs exceptional reset behavior beyond type-level policies.

store.title: Session Store Path
store.description: Sets the session storage file path used to persist session records across restarts. Use an explicit path only when you need custom disk layout, backup routing, or mounted-volume storage.

mainKey.title: Session Main Key
mainKey.description: Accepted but ignored: the per-agent main session suffix is always "main". Omit this field; global session scope uses "global" instead.

default.title: Session Send Policy Default Action
default.description: Sets fallback action when no sendPolicy rule matches: "allow" or "deny". Keep "allow" for simpler setups, or choose "deny" when you require explicit allow rules for every destination.

action.title: Session Send Rule Action
action.description: Defines rule decision as "allow" or "deny" when the corresponding match criteria are satisfied. Use deny-first ordering when enforcing strict boundaries with explicit allow exceptions.

channel.title: Session Send Rule Channel
channel.description: Matches rule application to a specific channel/provider id (for example discord, telegram, slack). Use this when one channel should permit or deny delivery independently of others.

chatType.title: Session Send Rule Chat Type
chatType.description: Matches rule application to chat type (direct, group, thread) so behavior varies by conversation form. Use this when DM and group destinations require different safety boundaries.

keyPrefix.title: Session Send Rule Key Prefix
keyPrefix.description: Matches a normalized session-key prefix after internal key normalization steps in policy consumers. Use this for general prefix controls, and prefer rawKeyPrefix when exact full-key matching is required.

rawKeyPrefix.title: Session Send Rule Raw Key Prefix
rawKeyPrefix.description: Matches the raw, unnormalized session-key prefix for exact full-key policy targeting. Use this when normalized keyPrefix is too broad and you need agent-prefixed or transport-specific precision.

match.title: Session Send Rule Match
match.description: Defines optional rule match conditions that can combine channel, chatType, and key-prefix constraints. Keep matches narrow so policy intent stays readable and debugging remains straightforward.

rules.title: Session Send Policy Rules
rules.description: Ordered allow/deny rules evaluated before the default action, for example `{ action: "deny", match: { channel: "discord" } }`. Put most specific rules first so broad rules do not shadow exceptions.

sendPolicy.title: Session Send Policy
sendPolicy.description: Controls session delivery using allow/deny rules evaluated against channel, chatType, and key prefixes. This is separate from incoming and outgoing peer-message admission; use session.communication for those defaults.

send.title: Send Messages to Other Sessions
send.description: Default for initiating messages to other sessions: always permits, ask requires human approval before sending, and never blocks. Requested replies and authorized delegated-task communication keep their existing authority.

receive.title: Receive Messages from Other Sessions
receive.description: Default for accepting new messages from other sessions: always permits, ask requires human approval before model input or new work, and never blocks. This does not change history visibility or human access.

communication.title: Session Communication Defaults
communication.description: Defaults for new messages between sessions. Each direction accepts always, ask, or never and defaults to always. Sessions inherit these values until a human selects an override; existing access restrictions still apply.

enabled.title: Thread Binding Enabled
enabled.description: Global master switch for thread-bound session spawning, routing, and delivery. Disable to turn off thread binding globally.

idleHours.title: Thread Binding Idle Timeout (hours)
idleHours.description: Default inactivity window in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables idle expiry). Default: 24.

maxAgeHours.title: Thread Binding Max Age (hours)
maxAgeHours.description: Optional hard max age in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables hard cap). Default: 0.

spawnSessions.title: Thread-Bound Session Spawns
spawnSessions.description: Global default gate for creating thread-bound work sessions from sessions_spawn and ACP thread spawns. Default: true when thread bindings are enabled.

defaultSpawnContext.title: Thread Spawn Context
defaultSpawnContext.description: Default native subagent context for thread-bound spawns. Use "fork" to start from the requester chat or "isolated" for a clean child. Default: "fork".

threadBindings.title: Session Thread Bindings
threadBindings.description: Shared defaults for thread-bound session spawning and routing across supported channels. Configure global defaults here and override per channel only when behavior differs.

readOnly.title: Allow Read-only Sessions
readOnly.description: Allows sessions to be made read-only for non-participants. Default: true.

suggest.title: Allow Suggest Sessions
suggest.description: Allows suggest visibility. In this phase it enforces the same admission policy as read-only; suggestion queues are configured by a later feature. Default: true.

drafts.title: Allow Draft Sessions
drafts.description: Allows draft visibility, which hides sessions from non-owner, non-admin operators. Default: true.

sharing.title: Session Sharing Modes
sharing.description: Controls which collaboration modes session owners and administrators may select. Omitted booleans default to enabled; set a mode false to remove it from the picker and reject new selections.

mode.title: Session Maintenance Mode
mode.description: Determines whether pruning and disk-budget policies are only reported ("warn") or actively applied ("enforce"). Keep "warn" during rollout and switch to "enforce" after validating safe thresholds. Cold storage is enabled by default and has its own opt-out setting.

enabled.title: Automatically Archive Old Chats
enabled.description: Enables background chat archival (default true). Set false to disable future extraction. A worker checks for eligible chats every minute. This archive policy is separate from deletion and disk-budget cleanup.

afterDays.title: Archive After Inactive Days
afterDays.description: Archive chats after this many inactive days (positive integer, default 30). Active work is protected; changing the cutoff takes effect on the next worker pass without a Gateway restart.

coldStorage.title: Chat Cold Storage
coldStorage.description: Moves inactive chats into compressed JSONL archives while retaining session metadata. Archive files become required history and must be included in backups. Changes apply without restarting the Gateway.

pruneAfter.title: Session Prune After
pruneAfter.description: Archives eligible durable conversations and removes disposable automation entries older than this duration (default `30d`; for example `12h`). Archived conversations retain their history and can be restored; protected or routable conversations remain active.

archiveDashboardAfter.title: Archive Inactive Dashboard Sessions After
archiveDashboardAfter.description: Archives inactive sessions started in the OpenClaw app after this duration (for example `7d`) so they remain available without crowding the active session list. Set `false` or `0` to disable this automatic archiving.

maxEntries.title: Session Max Entries
maxEntries.description: Caps unarchived session entries (default 5000). Eligible durable overflow conversations are archived with their history; disposable automation entries are removed. Existing archives do not consume the cap. Protected active entries still count and can keep the store above the limit.

preserveRecent.title: Preserve Recent Sessions
preserveRecent.description: Protects interactive sessions active within this duration (for example `7d`) from automatic age, count, and disk-budget history eviction. Unset or `false` keeps the normal oldest-first policy. Synthetic model-run, cron, hook, heartbeat, ACP, and sub-agent rows remain eligible for bounded cleanup.

resetArchiveRetention.title: Session Reset Archive Retention
resetArchiveRetention.description: Age-based retention for archived chats (`*.reset.<timestamp>` and `*.deleted.<timestamp>`). Defaults to keeping archives until the disk budget evicts them oldest-first; set a duration (for example `30d`) to opt into wall-clock deletion, or `false` to disable it explicitly.

maxDiskBytes.title: Session Max Disk Budget
maxDiskBytes.description: Per-agent physical disk budget covering SQLite main/WAL and counted session-directory artifacts (for example `500mb`). Defaults to `10gb`; protected data can keep usage above the target. When exceeded, warn mode reports pressure and enforce mode removes old reset/delete artifacts, unreferenced history, then cap-created archives. Manual, age-retention, app-session, recovery, and legacy archives remain protected. Set `false`, `0`, or `"0"` to disable.

highWaterBytes.title: Session Disk High-water Target
highWaterBytes.description: Target size after disk-budget cleanup (high-water mark). Defaults to 80% of maxDiskBytes; set explicitly for tighter reclaim behavior on constrained disks. A value that resolves to zero falls back to the default; negative values are invalid. Disable the budget with maxDiskBytes instead.

maintenance.title: Session Maintenance
maintenance.description: Automatic session-store maintenance controls for app-session archiving, pruning age, entry caps, reset archive retention, and disk budget cleanup. Start in warn mode to observe impact, then enforce once thresholds are tuned.

session.title: Session
session.description: Global session routing, reset, delivery policy, and maintenance controls for conversation history behavior. Keep defaults unless you need stricter isolation, retention, or delivery constraints.

enabled.title: Automations Enabled
enabled.description: Enables automation execution for stored schedules managed by the gateway. Keep enabled for normal reminder/automation flows, and disable only to pause all automation execution without deleting jobs.

defaultTools.title: Automation Default Tools
defaultTools.description: Tools added when the automations tool creates or explicitly revises a nonempty toolsAllow list, before creator-policy checks and approval. Unset adds nothing. Use toolsAllowMode: "exact" on that request to opt out; [] remains tool-less. Existing jobs and unrelated edits are unchanged.

skipMissedJobs.title: Skip Missed Recurring Automations
skipMissedJobs.description: Skips missed recurring cron/every slots at Gateway startup and schedules their next future occurrence instead of catching up. Default: false. Enable to avoid stale reminders after downtime; one-shot at jobs still catch up.

webhookToken.title: Automations Webhook Bearer Token
webhookToken.description: Bearer token attached to automation webhook POST deliveries when webhook mode is used. Prefer secret/env substitution and rotate this token regularly if shared webhook endpoints are internet-reachable.

dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.title: Automations Webhook Dangerously Allow Private Network
dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.description: Allows automation webhooks to private and internal network targets. Keep disabled unless every configured webhook destination is trusted.

allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange.title: Automations Webhook Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
allowRfc2544BenchmarkRange.description: Allows automation webhooks to RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

allowIpv6UniqueLocalRange.title: Automations Webhook Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
allowIpv6UniqueLocalRange.description: Allows automation webhooks to IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

allowedHostnames.title: Automations Webhook Allowed Hostnames
allowedHostnames.description: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed for automation webhook delivery, including otherwise blocked targets. Keep the list minimal.

blockedHostnames.title: Automations Webhook Blocked Hostnames
blockedHostnames.description: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules for automation webhook delivery. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

webhookSsrfPolicy.title: Automations Webhook SSRF Policy
webhookSsrfPolicy.description: SSRF policy applied to every outbound automation webhook. Private, loopback, link-local, and internal targets stay blocked unless this policy explicitly allows them. Keep unset for strict delivery.

sessionRetention.title: Automations Session Retention
sessionRetention.description: Controls how long completed automation run sessions are kept before pruning (`24h`, `7d`, `1h30m`, or `false` to disable pruning; a zero duration such as `0h` also disables; default: `24h`). Use shorter retention to reduce storage growth on high-frequency schedules.

channel.title: Automations Default Delivery Channel
channel.description: Channel for the default destination, such as `telegram`. Omit to use `last` resolution against the default recipient.

to.title: Automations Default Delivery Recipient
to.description: Recipient for the default destination, in the channel's target syntax (for example a Telegram chat id such as `-100123456789`).

threadId.title: Automations Default Delivery Thread
threadId.description: Optional thread or forum topic for the default destination, such as a Telegram topic id.

accountId.title: Automations Default Delivery Account
accountId.description: Optional channel account for the default destination when the channel has several accounts.

delivery.title: Automations Default Delivery
delivery.description: Gateway-wide default announce destination for automations that name no route of their own (no channel other than `last`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`, or owner targeting). It replaces the remembered session route at run time and never applies to `none` or `webhook` delivery. A `cron.creators.<profileId>.delivery` or `cron.agents.<agentId>.delivery` default wins over this one.

delivery.title: Agent Automations Default Delivery
delivery.description: Default announce destination for this agent's automations that name no route. Replaces `cron.delivery` whole for this agent; fields are not merged. A creator default for the job's human creator wins over it.

failureAlert.title: Agent Automations Failure Alert Route
failureAlert.description: Default failure-alert route (`mode`, `channel`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`) for this agent's automations. Replaces the `cron.failureAlert` route fields whole; `enabled`, `after`, `cooldownMs`, and `includeSkipped` stay Gateway-wide.

agents.title: Automations Per-agent Defaults
agents.description: Per-agent automation defaults keyed by agent id. Each automation uses the entry for its effective agent (its agentId, else the agent in its session key, else the default agent).

delivery.title: Creator Automations Default Delivery
delivery.description: Default announce destination for this person's automations that name no route. Wins over `cron.agents.<agentId>.delivery` and `cron.delivery`; replaces them whole.

failureAlert.title: Creator Automations Failure Alert Route
failureAlert.description: Default failure-alert route (`mode`, `channel`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`) for this person's automations. Wins over the owner agent's route and replaces the `cron.failureAlert` route fields whole; `enabled`, `after`, `cooldownMs`, and `includeSkipped` stay Gateway-wide.

creators.title: Automations Per-creator Defaults
creators.description: Per-creator automation defaults keyed by the Gateway profile id of the human who created the automation. Applies only when the automation records a human profile creator (directly, or as the profile that delegated creation to an agent); legacy automations and channel-only, unknown, agent, or system creators use no creator entry. Keys match exactly.

cron.title: Automations
cron.description: Global scheduler settings for stored automations, run concurrency, delivery fallback, and run-session retention. Keep defaults unless you are scaling automation volume or integrating external webhook receivers.

enabled.title: Transcripts Enabled
enabled.description: Enables durable automatic meeting notes, the transcripts agent tool, and configured auto-start sources. Default: true. Set false to disable persistence and the tool; explicit meeting transcribe mode retains its bounded live tail.

providerId.title: Transcript Source Provider ID
providerId.description: Transcript source provider id, such as a Discord voice or future Slack huddle provider. Use the exact id exposed by the provider plugin.

whenOccupied.title: Transcript Capture When Occupied
whenOccupied.description: Start a fresh transcript session each time humans are present in the source and stop it (generating notes) after the last human leaves. Requires a provider that reports occupancy, such as discord-voice. Default: false (capture continuously from gateway start).

sessionId.title: Transcript Session ID
sessionId.description: Optional fixed transcript session id for this auto-start source. Ignored when whenOccupied is true. Leave unset for generated ids unless you need a stable daily selector and can avoid same-day collisions.

title.title: Transcript Title
title.description: Optional title for future transcript captures. Changing only titles keeps current captures running and does not rename their admitted title or saved notes. Other source changes retain their normal restart handling.

accountId.title: Transcript Account ID
accountId.description: Optional provider account or workspace identifier for transcript sources that need account disambiguation. Use the provider's documented account id format.

guildId.title: Discord Guild ID
guildId.description: Optional Discord guild id for Discord voice transcript sources. Configure this with the matching channelId when the provider needs guild-scoped voice channel lookup.

channelId.title: Transcript Channel ID
channelId.description: Provider channel id for the live transcript source, such as a Discord voice channel or Slack huddle channel. Verify provider-specific id semantics before enabling auto-start.

meetingUrl.title: Transcript Meeting URL
meetingUrl.description: Optional meeting URL for providers that join by URL instead of channel id. Use only trusted meeting links because auto-start may join and capture that meeting.

autoStart.title: Transcripts Auto-start Sources
autoStart.description: Live transcript sources managed automatically from gateway startup. Each entry is enabled by being present; remove an entry to disable that source. Sources capture continuously unless whenOccupied is enabled.

transcripts.title: Transcripts
transcripts.description: Core transcript capture settings for meeting notes, recording-capable agent tools, and configured live meeting auto-start sources. Meeting plugins capture durable notes by default; set enabled to false to opt out globally.

enabled.title: Hooks Enabled
enabled.description: Enables the hooks endpoint and mapping execution pipeline for inbound webhook requests. Keep disabled unless you are actively routing external events into the gateway.

path.title: Hooks Endpoint Path
path.description: HTTP path used by the hooks endpoint (for example `/hooks`) on the gateway control server. Use a non-guessable path and combine it with token validation for defense in depth.

token.title: Hooks Auth Token
token.description: Shared bearer token checked by hooks ingress for request authentication before mappings run. Treat holders as full-trust callers for the hook ingress surface, not as a separate non-owner role. Use environment substitution and rotate regularly when webhook endpoints are internet-accessible.

defaultSessionKey.title: Hooks Default Session Key
defaultSessionKey.description: Fallback session key used for hook deliveries when a request does not provide one through allowed channels. Use a stable but scoped key to avoid mixing unrelated automation conversations.

allowRequestSessionKey.title: Hooks Allow Request Session Key
allowRequestSessionKey.description: Allows callers to supply a session key in hook requests when true, enabling caller-controlled routing. Keep false unless trusted integrators explicitly need custom session threading.

allowedSessionKeyPrefixes.title: Hooks Allowed Session Key Prefixes
allowedSessionKeyPrefixes.description: Allowlist of accepted session-key prefixes for inbound hook requests when caller-provided keys are enabled. Use narrow prefixes to prevent arbitrary session-key injection.

allowedAgentIds.title: Hooks Allowed Agent IDs
allowedAgentIds.description: Allowlist of effective agent IDs that hook requests and mappings are allowed to target, including default-agent routing when agentId is omitted. Use this to constrain automation events to dedicated service agents and limit the damage if a hook token is exposed.

presets.title: Hooks Presets
presets.description: Named hook preset bundles applied at load time to seed standard mappings and behavior defaults. Keep preset usage explicit so operators can audit which automations are active.

transformsDir.title: Hooks Transforms Directory
transformsDir.description: Base directory for hook transform modules referenced by mapping transform.module paths. Use a controlled repo directory so dynamic imports remain reviewable and predictable.

id.title: Hook Mapping ID
id.description: Optional stable identifier for a hook mapping entry used for auditing, troubleshooting, and targeted updates. Use unique IDs so logs and config diffs can reference mappings unambiguously.

path.title: Hook Mapping Match Path
path.description: Path match condition for a hook mapping, usually compared against the inbound request path. Use this to split automation behavior by webhook endpoint path families.

source.title: Hook Mapping Match Source
source.description: Source match condition for a hook mapping, typically set by trusted upstream metadata or adapter logic. Use stable source identifiers so routing stays the same across retries.

match.title: Hook Mapping Match
match.description: Grouping object for mapping match predicates such as path and source before action routing is applied. Keep match criteria specific so unrelated webhook traffic does not trigger automations.

action.title: Hook Mapping Action
action.description: Mapping action type: "wake" queues a notice for the owning session, while "agent" starts an independent agent turn. Session notices do not interrupt active work.

wakeMode.title: Hook Mapping Wake Mode
wakeMode.description: Wake scheduling mode: "now" queues a session turn immediately, while "next-heartbeat" assigns the notice to the next eligible scheduled automation for that session. Deferred wakes require an enabled automation that can receive the notice.

name.title: Hook Mapping Name
name.description: Human-readable mapping display name used in diagnostics and operator-facing config UIs. Keep names concise and descriptive so routing intent is obvious during incident review.

agentId.title: Hook Mapping Agent ID
agentId.description: Target agent ID for mapping execution when action routing should not use defaults. Use dedicated automation agents to isolate webhook behavior from interactive operator sessions.

sessionKey.title: Hook Mapping Session Key
sessionKey.description: Explicit session key override for mapping-delivered messages to control thread continuity. Use stable scoped keys so repeated events correlate without leaking into unrelated conversations.

sessionMode.title: Hook Mapping Session Mode
sessionMode.description: Controls mapping session continuity: "isolated" starts a fresh run session, while "persistent" reuses the resolved sessionKey. Keep isolated unless the integration intentionally needs durable context.

messageTemplate.title: Hook Mapping Message Template
messageTemplate.description: Template for synthesizing structured mapping input into the final message content sent to the target action path. Make the same inputs produce the same message so downstream parsing and behavior remain stable.

textTemplate.title: Hook Mapping Text Template
textTemplate.description: Text-only fallback template used when rich payload rendering is not desired or not supported. Use this to provide a concise, consistent summary string for chat delivery surfaces.

forEach.title: Hook Mapping Fan-Out Key
forEach.description: Top-level payload array key the mapping fans out over: each element dispatches its own action, and templates or transforms see a payload whose array holds only the current element. The Gmail preset uses forEach: messages so batched pushes dispatch one run per email.

deliver.title: Hook Mapping Deliver Reply
deliver.description: Controls whether mapping execution results are delivered back to a channel destination versus being processed silently. Disable delivery for background automations that should not post user-facing output.

allowUnsafeExternalContent.title: Hook Mapping Allow Unsafe External Content
allowUnsafeExternalContent.description: When true, mapping content may include less-sanitized external payload data in generated messages. Keep false by default and enable only for trusted sources with reviewed transform logic.

channel.title: Hook Mapping Delivery Channel
channel.description: Delivery channel override for mapping outputs (for example "last", "telegram", "discord", "slack", "signal", "imessage", or "msteams"). Keep channel overrides explicit to avoid accidental cross-channel sends.

to.title: Hook Mapping Delivery Destination
to.description: Destination identifier inside the selected channel when mapping replies should route to a fixed target. Verify provider-specific destination formats before enabling production mappings.

model.title: Hook Mapping Model Override
model.description: Optional model override for mapping-triggered runs when automation should use a different model than agent defaults. Use this sparingly so behavior remains predictable across mapping executions.

thinking.title: Hook Mapping Thinking Override
thinking.description: Optional thinking-effort override for mapping-triggered runs to tune latency versus reasoning depth. Keep low or minimal for high-volume hooks unless deeper reasoning is clearly required.

timeoutSeconds.title: Hook Mapping Timeout (sec)
timeoutSeconds.description: Maximum runtime allowed for mapping action execution before timeout handling applies. Use tighter limits for high-volume webhook sources to prevent queue pileups.

module.title: Hook Transform Module
module.description: Relative transform module path loaded from hooks.transformsDir to rewrite incoming payloads before delivery. Keep modules local, reviewed, and free of path traversal patterns.

export.title: Hook Transform Export
export.description: Named export to invoke from the transform module; defaults to module default export when omitted. Set this when one file hosts multiple transform handlers.

transform.title: Hook Mapping Transform
transform.description: Transform configuration block defining module/export preprocessing before mapping action handling. Use transforms only from reviewed code paths and keep behavior repeatable for repeatable automation.

mappings.title: Hook Mappings
mappings.description: Ordered mapping rules that match inbound hook requests and choose wake or agent actions with optional delivery routing. Use specific mappings first to avoid broad pattern rules capturing everything.

account.title: Gmail Hook Account
account.description: Google account identifier used for Gmail watch/subscription operations in this hook integration. Use a dedicated automation mailbox account to isolate operational permissions.

label.title: Gmail Hook Label
label.description: Optional Gmail label filter limiting which labeled messages trigger hook events. Keep filters narrow to avoid flooding automations with unrelated inbox traffic.

topic.title: Gmail Hook Pub/Sub Topic
topic.description: Google Pub/Sub topic name used by Gmail watch to publish change notifications for this account. Check that the topic IAM grants Gmail publish access before enabling watches.

subscription.title: Gmail Hook Subscription
subscription.description: Pub/Sub subscription consumed by the gateway to receive Gmail change notifications from the configured topic. Keep subscription ownership clear so multiple consumers do not race unexpectedly.

pushToken.title: Gmail Hook Push Token
pushToken.description: Shared secret token required on Gmail push hook callbacks before processing notifications. Use env substitution and rotate if callback endpoints are exposed externally.

hookUrl.title: Gmail Hook Callback URL
hookUrl.description: Public callback URL Gmail or intermediaries invoke to deliver notifications into this hook pipeline. Keep this URL protected with token validation and restricted network exposure.

includeBody.title: Gmail Hook Include Body
includeBody.description: When true, fetch and include email body content for downstream mapping/agent processing. Keep false unless body text is required, because this increases payload size and sensitivity.

maxBytes.title: Gmail Hook Max Body Bytes
maxBytes.description: Maximum Gmail payload bytes processed per event when includeBody is enabled. Keep conservative limits to reduce oversized message processing cost and risk.

renewEveryMinutes.title: Gmail Hook Renew Interval (min)
renewEveryMinutes.description: Renewal cadence in minutes for Gmail watch subscriptions to prevent expiration. Set below provider expiration windows and monitor renew failures in logs.

allowUnsafeExternalContent.title: Gmail Hook Allow Unsafe External Content
allowUnsafeExternalContent.description: Allows less-sanitized external Gmail content to pass into processing when enabled. Keep disabled for safer defaults, and enable only for trusted mail streams with controlled transforms.

bind.title: Gmail Hook Server Bind Address
bind.description: Bind address for the local Gmail callback HTTP server used when serving hooks directly. Keep loopback-only unless external ingress is intentionally required.

port.title: Gmail Hook Server Port
port.description: Port for the local Gmail callback HTTP server when serve mode is enabled. Use a dedicated port to avoid collisions with gateway/control interfaces.

path.title: Gmail Hook Server Path
path.description: HTTP path on the local Gmail callback server where push notifications are accepted. Keep this consistent with subscription configuration to avoid dropped events.

serve.title: Gmail Hook Local Server
serve.description: Local callback server settings block for directly receiving Gmail notifications without a separate ingress layer. Enable only when this process should terminate webhook traffic itself.

mode.title: Gmail Hook Tailscale Mode
mode.description: Tailscale exposure mode for Gmail callbacks: "off", "serve", or "funnel". Use "serve" for private tailnet delivery and "funnel" only when public internet ingress is required.

path.title: Gmail Hook Tailscale Path
path.description: Path published by Tailscale Serve/Funnel for Gmail callback forwarding when enabled. Keep it aligned with Gmail webhook config so requests reach the expected handler.

target.title: Gmail Hook Tailscale Target
target.description: Local service target forwarded by Tailscale Serve/Funnel (for example http://127.0.0.1:8787). Use explicit loopback targets to avoid ambiguous routing.

tailscale.title: Gmail Hook Tailscale
tailscale.description: Tailscale exposure configuration block for publishing Gmail callbacks through Serve/Funnel routes. Use private tailnet modes before enabling any public ingress path.

model.title: Gmail Hook Model Override
model.description: Optional model override for Gmail-triggered runs when mailbox automations should use dedicated model behavior. Keep unset to inherit agent defaults unless mailbox tasks need specialization.

thinking.title: Gmail Hook Thinking Override
thinking.description: Thinking effort override for Gmail-driven agent runs: "off", "minimal", "low", "medium", or "high". Keep modest defaults for routine inbox automations to control cost and latency.

gmail.title: Gmail Hook
gmail.description: Gmail push integration settings used for Pub/Sub notifications and optional local callback serving. Keep this scoped to dedicated Gmail automation accounts where possible.

enabled.title: Internal Hooks Enabled
enabled.description: Enables processing for internal hooks and configured entries in the internal hook runtime. Keep disabled unless internal hooks are intentionally configured.

entries.title: Internal Hook Entries
entries.description: Configured internal hook entry records used to register concrete runtime handlers and metadata. Keep entries explicit and versioned so production behavior is auditable.

extraDirs.title: Internal Hook Extra Directories
extraDirs.description: Additional directories searched for internal hook modules beyond default load paths. Keep this minimal and controlled to reduce accidental module shadowing.

load.title: Internal Hook Loader
load.description: Internal hook loader settings controlling where handler modules are discovered at startup. Use constrained load roots to reduce accidental module conflicts or shadowing.

internal.title: Internal Hooks
internal.description: Internal hook runtime settings for bundled/custom event handlers loaded from module paths. Use this for trusted in-process automations and keep handler loading tightly scoped.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.description: Inbound webhook automation surface for mapping external events into wake or agent actions in OpenClaw. Keep this locked down with explicit token/session/agent controls before exposing it beyond trusted networks.

groupPolicy.title: Default Group Policy
groupPolicy.description: Default group policy across channels: "open", "disabled", or "allowlist". Keep "allowlist" for safer production setups unless broad group participation is intentional.

contextVisibility.title: Default Context Visibility
contextVisibility.description: Default supplemental context visibility for fetched quote/thread/history content: "all" (keep all context), "allowlist" (only allowlisted senders), or "allowlist_quote" (allowlist + keep explicit quotes).

enabled.title: Default Bot Loop Protection Enabled
enabled.description: Enables pair loop protection by default for supporting channels when bot-authored messages can reach dispatch. Providers may still disable the guard when bots are ignored.

maxEventsPerWindow.title: Default Bot Loop Events per Window
maxEventsPerWindow.description: Maximum events a sender/receiver pair may exchange within the configured window before suppression starts. Default for supporting channels is 20.

windowSeconds.title: Default Bot Loop Window Seconds
windowSeconds.description: Sliding window length in seconds for pair loop budgets. Default for supporting channels is 60.

cooldownSeconds.title: Default Bot Loop Cooldown Seconds
cooldownSeconds.description: Cooldown seconds applied to a pair after it exceeds the loop budget. Default for supporting channels is 60.

botLoopProtection.title: Default Bot Loop Protection
botLoopProtection.description: Default pair loop protection settings for channel providers that support bot-to-bot loop guards. Use provider-specific overrides only when one channel needs a different budget.

replyToBot.title: Default Reply-to-Bot Implicit Mentions
replyToBot.description: Treat replies to the bot's own messages as implicit mentions by default. Defaults to true for backward compatibility.

quotedBot.title: Default Quoted-Bot Implicit Mentions
quotedBot.description: Treat quoted bot messages as implicit mentions by default. Defaults to true for backward compatibility.

threadParticipation.title: Default Thread-Participation Implicit Mentions
threadParticipation.description: Treat follow-ups in threads where the bot participated as implicit mentions by default. Defaults to true for backward compatibility.

implicitMentions.title: Default Implicit Mentions
implicitMentions.description: Default policy for whether reply-to-bot, quoted-bot, and bot-participated-thread facts activate supporting message channels without an explicit mention.

defaults.title: Channel Defaults
defaults.description: Default channel behavior applied across providers when provider-specific settings are not set. Use this to enforce consistent baseline policy before per-provider tuning.

modelByChannel.title: Channel Model Overrides
modelByChannel.description: Map provider -> channel id / DM peer id -> model override (values are provider/model or aliases).

requireMentionInBotThreads.description: Require mentions in threads started by this bot. False permits unmentioned messages; true requires a mention. Omit to preserve existing mention behavior.

dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.description: Dangerous opt-in for trusted Telegram fake-IP or transparent-proxy environments where api.telegram.org resolves to private/internal/special-use addresses during media downloads.

webhookUrl.description: Public HTTPS webhook URL registered with Telegram for inbound updates. This must be internet-reachable and requires channels.telegram.webhookSecret.

webhookSecret.description: Secret token sent to Telegram during webhook registration and verified on inbound webhook requests. Telegram returns this value for verification; this is not the gateway auth token and not the bot token.

webhookPath.description: Local webhook route path served by the gateway listener. Defaults to /telegram-webhook.

legacyWebhook.description: Explicit webhook forwarding endpoint. Doctor pins existing proxy endpoints once; remove the pin after moving the proxy to the Gateway, or set false to disable inherited forwarding.

webhookCertPath.description: Path to the self-signed certificate (PEM) to upload to Telegram during webhook registration. Required for self-signed certs (direct IP or no domain).

trustedLocalFileRoots.description: Trusted local filesystem roots for self-hosted Telegram Bot API absolute file_path values. Only absolute paths under these roots are read directly; all other absolute paths are rejected.

dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork.description: Dangerous opt-in for trusted Telegram fake-IP or transparent-proxy environments where api.telegram.org resolves to private/internal/special-use addresses during media downloads.

webhookUrl.description: Public HTTPS webhook URL registered with Telegram for inbound updates. This must be internet-reachable and requires channels.telegram.webhookSecret.

webhookSecret.description: Secret token sent to Telegram during webhook registration and verified on inbound webhook requests. Telegram returns this value for verification; this is not the gateway auth token and not the bot token.

webhookPath.description: Local webhook route path served by the gateway listener. Defaults to /telegram-webhook.

legacyWebhook.description: Explicit webhook forwarding endpoint. Doctor pins existing proxy endpoints once; remove the pin after moving the proxy to the Gateway, or set false to disable inherited forwarding.

webhookCertPath.description: Path to the self-signed certificate (PEM) to upload to Telegram during webhook registration. Required for self-signed certs (direct IP or no domain).

trustedLocalFileRoots.description: Trusted local filesystem roots for self-hosted Telegram Bot API absolute file_path values. Only absolute paths under these roots are read directly; all other absolute paths are rejected.

channels.title: Channels
channels.description: Channel provider configurations plus shared defaults that control access policies and per-surface behavior. Keep defaults centralized and override per provider only where required.

domain.title: Wide-area Discovery Domain
domain.description: Optional unicast DNS-SD domain for wide-area discovery, such as openclaw.internal. Use this when you intentionally publish gateway discovery beyond local mDNS scopes.

wideArea.title: Wide-area Discovery
wideArea.description: Wide-area discovery configuration group for exposing discovery signals beyond local-link scopes. Enable only in deployments that intentionally aggregate gateway presence across sites.

mode.title: mDNS Discovery Mode
mode.description: mDNS broadcast mode ("minimal" default, "full" includes cliPath/sshPort, "off" disables mDNS).

mdns.title: mDNS Discovery
mdns.description: mDNS discovery configuration group for local network advertisement and discovery behavior tuning. Keep minimal mode for routine LAN discovery unless extra metadata is required.

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.description: Service discovery settings for local mDNS advertisement and optional wide-area presence signaling. Keep discovery scoped to expected networks to avoid leaking service metadata.

agentId.title: Talk Agent
agentId.description: Agent that owns Talk sessions created without an explicit agent-scoped session key.

apiKey.title: Talk Provider API Key
apiKey.description: Provider API key for Talk mode.

additionalProperties.title: Talk Provider Config
additionalProperties.description: Provider-owned Talk config fields for the matching provider id.

providers.title: Talk Provider Settings
providers.description: Provider-specific Talk settings keyed by provider id. During migration, prefer this over legacy talk.* keys.

provider.title: Talk Realtime Provider
provider.description: Active realtime voice provider id, such as openai or google.

apiKey.title: Talk Realtime Provider API Key
apiKey.description: Provider API key for realtime Talk.

inputTranscriptionModel.description: Input transcription model or deployment name. Omit to keep the provider default.

additionalProperties.title: Talk Realtime Provider Config
additionalProperties.description: Provider-owned realtime voice config for the matching provider id.

providers.title: Talk Realtime Provider Settings
providers.description: Provider-specific realtime voice settings keyed by provider id.

model.title: Talk Realtime Model
model.description: Realtime provider model id override for browser or Gateway-owned Talk sessions.

speakerVoice.title: Talk Realtime Speaker Voice
speakerVoice.description: Realtime provider speaker voice name override for browser or Gateway-owned Talk sessions.

speakerVoiceId.title: Talk Realtime Speaker Voice ID
speakerVoiceId.description: Realtime provider speaker voice id override for browser or Gateway-owned Talk sessions.

instructions.title: Talk Realtime Instructions
instructions.description: Additional system instructions appended to OpenClaw's built-in realtime Talk prompt. Use this for voice style, tone, and other provider-facing realtime behavior while keeping agent-consult guidance intact.

mode.title: Talk Realtime Mode
mode.description: Talk execution mode: realtime, stt-tts, or transcription.

transport.title: Talk Realtime Transport
transport.description: Talk byte/session transport: webrtc, provider-websocket, gateway-relay, or managed-room.

vadThreshold.title: Talk Realtime VAD Threshold
vadThreshold.description: Realtime voice activity detection threshold from 0 (most sensitive) to 1 (least sensitive).

silenceDurationMs.title: Talk Realtime Silence Duration (ms)
silenceDurationMs.description: Milliseconds of silence before a realtime Talk user turn is committed.

prefixPaddingMs.title: Talk Realtime Prefix Padding (ms)
prefixPaddingMs.description: Milliseconds of audio retained before realtime voice activity is detected.

reasoningEffort.title: Talk Realtime Reasoning Effort
reasoningEffort.description: Provider-specific reasoning effort for realtime Talk sessions, such as minimal, low, medium, or high.

brain.title: Talk Realtime Brain
brain.description: Talk reasoning strategy: agent-consult for Gateway-mediated agent help, direct-tools for local tool calls, or none.

consultRouting.title: Talk Realtime Consult Routing
consultRouting.description: Gateway relay fallback for final user transcripts when the realtime provider skips openclaw_agent_consult. provider-direct preserves provider replies; force-agent-consult routes through OpenClaw.

realtime.title: Talk Realtime
realtime.description: Realtime Talk provider, model, voice, mode, transport, and brain strategy. Keep speech/TTS provider config in talk.provider and talk.providers.

consultThinkingLevel.title: Talk Consult Thinking Level
consultThinkingLevel.description: Use this to override the thinking level for the regular agent run behind Talk realtime consults.

consultFastMode.title: Talk Consult Fast Mode
consultFastMode.description: Use this to set true or false fast mode for the regular agent run behind Talk realtime consults.

speechLocale.title: Talk Speech Locale
speechLocale.description: BCP 47 locale id for Talk speech recognition on device nodes and the iOS system-voice fallback, for example "ru-RU". Leave unset to use each device default.

interruptOnSpeech.title: Talk Interrupt on Speech
interruptOnSpeech.description: If true (default), stop assistant speech when the user starts speaking in Talk mode. Keep enabled for conversational turn-taking.

silenceTimeoutMs.title: Talk Silence Timeout (ms)
silenceTimeoutMs.description: Milliseconds of user silence before Talk mode finalizes and sends the current transcript. Leave unset to keep the platform default pause window (700 ms on macOS and Android, 900 ms on iOS).

talk.title: Talk
talk.description: Talk-mode voice synthesis settings for voice identity, model selection, output format, and interruption behavior. Use this section to tune human-facing voice UX while controlling latency and cost.

port.title: Gateway Port
port.description: TCP port used by the gateway listener for API, web app, and channel-facing ingress paths. Use a dedicated port and avoid collisions with reverse proxies or local developer services.

mode.title: Gateway Mode
mode.description: Gateway operation mode: "local" runs channels and agent runtime on this host, while "remote" connects through remote transport. Keep "local" unless you intentionally run a split remote gateway topology.

bind.title: Gateway Bind Mode
bind.description: Network bind profile: "auto", "lan", "loopback", "custom", or "tailnet" to control interface exposure. Keep "loopback" for local-only operation; "auto" can expose all interfaces.

customBindHost.title: Gateway Custom Bind Host
customBindHost.description: IPv4 address used for a custom bind. Specific IPv4s also require the same Gateway port on 127.0.0.1; avoid 0.0.0.0 unless all-interface exposure is required.

publicOrigin.title: Gateway Public Origin
publicOrigin.description: Externally reachable HTTPS origin of the Gateway. Also the default browser origin when gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins is omitted. HTTP is allowed only for localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1]. Per-requester MCP OAuth uses it to build the callback URL at /oauth/mcp/callback; channel session links and plugin-generated viewer links use it to reach the web app and Gateway routes.

domain.title: Portal Wildcard Domain
domain.description: Bare DNS domain for random portal subdomains (for example previews.example.net). Configure wildcard DNS and HTTPS privately; do not share the Gateway or web app hostname namespace.

port.title: Portal Ingress Loopback Port
port.description: Dedicated loopback HTTP port receiving the private wildcard HTTPS proxy. Must differ from the Gateway port. This is the backend port, not the public HTTPS port.

ingress.title: Private Portal Ingress
ingress.description: Optional operator-managed private HTTPS wildcard reverse proxy. Forward original Host, paths, and WebSocket upgrades to the dedicated loopback listener. Portal bearer authentication remains required. Requires Gateway restart.

portals.title: Gateway Portals
portals.description: Portal publication and private ingress settings.

enabled.title: OpenClaw ID Remote Access Enabled
enabled.description: Turns on experimental OpenClaw ID remote access (default: false). Changes apply without restarting the Gateway. Remote access also needs relayUrl; linking a claw additionally needs issuerUrl, discoveryUrl and loaderDomain.

issuerUrl.title: OpenClaw ID Issuer URL
issuerUrl.description: OpenClaw ID issuer used to sign in for identity only while linking a claw. It is never trusted for membership, device approval or which server a client dials.

clientId.title: OpenClaw ID Web App Client ID
clientId.description: Public OAuth client (authorization code with PKCE) the web app uses for Sign in with OpenClaw ID in its account menu. Its redirect URI is <web app origin>/openclaw-id/callback. On this machine sign-in uses that redirect; a web app reached through a personal sign-in such as Tailscale uses the issuer's device grant.

discoveryUrl.title: OpenClaw ID Discovery URL
discoveryUrl.description: Discovery service that mirrors the claw descriptor and membership snapshot and relays mailbox messages. It is untrusted: every statement it returns is verified against the claw's pinned owner root.

relayUrl.title: OpenClaw ID Relay URL
relayUrl.description: The only iroh relay in the tunnel endpoint's relay map (no public n0 relays, DNS or pkarr). Browsers reach the claw only through this relay.

loaderDomain.title: OpenClaw ID Loader Domain
loaderDomain.description: Bare DNS domain of the OpenClaw ID loader; a linked claw is reachable at https://<name>-<account tag>.<loaderDomain> and its server binding is signed for that hostname.

ownerDeviceInactivityDays.title: OpenClaw ID Owner Device Inactivity (Days)
ownerDeviceInactivityDays.description: Days an owner device may go without reaching this claw before the claw removes it from its allowlist (default: 90). Devices it approved stay.

memberDeviceInactivityDays.title: OpenClaw ID Member Device Inactivity (Days)
memberDeviceInactivityDays.description: Days a member's browser may go without reaching this claw before the claw removes it (default: 30). The member stays listed.

openclawId.title: OpenClaw ID Remote Access
openclawId.description: Experimental OpenClaw ID remote access (Labs). When enabled, the Gateway supervises a tunnel child that accepts iroh connections from admitted devices and proxies them to this Gateway. Off by default; while off the Gateway starts no child process, opens no tunnel sockets, and contacts no OpenClaw ID, Discovery or relay service.

repositoryIntegration.title: Repository Integration
repositoryIntegration.description: Plugin ID required to admit worker repository source access, including native, GitHub App, and managed OAuth or PAT credentials. Missing, disabled or unloaded owners deny admission. Omit to use native repository behavior; enabling a plugin alone does not select it.

enabled.title: Web App Enabled
enabled.description: Enables serving the web app from the gateway HTTP process when true. Keep enabled for local administration, and disable when an external control surface replaces it.

basePath.title: Web App Base Path
basePath.description: Optional URL prefix where the web app is served (e.g. /openclaw).

customPlugins.title: Custom Plugin UI
customPlugins.description: Allow enabled user-installed plugins to execute native JavaScript in the web app (default: true). Retained as an advanced config-only opt-out; existing false values remain off. Bundled plugin views are unaffected. Native UI shares the signed-in operator's Gateway permissions; install only trusted plugins. Changes apply without a Gateway restart. After disabling, reload open web app pages to clear previously loaded plugin code.

templates.title: Templates
templates.description: Enable ClawHub discovery and one-way Add through the web app and Gateway (default: false). Existing agents keep running while this is off.

chatBubbles.title: Speech Bubbles
chatBubbles.description: Enable experimental speech bubbles in the web app (default: false). Home defaults to bubbles while enabled; browser-local per-session choices take precedence. Changes apply without a Gateway restart.

experimental.title: Experimental Web App Features
experimental.description: Web app experiments and retained advanced overrides. Experiments are disabled by default unless their setting documents otherwise.

root.title: Web App Assets Root
root.description: Optional filesystem root for web app assets (defaults to dist/control-ui).

label.title: Web App Environment Label
label.description: Environment label displayed in the web app and browser tab; surrounding whitespace is trimmed and the label must contain 1 to 24 characters.

color.title: Web App Environment Color
color.description: Named environment color ramp: teal, amber, purple, coral, pink, blue, green, red, or gray.

environment.title: Web App Environment
environment.description: Optional public environment identity shown in the web app stripe, agent avatar, label pills, browser title, and favicon. Omit it to preserve the default appearance.

communityInvite.title: Web App Community Invitation
communityInvite.description: Show a dismissible Community card in the web app sidebar (default on), with Discord, Reddit, and X links. Set false to hide it for every browser using this UI deployment. Changes apply after browser refresh or reconnect. Existing browser-local dismissals remain honored.

newSessionModelDefaults.title: New Session Model Defaults
newSessionModelDefaults.description: Choose "configured" to start fresh web app drafts with the selected agent’s configured model, runtime and reasoning defaults instead of remembered selections. Default: "last-used". Explicit draft and conversation choices remain editable; Fast Mode and placement preferences are unchanged. Applies after browser refresh or reconnect.

host.title: Web App GitHub Service Host
host.description: Host this service credential may access. Omit for github.com; set to gateway.github.host for Enterprise project discovery and account metadata.

token.title: Web App GitHub Service Credential
token.description: SecretRef-backed service credential for web app project discovery and GitHub hover previews without a managed identity. Set gateway.controlUi.github.host for Enterprise; an omitted host means github.com. Hover previews prefer the selected agent's configured GitHub identity. GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN fallback applies only to github.com. Requests using a mismatched or unavailable credential are rejected.

sessionObserver.title: Web App Session Observer
sessionObserver.description: Produce live session status digests for subscribed web app clients with each agent's utility model (default on). Set false to disable observer model calls gateway-wide; setting agents.defaults.utilityModel to an empty string disables utility-model observation for agents that do not override it.

embedSandbox.title: Web App Embed Sandbox Mode
embedSandbox.description: Iframe sandbox policy for hosted web app embeds. "strict" disables scripts, "scripts" allows interactive embeds while keeping origin isolation (default), and "trusted" adds `allow-same-origin` for same-site documents that intentionally need stronger privileges.

allowExternalEmbedUrls.title: Allow External Web App Embed URLs
allowExternalEmbedUrls.description: DANGEROUS toggle that allows hosted embeds to load absolute external http(s) URLs. Keep this off unless your web app intentionally embeds trusted third-party pages; hosted /__openclaw__/canvas documents do not need it.

automaticallyFetchFavicons.title: Automatically Fetch Link Favicons
automaticallyFetchFavicons.description: Fetch link favicons and external-link page previews through the Gateway (default on). Page previews load public page metadata and declared images without browser cookies or site credentials. All requests use strict SSRF checks and bounded HTML/image processing. Set false to disable both automatic favicon and page-preview fetches; live browser screenshots are unaffected.

allowedOrigins.title: Web App Allowed Origins
allowedOrigins.description: Allowed browser origins for web app/WebChat connections (full origins only, e.g. https://control.example.com). When omitted, defaults to gateway.publicOrigin if configured. An explicit list, including [], overrides that default; existing local/private-origin rules still apply. Setting ["*"] means allow any browser origin and should be avoided outside tightly controlled local testing.

dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback.title: Dangerously Allow Host-Header Origin Fallback
dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback.description: DANGEROUS toggle that enables Host-header based origin fallback for web app/WebChat websocket checks. This mode is supported when your deployment intentionally relies on Host-header origin policy; explicit gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins remains the recommended hardened default.

controlUi.title: Web app
controlUi.description: Web app hosting settings including enablement, pathing, and browser-origin/auth hardening behavior. Keep UI exposure minimal and pair with strong auth controls before internet-facing deployments.

enabled.title: Uploads Enabled
enabled.description: Allows client file and image uploads (default: true). Set false to reject attachments, workspace/terminal uploads, avatar uploads, and archive imports at the Gateway, including direct API requests. Changes apply without restarting. This is not a sandbox or a restriction on channel media, agent tools, or operator shell access.

uploads.title: File and Image Uploads
uploads.description: Client file and image upload policy for the Gateway and web app. Downloads and agent-generated media remain available.

enabled.title: CLI Agents Enabled
enabled.description: Shows catalog-backed CLI agents in the web app new-session model picker when true (default: true). Set false to disable CLI agents and native CLI session creation. Only catalogs that advertise session creation are listed, and the picker stays hidden when the Gateway does not advertise session catalog support.

cliAgents.title: CLI Agents
cliAgents.description: Web app discovery for external CLI session engines exposed by the Gateway session catalog. Enabled by default; disable to prevent starting those engines from the new-session model picker.

enabled.title: Operator Terminal Enabled
enabled.description: Enables the operator terminal for admin-scope clients (default: true). This exposes a browser/mobile shell with the gateway process environment; set false to opt out on deployments where admin operators should not get a host shell. Changes apply without restarting the Gateway.

shell.title: Operator Terminal Shell
shell.description: Shell executable the operator terminal launches. Leave unset to use the host login shell ($SHELL on Unix, %ComSpec% on Windows), or pin an explicit interpreter for a consistent operator environment.

detachedSessionTimeoutSeconds.title: Operator Terminal Detached Session Timeout
detachedSessionTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a terminal session survives after its connection drops (laptop sleep, page reload), staying reattachable via terminal.attach with its recent output replayed. Set 0 to kill sessions the moment the connection drops. Default: 300 (5 minutes). Detached sessions keep running their commands, so shorten this on shared or exposed hosts.

terminal.title: Operator Terminal
terminal.description: Operator terminal served to web app and mobile clients: a PTY-backed shell on the gateway host, restricted to admin-scope operator sessions. It starts in the target agent's workspace and is refused for fully-sandboxed agents (sandbox.mode 'all') rather than handing back an unconfined host shell.

mode.title: Gateway Auth Mode
mode.description: Gateway auth mode: "none", "token", "password", or "trusted-proxy" depending on your edge architecture. Token/password mode selects the configured secret (gateway.auth.token or gateway.auth.password); clients may send it in either connect auth field. Use token/password for direct exposure, and trusted-proxy only behind hardened identity-aware proxies.

token.title: Gateway Token
token.description: Shared secret selected by gateway.auth.mode=token, the default for new local onboarding. Clients may send it in either auth.token or auth.password. Non-loopback binds require an enabled authentication mode.

password.title: Gateway Password
password.description: Shared secret selected by gateway.auth.mode=password. Clients may send it in either auth.token or auth.password. Password mode is required for Tailscale Funnel.

allowTailscale.title: Gateway Auth Allow Tailscale Identity
allowTailscale.description: Allows trusted Tailscale identity paths to satisfy gateway auth checks when configured. Use this only when your tailnet identity posture is strong and operator workflows depend on it.

identityScopes.title: Gateway Identity Scope Grants
identityScopes.description: Maps verified trusted-proxy or Tailscale identities to connection-only operator scope grants. Email keys match case-insensitively; grants augment device scopes before the connection scope cap is applied.

rateLimit.title: Gateway Auth Rate Limit
rateLimit.description: Login/auth attempt throttling controls to reduce credential brute-force risk at the gateway boundary. Keep enabled in exposed environments and tune thresholds to your traffic baseline.

credentialFile.title: Delegation Credential File
credentialFile.description: Absolute path to a private file containing the revision's 32-byte credential as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. File replacement or removal invalidates existing grants.

delegation.title: Enterprise Browser Delegation
delegation.description: Accept revision-scoped OCE browser identity and scope grants through the private trusted proxy. Delegated profiles do not use email aliases or device grants.

nameHeader.description: Header containing the organization's co-author name for the authenticated principal.

emailHeader.description: Header containing the organization's commit credit email for the authenticated principal.

emailVerifiedHeader.description: Optional header that must equal true before organization defaults are imported. Omit only when the proxy's email assertion is sufficient for your policy.

gitCoauthor.description: Optional organization co-author defaults from authenticated proxy headers. The proxy must overwrite these fields. They do not verify GitHub identity or grant permissions; supplied email addresses require saved consent before appearing in commit history.

issuer.title: Cloudflare Access Issuer
issuer.description: Exact HTTPS origin of the trusted Cloudflare Access team, such as https://example.cloudflareaccess.com, without a trailing slash. Claims from other issuers do not supply GitHub identity.

providerId.title: Cloudflare Access OIDC Provider ID
providerId.description: Exact Access identity-provider ID for the trusted OIDC integration. A provider display name or a matching claim name alone does not establish trust.

githubAccountIdClaim.title: GitHub Account ID Claim
githubAccountIdClaim.description: Exact forwarded OIDC claim whose value is a verified positive decimal-string GitHub account ID. Configure Access to forward it, then inspect the authenticated Access identity response. OpenClaw reads oidc_fields, or custom when oidc_fields is absent. Never use an unverified user-editable claim.

cloudflareAccessOidc.title: Cloudflare Access OIDC GitHub Identity
cloudflareAccessOidc.description: Optional verified GitHub identity from a selected Cloudflare Access OIDC provider. Requires the standard Access email and assertion headers. Missing claims keep email-only profiles; existing profile roles and co-author preferences are preserved.

enabled.title: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval Enabled
enabled.description: Automatically approves new browser and native UI operator devices and same-key scope upgrades after the reverse proxy authenticates an allowed user. Default: false. Enable only when the proxy identity boundary is strong enough to replace manual device pairing.

scopes.title: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval Scopes
scopes.description: Maximum scopes granted to auto-approved operator devices. Defaults to operator.read, operator.write, operator.approvals, and operator.questions. Requested scopes are capped to this list; requests without scopes receive this list. When unset, auto-approval also adds operator.questions for older UI clients; an explicit list is never widened. Explicitly listing operator.admin lets every proxy-authenticated user auto-approve full admin and makes scope-less requests receive full admin automatically; it also triggers a critical security audit finding and Gateway startup warning.

deviceAutoApprove.title: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval
deviceAutoApprove.description: Optional policy for automatically approving new browser and native UI operator devices and same-key scope upgrades after trusted-proxy authentication. Grants are capped by deviceAutoApprove.scopes and the proxy's x-openclaw-scopes header when present.

trustedProxy.title: Gateway Trusted Proxy Auth
trustedProxy.description: Trusted-proxy auth header mapping for upstream identity providers that inject user claims. Use only with known proxy CIDRs and strict header allowlists to prevent spoofed identity headers.

auth.title: Gateway Auth
auth.description: Authentication policy for gateway HTTP/WebSocket access including mode, credentials, trusted-proxy behavior, and rate limiting. Keep auth enabled for every non-loopback deployment.

default.title: Default Operator Role (Enables Enforcement)
default.description: Optional default that enables named-role enforcement and applies to authenticated profiles without a valid explicit or GitHub login assignment. Its name must match a configured definition. Omitting it leaves named-role enforcement off, even when definitions exist.

additionalProperties.title: GitHub Login Operator Role
additionalProperties.description: Configured role name for this GitHub login. Applies when the profile has a matching cached GitHub identity and no valid explicit role assignment. Changes hot-apply when config reload is enabled.

byGithubLogin.title: Operator Roles by GitHub Login
byGithubLogin.description: Requires gateway.roles.default, even for an empty mapping. Maps cached GitHub identity logins to configured role names, matching case-insensitively after trimming. Invalid logins, duplicate normalized logins, and unknown roles are rejected. Profiles without a cached GitHub identity use their explicit assignment or default role.

assignments.title: Operator Role Assignments
assignments.description: Optional declarative role assignments for authenticated profiles. A valid explicit assignment made with users.setRole takes precedence over these mappings, followed by the default role.

others.title: Operator Role Access to Other Sessions
others.description: Access to other people's sessions: "none" hides them even with explicit session membership, "invited" requires explicit membership, "view" allows reading, "suggest" permits the suggestion flow, and "write" permits participation without membership. Explicit session membership can raise "view" or "suggest" access for a specific session. Session creators and connections holding operator.admin retain their session access. A creator or admin can invite an explicitly configured "invited" profile with a selected human @mention; connection scopes and draft/incognito restrictions still apply.

sessions.title: Operator Role Session Access
sessions.description: Session-sharing permissions granted to this role for sessions created by other authenticated people; a person's own sessions remain owner-accessible.

sandbox.title: Operator Role Sandbox Isolation
sandbox.description: Execution isolation for newly created sessions: "inherit" (default) uses the agent policy; "required" permanently requires a sandbox, even when the agent sandbox mode is off, and blocks execution if the backend is unavailable.

agents.title: Operator Role Allowed Agents
agents.description: Agents available when this role creates sessions or starts runs: set "*" to allow every agent, list agent IDs to allow only those agents, or use an empty list to disable both.

workerProfiles.title: Operator Role Worker Profiles
workerProfiles.description: Cloud worker profiles this role may explicitly dispatch its own sessions to. Omitted or empty denies cloud dispatch; administrators retain access. Setup and moves to cloud profiles remain administrator-only.

sourceAgent.title: Operator Role Model Source Agent
sourceAgent.description: Agent whose primary, fallbacks, and model aliases supply this role's model policy. Defaults to the configured system/default agent or the sole agent. Set this explicitly when a multi-agent Gateway has no ambient owner.

allow.title: Operator Role Allowed Models
allow.description: Optional replacement allowlist of model references, configured aliases, or trailing prefix wildcards such as "provider/*" or "provider/family-*". Omitted uses the source agent primary and fallbacks; an empty list denies all models. The first permitted source model remains Default, followed by explicit allowed models.

deny.title: Operator Role Excluded Models
deny.description: Model references, source-agent aliases, or trailing prefix wildcards excluded from this role. A pattern such as "provider/family-*" excludes future members of that family too. Exclusions match resolved model identities and take precedence over allowed and source-agent models.

modelPolicy.title: Operator Role Model Policy
modelPolicy.description: Optional model ceiling for this role's requests and descendants. An empty object allows only the source agent's configured primary and fallback models; omitting the policy leaves model access unchanged. Model aliases resolve before enforcement, and denied models cannot be used by retries or fallbacks. With config reload enabled, changes confined to existing roles' model policies apply when committed without restarting permitted work. Other role changes hot-apply and reconnect clients with current authority.

scopes.title: Operator Role Scope Ceiling
scopes.description: Closed list of operator scopes granted as this role's maximum connection authority. Requested, paired, identity-granted, and upgraded scopes are intersected with this list.

accessPolicyPlugin.title: Operator Role Access Policy Plugin
accessPolicyPlugin.description: Optional exact plugin ID whose Gateway access policy must authorize this role. Access is denied when the plugin is missing, disabled, fails to load, or supplies no current authority. Unavailable plugin IDs remain valid configuration so independent staff roles and the Gateway owner can repair access. Omitting this field adds no plugin dependency.

additionalProperties.title: Operator Role Definition
additionalProperties.description: One named operator role. Every definition must explicitly provide its session-sharing policy, allowed session and run agents, and operator-scope ceiling, and can require sandbox isolation for newly created sessions and a plugin access policy.

definitions.title: Operator Role Definitions
definitions.description: Nonempty administrator-named role catalog bundling session-sharing, sandbox-isolation, agent-access, and operator-scope policies. Definitions alone do not enable enforcement; set gateway.roles.default to apply named roles to authenticated profiles.

roles.title: Gateway Operator Roles
roles.description: Named operator-role definitions for team Gateways. Setting gateway.roles.default enables profile-bound enforcement of session access, sandbox isolation, agents, and operator scopes. Definitions without a default are a catalog only and preserve the behavior of a Gateway without gateway.roles.

trustedProxies.title: Gateway Trusted Proxy CIDRs
trustedProxies.description: CIDR/IP allowlist of upstream proxies permitted to provide forwarded client identity headers. Keep this list narrow so untrusted hops cannot impersonate users.

allowRealIpFallback.title: Gateway Allow x-real-ip Fallback
allowRealIpFallback.description: Enables x-real-ip fallback when x-forwarded-for is missing in proxy scenarios. Keep disabled unless your ingress stack requires this compatibility behavior.

deny.title: Gateway Tool Denylist
deny.description: Explicit gateway-level tool denylist to block risky tools even if lower-level policies allow them. Use deny rules for emergency response and defense-in-depth hardening.

allow.title: Gateway Tool Allowlist
allow.description: Explicit gateway-level tool allowlist when you want a narrow set of tools available at runtime. Use this for locked-down environments where tool scope must be tightly controlled.

tools.title: Gateway Tool Exposure Policy
tools.description: Gateway-level tool exposure allow/deny policy that can restrict runtime tool availability independent of agent/tool profiles. Use this for coarse emergency controls and production hardening.

mode.title: Gateway Tailscale Mode
mode.description: Tailscale publish mode: "off", "serve", or "funnel" for private or public exposure paths. Use "serve" for tailnet-only access and "funnel" only when public internet reachability is required.

preserveFunnel.title: Gateway Tailscale External Funnel Migration Guard
preserveFunnel.description: Deprecated migration guard for mode='serve'. If an external Funnel still targets the ordinary Gateway listener, OpenClaw leaves exposure unchanged and warns that only plugin-authenticated webhooks remain usable until password auth is configured and mode is migrated to 'funnel'.

tailscale.title: Gateway Tailscale
tailscale.description: Tailscale integration settings for Serve/Funnel exposure and lifecycle handling on gateway start/exit. Keep off unless your deployment intentionally relies on Tailscale ingress.

url.title: Remote Gateway URL
url.description: Remote Gateway WebSocket URL (ws:// or wss://).

transport.title: Remote Gateway Transport
transport.description: Remote connection transport: "direct" uses configured URL connectivity, while "ssh" tunnels through SSH. Use SSH when you need encrypted tunnel semantics without exposing remote ports.

token.title: Remote Gateway Token
token.description: Shared secret sent in the token field to authenticate this client to a remote gateway. The server's gateway.auth.mode selects its configured secret; either client token or password field is accepted. Store via secret/env substitution and rotate alongside remote gateway auth changes.

password.title: Remote Gateway Password
password.description: Shared secret sent in the password field to authenticate this client to a remote gateway. The server's gateway.auth.mode selects its configured secret; either client token or password field is accepted. Keep this secret managed externally and avoid plaintext values in committed config.

edgeAuth.title: Remote Gateway Edge Auth Headers
edgeAuth.description: Secret-backed HTTP headers presented to an identity-aware proxy in front of the configured remote Gateway. Headers are sent only to the exact gateway.remote.url origin over WSS and never follow redirects.

tlsFingerprint.title: Remote Gateway TLS Fingerprint
tlsFingerprint.description: Expected sha256 TLS fingerprint for the remote gateway (pin to avoid MITM).

sshTarget.title: Remote Gateway SSH Target
sshTarget.description: Remote gateway over SSH (tunnels the gateway port to localhost). Format: user@host or user@host:port.

sshIdentity.title: Remote Gateway SSH Identity
sshIdentity.description: Optional SSH identity file path (passed to ssh -i).

sshHostKeyPolicy.title: Remote Gateway SSH Host-Key Policy
sshHostKeyPolicy.description: macOS SSH host-key verification policy. "strict" requires an already trusted host key; "openssh" explicitly delegates to effective OpenSSH configuration.

remote.title: Remote Gateway
remote.description: Remote gateway connection settings for direct or SSH transport when this instance proxies to another runtime host. Use remote mode only when split-host operation is intentionally configured.

mode.title: Config Reload Mode
mode.description: Controls how config edits are applied: "off" ignores live edits and "hybrid" applies hot-safe changes then restarts when required.

reload.title: Config Reload
reload.description: Live config-reload policy for how edits are applied and when full restarts are triggered. Keep hybrid behavior for safest operational updates unless debugging reload internals.

enabled.title: Gateway TLS Enabled
enabled.description: Enables TLS termination at the gateway listener so clients connect over HTTPS/WSS directly. Keep enabled for direct internet exposure or any untrusted network boundary.

autoGenerate.title: Gateway TLS Auto-Generate Cert
autoGenerate.description: Auto-generates a local TLS certificate/key pair when explicit files are not configured. Use only for local/dev setups and replace with real certificates for production traffic.

certPath.title: Gateway TLS Certificate Path
certPath.description: Filesystem path to the TLS certificate file used by the gateway when TLS is enabled. Use managed certificate paths and keep renewal automation aligned with this location.

keyPath.title: Gateway TLS Key Path
keyPath.description: Filesystem path to the TLS private key file used by the gateway when TLS is enabled. Keep this key file permission-restricted and rotate per your security policy.

caPath.title: Gateway TLS CA Path
caPath.description: Optional CA bundle path for client verification or custom trust-chain requirements at the gateway edge. Use this when private PKI or custom certificate chains are part of deployment.

tls.title: Gateway TLS
tls.description: TLS certificate and key settings for terminating HTTPS directly in the gateway process. Use explicit certificates in production and avoid plaintext exposure on untrusted networks.

enabled.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Endpoint
enabled.description: Enable the OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/chat/completions` endpoint (default: false).

allowUrl.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Allow Image URLs
allowUrl.description: Allow server-side URL fetches for `image_url` parts (default: false; data URIs remain supported). Set this to `false` to disable URL fetching entirely.

urlAllowlist.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Image URL Allowlist
urlAllowlist.description: Optional hostname allowlist for `image_url` URL fetches; supports exact hosts and `*.example.com` wildcards. Empty or omitted lists mean no hostname allowlist restriction.

allowedMimes.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Image MIME Allowlist
allowedMimes.description: Allowed MIME types for `image_url` parts (case-insensitive list).

maxBytes.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Image Max Bytes

maxRedirects.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Image Max Redirects
maxRedirects.description: Max HTTP redirects allowed when fetching `image_url` URLs (default: 3).

timeoutMs.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Image Timeout (ms)
timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds for `image_url` URL fetches (default: 10000).

images.title: OpenAI Chat Completions Image Limits
images.description: Image fetch/validation controls for OpenAI-compatible `image_url` parts.

endpoints.title: Gateway HTTP Endpoints
