browser.noSandbox.help: Disables Chromium sandbox isolation flags for environments where sandboxing fails at runtime. Keep this off whenever possible because process isolation protections are reduced.

browser.attachOnly.label: Browser Attach-only Mode
browser.attachOnly.help: Restricts browser mode to attach-only behavior without starting local browser processes. Use this when all browser sessions are externally managed by a remote CDP provider.

browser.defaultProfile.label: Browser Default Profile
browser.defaultProfile.help: Default browser profile name selected when callers do not explicitly choose a profile. Use a stable low-privilege profile as the default to reduce accidental cross-context state use.

browser.profiles.label: Browser Profiles
browser.profiles.help: Named browser profile connection map used for explicit routing to CDP ports or URLs with optional metadata. Keep profile names consistent and avoid overlapping endpoint definitions.

browser.profiles.*.engine.label: Browser Profile Engine
browser.profiles.*.engine.help: Browser engine capability preset: "chromium" (default) or experimental "lightpanda" / "kitesurf" for external CDP browsing. External engines require an explicit ws/wss cdpUrl dedicated to one profile and attachOnly: true, never launches a local browser, and expose only their supported operations. Lightpanda has no screenshots; Kitesurf renders experimental screenshots.

browser.profiles.*.cdpPort.label: Browser Profile CDP Port
browser.profiles.*.cdpPort.help: Per-profile local CDP port used when connecting to browser instances by port instead of URL. Use unique ports per profile to avoid connection collisions.

browser.profiles.*.cdpUrl.label: Browser Profile CDP URL
browser.profiles.*.cdpUrl.help: Per-profile CDP/DevTools endpoint URL used for explicit browser routing by profile name. Use this for remote CDP hosts, tunnels, or existing-session profiles that should attach through a running Chrome DevTools endpoint.

browser.profiles.*.userDataDir.label: Browser Profile User Data Dir
browser.profiles.*.userDataDir.help: Per-profile Chromium user data directory for existing-session attachment through Chrome DevTools MCP. Use this for Brave, Edge, Chromium, or non-default Chrome profiles when the built-in auto-connect path would pick the wrong browser data directory on the selected host or browser node. Paths starting with ~ expand to the OS home directory.

browser.profiles.*.mcpCommand.label: Browser Profile Chrome MCP Command
browser.profiles.*.mcpCommand.help: Per-profile Chrome DevTools MCP command for existing-session attachment. Defaults to npx.

browser.profiles.*.mcpArgs.label: Browser Profile Chrome MCP Args
browser.profiles.*.mcpArgs.help: Extra per-profile Chrome DevTools MCP arguments for existing-session attachment, such as --no-usage-statistics. Endpoint arguments here override the built-in auto-connect or browser URL selection.

browser.profiles.*.driver.label: Browser Profile Driver
browser.profiles.*.driver.help: Per-profile browser driver mode. Use "openclaw" (or legacy "clawd") for CDP-based profiles, "existing-session" for Chrome DevTools MCP attachment, or "extension" for the authenticated Chrome extension relay.

browser.profiles.*.executablePath.label: Browser Profile Executable Path
browser.profiles.*.executablePath.help: Per-profile browser executable path for locally launched managed browser profiles. Overrides browser.executablePath and accepts paths starting with ~ for the OS home directory.

browser.profiles.*.headless.label: Browser Profile Headless Mode
browser.profiles.*.headless.help: Per-profile headless override for locally launched browser instances. Use this when one profile should stay headless without forcing browser.headless for every other profile.

browser.profiles.*.attachOnly.label: Browser Profile Attach-only Mode
browser.profiles.*.attachOnly.help: Per-profile attach-only override that skips local browser launch and only attaches to an existing CDP endpoint. Useful when one profile is externally managed but others are locally launched.

browser.extensionRelay.label: Browser Extension Relay
browser.extensionRelay.help: Chrome extension relay authentication compatibility settings. Keep the legacy window only while older paired extensions or external CDP clients still need it.

browser.extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth.label: Allow Legacy Browser Relay Auth
browser.extensionRelay.allowLegacyAuth.help: Temporarily accepts legacy Bearer, Basic, and token-subprotocol relay authentication. Default: true for one migration window. Set false after every extension and external CDP client uses Browser Relay Authentication v2.

browser.evaluateEnabled.label: Browser Evaluate Enabled
browser.evaluateEnabled.help: Enables browser-side evaluate helpers for runtime script evaluation capabilities where supported. Keep disabled unless your workflows require evaluate semantics beyond snapshots/navigation.

browser.snapshotDefaults.label: Browser Snapshot Defaults
browser.snapshotDefaults.help: Default snapshot capture configuration used when callers do not provide explicit snapshot options. Tune this for consistent capture behavior across channels and automation paths.

browser.snapshotDefaults.mode.label: Browser Snapshot Mode
browser.snapshotDefaults.mode.help: Default snapshot extraction mode controlling how page content is transformed for agent consumption. Choose the mode that balances readability, fidelity, and token footprint for your workflows.

browser.tabCleanup.label: Browser Tab Cleanup
browser.tabCleanup.help: Best-effort cleanup policy for browser tabs opened by primary-agent sessions. Keep enabled to avoid stale sandbox or managed-browser tabs accumulating across long-lived gateways.

browser.tabCleanup.enabled.label: Browser Tab Cleanup Enabled
browser.tabCleanup.enabled.help: Enables cleanup of idle tracked browser tabs for primary-agent sessions. Disable only when external tooling owns tab lifecycle completely.

browser.ssrfPolicy.label: Browser SSRF Policy
browser.ssrfPolicy.help: Server-side request forgery guardrail settings for browser/network fetch paths that could reach internal hosts. Keep restrictive defaults in production and open only explicitly approved targets.

browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPriva.label: Browser Dangerously Allow Private Network
browser.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPriva.help: Allows access to private-network address ranges from browser tooling. Default is disabled when unset; enable only for explicitly trusted private-network destinations.

browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.label: Browser Allowed Hostnames
browser.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.help: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed by browser SSRF policy checks. Keep the list minimal.

browser.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.label: Browser Blocked Hostnames
browser.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.help: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules, even with private-network access enabled. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

browser.ssrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Benchmark.label: Browser Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
browser.ssrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Benchmark.help: Allow RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15) for trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

browser.ssrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLocalR.label: Browser Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
browser.ssrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLocalR.help: Allow IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7) for trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

env.shellEnv.label: Shell Environment Import
env.shellEnv.help: Shell environment import controls for loading variables from your login shell during startup. Keep this enabled when you depend on profile-defined secrets or PATH customizations.

env.shellEnv.enabled.label: Shell Environment Import Enabled
env.shellEnv.enabled.help: Enables loading environment variables from the user shell profile during startup initialization. Keep enabled for developer machines, or disable in locked-down service environments with explicit env management.

env.shellEnv.timeoutMs.label: Shell Environment Import Timeout (ms)
env.shellEnv.timeoutMs.help: Maximum time in milliseconds allowed for shell environment resolution before fallback behavior applies. Use tighter timeouts for faster startup, or increase when shell initialization is heavy.

env.vars.label: Environment Variable Overrides
env.vars.help: Explicit key/value environment variable overrides merged into runtime process environment for OpenClaw. Use this for predictable environment configuration instead of relying only on shell profile side effects.

secrets.egressProxy.label: Secret Egress Proxy
secrets.egressProxy.help: Gateway-owned loopback proxy that replaces shared-store secret sentinels only at outbound request time. Restart the Gateway after changing this startup-scoped section.

secrets.egressProxy.enabled.label: Secret Egress Proxy Enabled
secrets.egressProxy.enabled.help: Enables secret egress substitution for Gateway-hosted agent subprocesses. Default: false.

secrets.egressProxy.allowedHosts.label: Secret Egress Proxy Allowed Hosts
secrets.egressProxy.allowedHosts.help: Opt-in traffic allowlist for requests and CONNECT tunnels. When present, destinations must appear in this list, a per-secret host binding, or bypassHosts. An empty list permits only bound or bypassed hosts. Restart the Gateway after changing it.

secrets.egressProxy.bypassHosts.label: Secret Egress Proxy Bypass Hosts
secrets.egressProxy.bypassHosts.help: Exact hostnames that use authenticated blind CONNECT tunnels for certificate-pinned clients. Sentinels remain ciphertext and will fail vendor authentication instead of exposing plaintext.

security.audit.suppressions.label: Audit Suppressions
security.audit.suppressions.help: Accepted security audit findings to omit from the active summary and findings list. Matching findings remain available under suppressedFindings in JSON output.

security.installPolicy.enabled.label: Enable Install Policy
security.installPolicy.enabled.help: Enable a trusted local policy command for skill and plugin installs and updates. When enabled without a configured command, supported install targets are blocked.

security.installPolicy.targets.label: Install Policy Targets
security.installPolicy.targets.help: Apply the install policy to "skill", "plugin", or both. Omit this list to cover every supported target.

security.installPolicy.exec.label: Install Policy Command
security.installPolicy.exec.help: Trusted local command that returns an "allow", "warn", or "block" install decision. Set an absolute executable path; OpenClaw runs it without a shell.

wizard.accessMode.label: Setup Discovery Access
wizard.accessMode.help: Discovery consent for guided setup: "full" scans silently while "guarded" asks before inspecting local applications.

wizard.appRecommendations.label: Setup App Recommendations
wizard.appRecommendations.help: Controls whether guided setup may use installed-application labels to recommend relevant plugins and skills.

wizard.lastRunAt.label: Wizard Last Run Timestamp
wizard.lastRunAt.help: Timestamp of the last successfully committed wizard run.

wizard.lastRunVersion.label: Wizard Last Run Version
wizard.lastRunVersion.help: OpenClaw version used by the last wizard run.

wizard.lastRunCommit.label: Wizard Last Run Commit
wizard.lastRunCommit.help: Source commit used by the last development wizard run.

wizard.lastRunCommand.label: Wizard Last Run Command
wizard.lastRunCommand.help: Command that invoked the last wizard run.

wizard.lastRunMode.label: Wizard Last Run Mode
wizard.lastRunMode.help: Whether the last wizard run targeted "local" or "remote" setup.

wizard.securityAcknowledgedAt.label: Wizard Security Acknowledgement Timestamp
wizard.securityAcknowledgedAt.help: Timestamp of the setup security acknowledgement, committed with the target config.

logging.audit.label: Audit Ledger
logging.audit.help: Bounded metadata-only audit history for operator review. Run and tool records are enabled by default; message lifecycle metadata is a separate privacy-sensitive opt-in. The background writer is best-effort rather than a lossless compliance archive.

logging.audit.enabled.label: Audit Ledger Enabled
logging.audit.enabled.help: Records new run, tool, and enabled message audit events. Default: true. Changes apply immediately; accepted writes finish and retained rows remain queryable until they expire.

logging.audit.executionIdentity.label: Execution Identity Audit
logging.audit.executionIdentity.help: Retains bounded execution-identity attribution for exact-run inspection. Default: false. Requires logging.audit.enabled and applies to newly admitted runs; existing contexts remain unchanged.

logging.audit.messages.label: Message Audit Scope
logging.audit.messages.help: Controls content-free message lifecycle records: "off" (default), "direct" for known direct conversations only, or "all" for direct, group, channel, and unknown conversation kinds. Requires logging.audit.enabled. Changes apply to subsequent lifecycle events.

diagnostics.otel.label: OpenTelemetry
diagnostics.otel.help: OpenTelemetry export settings for traces, metrics, and logs emitted by gateway components. Use this when integrating with centralized observability backends and distributed tracing pipelines.

diagnostics.cacheTrace.label: Cache Trace
diagnostics.cacheTrace.help: Cache-trace logging settings for observing cache decisions and payload context in embedded runs. Enable this temporarily for debugging and disable afterward to reduce sensitive log footprint.

logging.level.label: Log Level
logging.level.help: Primary log level threshold for runtime logger output: "silent", "fatal", "error", "warn", "info", "debug", or "trace". Keep "info" or "warn" for production, and use debug/trace only during investigation.

logging.file.label: Log File Path
logging.file.help: Optional file path for persisted log output in addition to or instead of console logging. Use a managed writable path and align retention/rotation with your operational policy.

logging.consoleLevel.label: Console Log Level
logging.consoleLevel.help: Console-specific log threshold: "silent", "fatal", "error", "warn", "info", "debug", or "trace" for terminal output control. Use this to keep local console quieter while retaining richer file logging if needed.

logging.consoleStyle.label: Console Log Style
logging.consoleStyle.help: Console output format style: "pretty" or "json". Use json for machine parsing pipelines and pretty for human-first terminal workflows.

logging.redactPatterns.label: Custom Redaction Patterns
logging.redactPatterns.help: Custom regex strings replace the default string list for logs and diagnostics. Built-in form-body, structured-auth, and AWS bare-key protections always apply. Tool arguments, results, and chat history are not redacted. Use this to mask deployment-specific tokens and identifiers in diagnostic output.

update.channel.label: Update Channel
update.channel.help: Update channel for git + npm installs ("stable", "extended-stable", "beta", or "dev"). Extended-stable is package-only: installation is foreground-only, with optional read-only startup hints.

update.checkOnStart.label: Update Check on Start
update.checkOnStart.help: Checks for updates when the Gateway starts, including read-only extended-stable hints (default: true). Set false to disable automatic Gateway and headless-node update checks, applies, and anonymous update pings.

update.auto.enabled.label: Auto Update Enabled
update.auto.enabled.help: Enable background auto-update for stable and beta package installs; extended-stable never auto-applies (default: false).

update.auto.schedule.label: Automatic Update Schedule
update.auto.schedule.help: Optional cron expression for Gateway automatic-update campaign starts, in the Gateway host timezone. Omit for the existing hourly cadence. Rollout delays and idle countdowns still apply; missed windows are skipped.

telemetry.enabled.label: Anonymous Feature Statistics
telemetry.enabled.help: Shares enabled channel and provider names, plugin count, and recent session count with the daily update check. Disabled by default and always disabled when DO_NOT_TRACK=1.

telemetry.consentedAt.label: Feature Statistics Consent Timestamp
telemetry.consentedAt.help: ISO timestamp recording when the operator accepted or declined anonymous feature statistics. Prevents the setup wizard from asking again.

surfaces.*.silentReply.label: Surface Silent Reply Policy
surfaces.*.silentReply.help: Overrides group silent-reply policy for one resolved delivery surface. Unset fields inherit agents.defaults.silentReply. Direct chats and internal sessions always require a reply.

diagnostics.enabled.label: Diagnostics Enabled
diagnostics.enabled.help: Master toggle for diagnostics instrumentation output in logs and telemetry wiring paths. Defaults to enabled; set false only in tightly constrained environments.

diagnostics.flags.label: Diagnostics Flags
diagnostics.flags.help: Enable targeted diagnostics logs by flag (e.g. ["telegram.http"]). Supports wildcards like "telegram.*" or "*".

diagnostics.otel.enabled.label: OpenTelemetry Enabled
diagnostics.otel.enabled.help: Enables OpenTelemetry export pipeline for traces, metrics, and logs based on configured endpoint/protocol settings. Keep disabled unless your collector endpoint and auth are fully configured.

diagnostics.otel.endpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.endpoint.help: Collector endpoint URL used for OpenTelemetry export transport, including scheme and port. Use a reachable, trusted collector endpoint and monitor ingestion errors after rollout.

diagnostics.otel.tracesEndpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Traces Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.tracesEndpoint.help: Signal-specific OTLP/HTTP trace endpoint. When set, this overrides diagnostics.otel.endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for trace export only.

diagnostics.otel.metricsEndpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Metrics Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.metricsEndpoint.help: Signal-specific OTLP/HTTP metrics endpoint. When set, this overrides diagnostics.otel.endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for metrics export only.

diagnostics.otel.logsEndpoint.label: OpenTelemetry Logs Endpoint
diagnostics.otel.logsEndpoint.help: Signal-specific OTLP/HTTP logs endpoint. When set, this overrides diagnostics.otel.endpoint and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT for log export only.

diagnostics.otel.protocol.label: OpenTelemetry Protocol
diagnostics.otel.protocol.help: OTel transport protocol for telemetry export. Only "http/protobuf" is accepted; run "openclaw doctor --fix" to repair a persisted legacy "grpc" value or get source-specific manual-edit guidance.

diagnostics.otel.headers.label: OpenTelemetry Headers
diagnostics.otel.headers.help: Additional HTTP request headers sent with OpenTelemetry export requests, often used for tenant auth or routing. Keep secrets in env-backed values and avoid unnecessary header sprawl.

diagnostics.otel.serviceName.label: OpenTelemetry Service Name
diagnostics.otel.serviceName.help: Service name reported in telemetry resource attributes to identify this gateway instance in observability backends. Use stable names so dashboards and alerts remain consistent over deployments.

diagnostics.otel.metricNamePrefix.label: OpenTelemetry Metric Name Prefix
diagnostics.otel.metricNamePrefix.help: Replaces the default "openclaw." prefix on OpenClaw-owned metric names. Use an empty string to remove the prefix, or up to 128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots, hyphens, and slashes starting with a letter. Include any separator you need, for example "acme."; standard gen_ai.* metric names are unchanged. Changing this value requires updating dashboards and alerts that query the old names.

diagnostics.otel.traces.label: OpenTelemetry Traces Enabled
diagnostics.otel.traces.help: Enable trace signal export to the configured OpenTelemetry collector endpoint. Keep enabled when latency/debug tracing is needed, and disable if you only want metrics/logs.

diagnostics.otel.metrics.label: OpenTelemetry Metrics Enabled
diagnostics.otel.metrics.help: Enable metrics signal export to the configured OpenTelemetry collector endpoint. Keep enabled for runtime health dashboards, and disable only if metric volume must be minimized.

diagnostics.otel.logs.label: OpenTelemetry Logs Enabled
diagnostics.otel.logs.help: Enable log signal export through OpenTelemetry in addition to local logging sinks. Use this when centralized log correlation is required across services and agents.

diagnostics.otel.logsExporter.label: OpenTelemetry Logs Exporter
diagnostics.otel.logsExporter.help: Log export sink for diagnostics.otel.logs. Use "otlp" for the configured OTLP logs endpoint, "stdout" for one JSON record per stdout line in container log pipelines, and "both" when both sinks are required.

diagnostics.otel.sampleRate.label: OpenTelemetry Trace Sample Rate
diagnostics.otel.sampleRate.help: Trace sampling rate (0-1) controlling how much trace traffic is exported to observability backends. Lower rates reduce overhead/cost, while higher rates improve debugging fidelity.

diagnostics.otel.flushIntervalMs.label: OpenTelemetry Flush Interval (ms)
diagnostics.otel.flushIntervalMs.help: Interval in milliseconds for periodic telemetry flush from buffers to the collector. Increase to reduce export chatter, or lower for faster visibility during active incident response.

diagnostics.otel.captureContent.label: OpenTelemetry Content Capture
diagnostics.otel.captureContent.help: Opt-in OTEL span content capture. Defaults to off; true captures non-system message and tool content.

diagnostics.cacheTrace.enabled.label: Cache Trace Enabled
diagnostics.cacheTrace.enabled.help: Log cache trace snapshots for embedded agent runs (default: false).

agents.entries.*.description.label: Description
agents.entries.*.description.help: Optional agent purpose shown on the Control UI chat welcome screen.

agents.entries.*.recommendedPrompts.label: Recommended Prompts
agents.entries.*.recommendedPrompts.help: Optional plain-text prompts on the agent chat welcome when no recent chats are available. Up to three entries, each at most 128 Unicode code points after whitespace normalization. Clicking a prompt submits it; omitted or empty uses defaults.

agents.entries.*.identity.avatar.label: Identity Avatar
agents.entries.*.identity.avatar.help: Agent avatar (workspace-relative path, http(s) URL, or data URI).

agents.entries.*.skills.label: Agent Skill Filter
agents.entries.*.skills.help: Optional allowlist of skills for this agent. If omitted, the agent inherits agents.defaults.skills when set; otherwise skills stay unrestricted. Set [] for no skills. An explicit list fully replaces inherited defaults instead of merging with them.

agents.entries.*.cwd.label: Agent Working Directory
agents.entries.*.cwd.help: Working directory for this agent's reply runs. Overrides agents.defaults.cwd but not session-spawned cwd; bootstrap and memory files stay in workspace. Supports ~ and relative paths; a distinct cwd requires an unsandboxed run.

agents.entries.*.runtime.label: Agent Runtime
agents.entries.*.runtime.help: Optional runtime descriptor for this agent. Use embedded for default OpenClaw execution or acp for external ACP harness defaults.

agents.entries.*.runtime.type.label: Agent Runtime Type
agents.entries.*.runtime.type.help: Runtime type for this agent: "embedded" (default OpenClaw runtime) or "acp" (ACP harness defaults).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.label: Agent ACP Runtime
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.help: ACP runtime defaults for this agent when runtime.type=acp. Binding-level ACP overrides still take precedence per conversation.

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.agent.label: Agent ACP Harness Agent
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.agent.help: Optional ACP harness agent id to use for this OpenClaw agent (for example codex, claude, cursor, gemini, openclaw).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.backend.label: Agent ACP Backend
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.backend.help: Optional ACP backend override for this agent's ACP sessions (falls back to global acp.backend).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.mode.label: Agent ACP Mode
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.mode.help: Optional ACP session mode default for this agent (persistent or oneshot).

agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.cwd.label: Agent ACP Working Directory
agents.entries.*.runtime.acp.cwd.help: Optional default working directory for this agent's ACP sessions.

agents.entries.*.thinkingDefault.label: Agent Thinking Default
agents.entries.*.thinkingDefault.help: Optional per-agent default thinking level. Overrides agents.defaults.thinkingDefault for this agent when no per-message or session override is set.

agents.entries.*.reasoningDefault.label: Agent Reasoning Default
agents.entries.*.reasoningDefault.help: Optional per-agent default reasoning visibility (on|off|stream). Applies when no per-message or session reasoning override is set.

agents.entries.*.fastModeDefault.label: Agent Fast Mode Default
agents.entries.*.fastModeDefault.help: Optional per-agent default for fast mode ("auto", "ultrafast", true, or false). Applies when no per-message or session fast-mode override is set.

agents.defaults.fastModeDefault.label: Default Agent Fast Mode
agents.defaults.fastModeDefault.help: Default fast-mode policy for the agent loop ("auto", "ultrafast", true, or false). Individual agent entries override it.

agents.entries.*.contextInjection.label: Agent Context Injection
agents.entries.*.contextInjection.help: Per-agent override for workspace bootstrap-file injection in the embedded runtime. Omit to inherit agents.defaults.contextInjection. Does not control CLI-backed prompt preparation.

agents.entries.*.bootstrapMaxChars.label: Agent Bootstrap Max Chars
agents.entries.*.bootstrapMaxChars.help: Per-agent override for max characters of each workspace bootstrap file injected into this agent's system prompt. Omit to inherit agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars.

agents.entries.*.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.label: Agent Bootstrap Total Max Chars
agents.entries.*.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.help: Per-agent override for max total characters across all workspace bootstrap files injected into this agent's system prompt. Omit to inherit agents.defaults.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.

agents.entries.*.experimental.label: Agent Experimental Flags
agents.entries.*.experimental.help: Per-agent experimental flags. Omitted fields inherit agents.defaults.experimental.

agents.entries.*.experimental.localModel.label: Agent Lean Local Model Mode
agents.entries.*.experimental.localModel.help: Per-agent troubleshooting override for lean local-model mode. Enable it only when restricting optional tools resolves a demonstrated model failure, without trimming tools from every agent.

agents.ownership.label: Agent Ownership Generation
agents.ownership.help: Durable multi-agent ownership generation marker. "explicit" means ambient channels, system-agent consults, Talk, cron, and bare CLI operations must resolve a surface-specific owner or stop when no owner can be identified. OpenClaw stamps this automatically when creating or migrating a fleet; omit it for a sole agent.

agents.defaults.label: Agent Defaults
agents.defaults.help: Shared default settings inherited by agents unless overridden per entry in agents.entries. Use defaults to enforce consistent baseline behavior and reduce duplicated per-agent configuration.

agents.defaults.contextLimits.label: Default Context Limits
agents.defaults.contextLimits.help: Focused per-agent-context budget defaults for selected high-volume excerpts and injected prompt blocks. Use this to tune bounded read/injection sizes without reopening any unbounded call paths.

agents.defaults.contextLimits.memoryGetM.label: Default memory_get Max Chars
agents.defaults.contextLimits.memoryGetM.help: Default max characters returned by memory_get before truncation metadata and continuation notice are added. Increase to approximate older larger excerpts, but keep it bounded.

agents.defaults.contextLimits.postCompac.label: Default Post-compaction Max Chars
agents.defaults.contextLimits.postCompac.help: Default max characters retained from AGENTS.md during post-compaction context refresh injection. Lower this to make compaction recovery cheaper, or raise it for agents that depend on longer startup guidance.

agents.entries.label: Agent List
agents.entries.help: Explicit list of configured agents with IDs and optional overrides for model, tools, identity, and workspace. Keep IDs stable over time so bindings, approvals, and session routing remain consistent.

agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.label: Agent Skills Limits
agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.help: Optional per-agent overrides for skills subsystem budgets. Use this when an agent needs a different skills prompt budget without introducing a second generic context-limits path.

agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.maxSkillsP.label: Agent Skills Prompt Max Chars
agents.entries.*.skillsLimits.maxSkillsP.help: Per-agent override for the skills prompt character budget. This extends the existing skills.limits.maxSkillsPromptChars path instead of routing the same budget through contextLimits.

agents.entries.*.contextLimits.label: Agent Context Limits
agents.entries.*.contextLimits.help: Optional per-agent overrides for the focused context budget knobs. Omitted fields inherit agents.defaults.contextLimits.

agents.entries.*.contextLimits.memoryGet.label: Agent memory_get Max Chars
agents.entries.*.contextLimits.memoryGet.help: Per-agent override for the default memory_get max character budget.

agents.entries.*.contextLimits.postCompa.label: Agent Post-compaction Max Chars
agents.entries.*.contextLimits.postCompa.help: Per-agent override for the post-compaction AGENTS.md excerpt budget.

cloudWorkers.requiredProfile.label: Required Worker Profile
cloudWorkers.requiredProfile.help: Require every session to execute on this worker profile. Sessions are placed automatically and cannot fall back to Gateway execution. Unavailable workers block turns, not Gateway startup.

cloudWorkers.desktop.label: Cloud Worker Desktop (Labs)
cloudWorkers.desktop.help: Enables the experimental worker.desktop.observe surface and web app Desktop panel for desktop-capable cloud worker environments.

cloudWorkers.preparedPool.label: Cloud Worker Prepared Pool
cloudWorkers.preparedPool.help: Limits for prepared cloud workers kept ready for later sessions. Reserves incur running-machine charges until provider cleanup completes; their fixed expiry follows actual project demand and the provider's existing idle policy.

cloudWorkers.preparedPool.maxTotal.label: Cloud Worker Ready Reserve Cap
cloudWorkers.preparedPool.maxTotal.help: Gateway-wide cap on unassigned prepared cloud workers across projects and profiles (default: 4). Preparing workers and unconfirmed reserve cleanup count toward the cap. Set 0 to drain unassigned reserves and disable replenishment while preserving snapshot reuse and active sessions.

cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.label: Cloud Worker Project Profiles
cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.help: Default cloud worker profile names keyed by normalized lowercase repository identity (host/owner/repo). Explicit dispatch profile ids take precedence.

cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.*.label: Cloud Worker Project Profile
cloudWorkers.projectProfiles.*.help: Cloud worker profile name used by default when a session worktree's origin matches this repository identity.

cloudWorkers.profiles.label: Cloud Worker Profiles
cloudWorkers.profiles.help: Named cloud worker profiles. Each profile selects a worker provider registered by a plugin and carries provider-owned settings.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.label: Cloud Worker Profile
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.help: One cloud worker profile selected by name when creating an environment. Keep provider credentials in supported references rather than embedding secret material in this block.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.provider.label: Cloud Worker Provider
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.provider.help: Worker provider id registered by a plugin. The configured plugin must expose this id before the gateway can provision environments from the profile.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.install.label: Cloud Worker Install Method
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.install.help: Worker installation method: "bundle" (default) transfers the gateway's content-hashed installed build and supports released, development, and unreleased versions; "npm" installs the exact gateway version and is available only when that version is released.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.workspaceDurabil.label: Repository Workspace Durability
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.workspaceDurabil.help: Mirrored by default. Retained-disk repositories require an exact-resource managed-node provider and an explicit finite compute window in seconds. The original disk remains authoritative between turns; Move to Gateway exports and retires it.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.suspendAfter.label: Cloud Worker Idle Suspend Duration
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.suspendAfter.help: Automatically reclaims an idle cloud worker after this duration, such as 45m or 2h; the next message provisions a replacement. Minimum: 1m. Leave unset to keep workers running.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.readyWorkers.label: Cloud Worker Ready Reserve Target
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.readyWorkers.help: Target unassigned prepared workers per eligible project using this profile (default: 1), subject to the Gateway-wide prepared pool cap. Set 0 to disable this profile's reserves while preserving snapshot reuse. Preparing workers and unconfirmed reserve cleanup count toward the target.

cloudWorkers.profiles.*.settings.label: Cloud Worker Provider Settings
cloudWorkers.profiles.*.settings.help: Provider-owned settings validated by the selected plugin. Use SecretRef objects for secret-bearing values; opaque settings do not gain automatic secret resolution.

database.engine.label: Database Engine
database.engine.help: Default store engine (default: sqlite). PostgreSQL supports state, agent, workboard, logbook, and team-reports unless database.families overrides them; safety stores stay local SQLite. Changing an engine does not migrate existing data.

database.families.label: Family Database Engines
database.families.help: Optional engine overrides for state, agent, workboard, logbook, and team-reports. Each override requires engine. State and agent families may use different engines; local safety journals are not configurable. All PostgreSQL families share database.postgres.

database.families.state.engine.label: Family Database Engine
database.families.state.engine.help: Override database.engine for this family. Changing an engine requires database port --family and a restart; editing config does not migrate existing data. Mixed-engine backup/restore preserves each store's engine, and updates require candidate family support.

database.families.agent.engine.label: Family Database Engine
database.families.agent.engine.help: Override database.engine for this family. Changing an engine requires database port --family and a restart; editing config does not migrate existing data. Mixed-engine backup/restore preserves each store's engine, and updates require candidate family support.

database.families.workboard.engine.label: Family Database Engine
database.families.workboard.engine.help: Override database.engine for this family. Changing an engine requires database port --family and a restart; editing config does not migrate existing data. Mixed-engine backup/restore preserves each store's engine, and updates require candidate family support.

database.families.logbook.engine.label: Family Database Engine
database.families.logbook.engine.help: Override database.engine for this family. Changing an engine requires database port --family and a restart; editing config does not migrate existing data. Mixed-engine backup/restore preserves each store's engine, and updates require candidate family support.

database.families.team-reports.engine.label: Family Database Engine
database.families.team-reports.engine.help: Override database.engine for this family. Changing an engine requires database port --family and a restart; editing config does not migrate existing data. Mixed-engine backup/restore preserves each store's engine, and updates require candidate family support.

database.postgres.label: PostgreSQL
database.postgres.help: PostgreSQL connection and schema naming. PostgreSQL 16–18 are qualified; other admitted majors remain experimental pending conformance. Back up each store schema together with its local SQLite anchor. See the PostgreSQL operator guide for deployment qualification limits.

database.postgres.connection.label: PostgreSQL Connection
database.postgres.connection.help: Shared PostgreSQL DSN, required when any effective family engine is postgres. Supports env, file, and exec SecretRefs and TLS connections; see the PostgreSQL operator guide for setup and qualification limits. Store-backed refs cannot bootstrap the database. The host resolves it once for database workers. Connection failures never fall back to SQLite.

database.postgres.schemaPrefix.label: PostgreSQL Schema Prefix
database.postgres.schemaPrefix.help: Prefix for new PostgreSQL store schemas (default: openclaw). Use 1–27 lowercase letters, digits, or underscores, starting with a letter or underscore. Existing anchors retain their schema.

database.postgres.recoveryCaptures.label: PostgreSQL Recovery Captures
database.postgres.recoveryCaptures.help: Where update and Doctor rollback captures keep PostgreSQL rows (default: portable). portable writes a local SQLite export image. server keeps the rows in a restore_ schema on the same database and writes only the anchor and manifest locally; it saves local disk and export time but does not survive loss of the server. User backups stay portable.

database.postgres.ownership.label: PostgreSQL Gateway Ownership
database.postgres.ownership.help: Scope of Gateway state ownership (default: state-directory, a local lock file). installation also holds a PostgreSQL session advisory lock keyed by the database and schema prefix, so a second Gateway or maintenance owner for the same installation is refused on any host, and losing that session stops the Gateway. Requires every configurable family to use postgres. Store anchors and other local files are unchanged; see the PostgreSQL operator guide.

storage.locations.label: Storage Locations
storage.locations.help: Named storage destinations. Names contain 1–63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens and start with a letter or digit. Each destination keeps an initialization marker that runtime writes never create.

storage.locations.*.label: Storage Location
storage.locations.*.help: One named storage destination with provider settings and an explicit encryption choice. Initialize a new destination with openclaw storage init before writing objects.

storage.locations.*.provider.label: Storage Provider
storage.locations.*.provider.help: Storage provider id, such as "filesystem". Referencing a bundled provider automatically enables its plugin unless plugin policy disables it.

storage.locations.*.settings.label: Storage Provider Settings
storage.locations.*.settings.help: Provider-owned bounded JSON settings. Secret-bearing values must use SecretRef objects, which the provider resolves only when needed. The filesystem provider requires an absolute path to an existing directory.

storage.locations.*.encryption.label: Storage Encryption
storage.locations.*.encryption.help: Required encryption choice: a passphrase object encrypts objects before upload; "none" explicitly disables encryption. Backups can contain credentials, so use "none" only when the destination already provides suitable protection.

storage.locations.*.encryption.passphras.label: Storage Encryption Passphrase
storage.locations.*.encryption.passphras.help: Passphrase used to encrypt this location. Prefer a SecretRef and keep a recoverable copy: losing or changing the passphrase makes existing encrypted objects unreadable.

desktop.host.label: Local Desktop
desktop.host.help: Desktop observation for paired nodes, or the experimental Gateway host source, backed by a local VNC server.

desktop.host.enabled.label: Desktop Sharing
desktop.host.enabled.help: Enables this machine's desktop source. Paired macOS, Windows, and Linux nodes default to enabled; an explicit desktop-app sharing preference takes precedence. The Gateway host Labs source defaults to disabled and applies changes live. Restart a paired node after changing its desktop config.

desktop.host.managed.label: Managed Linux Host Desktop
desktop.host.managed.help: Runs and supervises a loopback-only headless TigerVNC/XFCE desktop on Linux. An explicit port or existing default-port VNC server still takes precedence.

desktop.host.port.label: Local VNC Port
desktop.host.port.help: Loopback RFB port of an already-running VNC server on this machine (default: 5900).

desktop.host.passwordFile.label: Local VNC Password File
desktop.host.passwordFile.help: Absolute path to the VNC password file. Omit on macOS to enter account credentials when opening the desktop viewer.

gateway.repositoryIntegration.label: Repository Integration
gateway.repositoryIntegration.help: Plugin ID required to admit worker repository source access, including native, GitHub App, and managed OAuth or PAT credentials. Missing, disabled or unloaded owners deny admission. Omit to use native repository behavior; enabling a plugin alone does not select it.

gateway.port.label: Gateway Port
gateway.port.help: TCP port used by the gateway listener for API, web app, and channel-facing ingress paths. Use a dedicated port and avoid collisions with reverse proxies or local developer services.

gateway.mode.label: Gateway Mode
gateway.mode.help: Gateway operation mode: "local" runs channels and agent runtime on this host, while "remote" connects through remote transport. Keep "local" unless you intentionally run a split remote gateway topology.

gateway.bind.label: Gateway Bind Mode
gateway.bind.help: Network bind profile: "auto", "lan", "loopback", "custom", or "tailnet" to control interface exposure. Keep "loopback" for local-only operation; "auto" can expose all interfaces.

gateway.customBindHost.label: Gateway Custom Bind Host
gateway.customBindHost.help: IPv4 address used for a custom bind. Specific IPv4s also require the same Gateway port on 127.0.0.1; avoid 0.0.0.0 unless all-interface exposure is required.

gateway.portals.label: Gateway Portals
gateway.portals.help: Portal publication and private ingress settings.

gateway.portals.ingress.label: Private Portal Ingress
gateway.portals.ingress.help: Optional operator-managed private HTTPS wildcard reverse proxy. Forward original Host, paths, and WebSocket upgrades to the dedicated loopback listener. Portal bearer authentication remains required. Requires Gateway restart.

gateway.portals.ingress.domain.label: Portal Wildcard Domain
gateway.portals.ingress.domain.help: Bare DNS domain for random portal subdomains (for example previews.example.net). Configure wildcard DNS and HTTPS privately; do not share the Gateway or web app hostname namespace.

gateway.portals.ingress.port.label: Portal Ingress Loopback Port
gateway.portals.ingress.port.help: Dedicated loopback HTTP port receiving the private wildcard HTTPS proxy. Must differ from the Gateway port. This is the backend port, not the public HTTPS port.

gateway.openclawId.label: OpenClaw ID Remote Access
gateway.openclawId.help: Experimental OpenClaw ID remote access (Labs). When enabled, the Gateway supervises a tunnel child that accepts iroh connections from admitted devices and proxies them to this Gateway. Off by default; while off the Gateway starts no child process, opens no tunnel sockets, and contacts no OpenClaw ID, Discovery or relay service.

gateway.openclawId.enabled.label: OpenClaw ID Remote Access Enabled
gateway.openclawId.enabled.help: Turns on experimental OpenClaw ID remote access (default: false). Changes apply without restarting the Gateway. Remote access also needs relayUrl; linking a claw additionally needs issuerUrl, discoveryUrl and loaderDomain.

gateway.openclawId.issuerUrl.label: OpenClaw ID Issuer URL
gateway.openclawId.issuerUrl.help: OpenClaw ID issuer used to sign in for identity only while linking a claw. It is never trusted for membership, device approval or which server a client dials.

gateway.openclawId.clientId.label: OpenClaw ID Web App Client ID
gateway.openclawId.clientId.help: Public OAuth client (authorization code with PKCE) the web app uses for Sign in with OpenClaw ID in its account menu. Its redirect URI is <web app origin>/openclaw-id/callback. On this machine sign-in uses that redirect; a web app reached through a personal sign-in such as Tailscale uses the issuer's device grant.

gateway.openclawId.discoveryUrl.label: OpenClaw ID Discovery URL
gateway.openclawId.discoveryUrl.help: Discovery service that mirrors the claw descriptor and membership snapshot and relays mailbox messages. It is untrusted: every statement it returns is verified against the claw's pinned owner root.

gateway.openclawId.relayUrl.label: OpenClaw ID Relay URL
gateway.openclawId.relayUrl.help: The only iroh relay in the tunnel endpoint's relay map (no public n0 relays, DNS or pkarr). Browsers reach the claw only through this relay.

gateway.openclawId.loaderDomain.label: OpenClaw ID Loader Domain
gateway.openclawId.loaderDomain.help: Bare DNS domain of the OpenClaw ID loader; a linked claw is reachable at https://<name>-<account tag>.<loaderDomain> and its server binding is signed for that hostname.

gateway.openclawId.ownerDeviceInactivity.label: OpenClaw ID Owner Device Inactivity (Days)
gateway.openclawId.ownerDeviceInactivity.help: Days an owner device may go without reaching this claw before the claw removes it from its allowlist (default: 90). Devices it approved stay.

gateway.openclawId.memberDeviceInactivit.label: OpenClaw ID Member Device Inactivity (Days)
gateway.openclawId.memberDeviceInactivit.help: Days a member's browser may go without reaching this claw before the claw removes it (default: 30). The member stays listed.

gateway.publicOrigin.label: Gateway Public Origin
gateway.publicOrigin.help: Externally reachable HTTPS origin of the Gateway. Also the default browser origin when gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins is omitted. HTTP is allowed only for localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1]. Per-requester MCP OAuth uses it to build the callback URL at /oauth/mcp/callback; channel session links and plugin-generated viewer links use it to reach the web app and Gateway routes.

gateway.controlUi.label: Web app
gateway.controlUi.help: Web app hosting settings including enablement, pathing, and browser-origin/auth hardening behavior. Keep UI exposure minimal and pair with strong auth controls before internet-facing deployments.

gateway.controlUi.enabled.label: Web App Enabled
gateway.controlUi.enabled.help: Enables serving the web app from the gateway HTTP process when true. Keep enabled for local administration, and disable when an external control surface replaces it.

gateway.controlUi.basePath.label: Web App Base Path
gateway.controlUi.basePath.help: Optional URL prefix where the web app is served (e.g. /openclaw).

gateway.controlUi.experimental.label: Experimental Web App Features
gateway.controlUi.experimental.help: Web app experiments and retained advanced overrides. Experiments are disabled by default unless their setting documents otherwise.

gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlu.label: Custom Plugin UI
gateway.controlUi.experimental.customPlu.help: Allow enabled user-installed plugins to execute native JavaScript in the web app (default: true). Retained as an advanced config-only opt-out; existing false values remain off. Bundled plugin views are unaffected. Native UI shares the signed-in operator's Gateway permissions; install only trusted plugins. Changes apply without a Gateway restart. After disabling, reload open web app pages to clear previously loaded plugin code.

gateway.controlUi.experimental.templates.label: Templates
gateway.controlUi.experimental.templates.help: Enable ClawHub discovery and one-way Add through the web app and Gateway (default: false). Existing agents keep running while this is off.

gateway.controlUi.experimental.chatBubbl.label: Speech Bubbles
gateway.controlUi.experimental.chatBubbl.help: Enable experimental speech bubbles in the web app (default: false). Home defaults to bubbles while enabled; browser-local per-session choices take precedence. Changes apply without a Gateway restart.

gateway.controlUi.environment.label: Web App Environment
gateway.controlUi.environment.help: Optional public environment identity shown in the web app stripe, agent avatar, label pills, browser title, and favicon. Omit it to preserve the default appearance.

gateway.controlUi.environment.label.label: Web App Environment Label
gateway.controlUi.environment.label.help: Environment label displayed in the web app and browser tab; surrounding whitespace is trimmed and the label must contain 1 to 24 characters.

gateway.controlUi.environment.color.label: Web App Environment Color
gateway.controlUi.environment.color.help: Named environment color ramp: teal, amber, purple, coral, pink, blue, green, red, or gray.

gateway.controlUi.communityInvite.label: Web App Community Invitation
gateway.controlUi.communityInvite.help: Show a dismissible Community card in the web app sidebar (default on), with Discord, Reddit, and X links. Set false to hide it for every browser using this UI deployment. Changes apply after browser refresh or reconnect. Existing browser-local dismissals remain honored.

gateway.controlUi.newSessionModelDefault.label: New Session Model Defaults
gateway.controlUi.newSessionModelDefault.help: Choose "configured" to start fresh web app drafts with the selected agent’s configured model, runtime and reasoning defaults instead of remembered selections. Default: "last-used". Explicit draft and conversation choices remain editable; Fast Mode and placement preferences are unchanged. Applies after browser refresh or reconnect.

gateway.controlUi.github.host.label: Web App GitHub Service Host
gateway.controlUi.github.host.help: Host this service credential may access. Omit for github.com; set to gateway.github.host for Enterprise project discovery and account metadata.

gateway.controlUi.github.token.label: Web App GitHub Service Credential
gateway.controlUi.github.token.help: SecretRef-backed service credential for web app project discovery and GitHub hover previews without a managed identity. Set gateway.controlUi.github.host for Enterprise; an omitted host means github.com. Hover previews prefer the selected agent's configured GitHub identity. GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN fallback applies only to github.com. Requests using a mismatched or unavailable credential are rejected.

gateway.controlUi.sessionObserver.label: Web App Session Observer
gateway.controlUi.sessionObserver.help: Produce live session status digests for subscribed web app clients with each agent's utility model (default on). Set false to disable observer model calls gateway-wide; setting agents.defaults.utilityModel to an empty string disables utility-model observation for agents that do not override it.

gateway.controlUi.root.label: Web App Assets Root
gateway.controlUi.root.help: Optional filesystem root for web app assets (defaults to dist/control-ui).

gateway.controlUi.embedSandbox.label: Web App Embed Sandbox Mode
gateway.controlUi.embedSandbox.help: Iframe sandbox policy for hosted web app embeds. "strict" disables scripts, "scripts" allows interactive embeds while keeping origin isolation (default), and "trusted" adds `allow-same-origin` for same-site documents that intentionally need stronger privileges.

gateway.controlUi.allowExternalEmbedUrls.label: Allow External Web App Embed URLs
gateway.controlUi.allowExternalEmbedUrls.help: DANGEROUS toggle that allows hosted embeds to load absolute external http(s) URLs. Keep this off unless your web app intentionally embeds trusted third-party pages; hosted /__openclaw__/canvas documents do not need it.

gateway.controlUi.automaticallyFetchFavi.label: Automatically Fetch Link Favicons
gateway.controlUi.automaticallyFetchFavi.help: Fetch link favicons and external-link page previews through the Gateway (default on). Page previews load public page metadata and declared images without browser cookies or site credentials. All requests use strict SSRF checks and bounded HTML/image processing. Set false to disable both automatic favicon and page-preview fetches; live browser screenshots are unaffected.

gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins.label: Web App Allowed Origins
gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins.help: Allowed browser origins for web app/WebChat connections (full origins only, e.g. https://control.example.com). When omitted, defaults to gateway.publicOrigin if configured. An explicit list, including [], overrides that default; existing local/private-origin rules still apply. Setting ["*"] means allow any browser origin and should be avoided outside tightly controlled local testing.

gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHe.label: Dangerously Allow Host-Header Origin Fallback
gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHe.help: DANGEROUS toggle that enables Host-header based origin fallback for web app/WebChat websocket checks. This mode is supported when your deployment intentionally relies on Host-header origin policy; explicit gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins remains the recommended hardened default.

gateway.uploads.label: File and Image Uploads
gateway.uploads.help: Client file and image upload policy for the Gateway and web app. Downloads and agent-generated media remain available.

gateway.uploads.enabled.label: Uploads Enabled
gateway.uploads.enabled.help: Allows client file and image uploads (default: true). Set false to reject attachments, workspace/terminal uploads, avatar uploads, and archive imports at the Gateway, including direct API requests. Changes apply without restarting. This is not a sandbox or a restriction on channel media, agent tools, or operator shell access.

gateway.cliAgents.label: CLI Agents
gateway.cliAgents.help: Web app discovery for external CLI session engines exposed by the Gateway session catalog. Enabled by default; disable to prevent starting those engines from the new-session model picker.

gateway.cliAgents.enabled.label: CLI Agents Enabled
gateway.cliAgents.enabled.help: Shows catalog-backed CLI agents in the web app new-session model picker when true (default: true). Set false to disable CLI agents and native CLI session creation. Only catalogs that advertise session creation are listed, and the picker stays hidden when the Gateway does not advertise session catalog support.

gateway.terminal.label: Operator Terminal
gateway.terminal.help: Operator terminal served to web app and mobile clients: a PTY-backed shell on the gateway host, restricted to admin-scope operator sessions. It starts in the target agent's workspace and is refused for fully-sandboxed agents (sandbox.mode 'all') rather than handing back an unconfined host shell.

gateway.terminal.enabled.label: Operator Terminal Enabled
gateway.terminal.enabled.help: Enables the operator terminal for admin-scope clients (default: true). This exposes a browser/mobile shell with the gateway process environment; set false to opt out on deployments where admin operators should not get a host shell. Changes apply without restarting the Gateway.

gateway.terminal.shell.label: Operator Terminal Shell
gateway.terminal.shell.help: Shell executable the operator terminal launches. Leave unset to use the host login shell ($SHELL on Unix, %ComSpec% on Windows), or pin an explicit interpreter for a consistent operator environment.

gateway.terminal.detachedSessionTimeoutS.label: Operator Terminal Detached Session Timeout
gateway.terminal.detachedSessionTimeoutS.help: Seconds a terminal session survives after its connection drops (laptop sleep, page reload), staying reattachable via terminal.attach with its recent output replayed. Set 0 to kill sessions the moment the connection drops. Default: 300 (5 minutes). Detached sessions keep running their commands, so shorten this on shared or exposed hosts.

gateway.auth.label: Gateway Auth
gateway.auth.help: Authentication policy for gateway HTTP/WebSocket access including mode, credentials, trusted-proxy behavior, and rate limiting. Keep auth enabled for every non-loopback deployment.

gateway.auth.mode.label: Gateway Auth Mode
gateway.auth.mode.help: Gateway auth mode: "none", "token", "password", or "trusted-proxy" depending on your edge architecture. Token/password mode selects the configured secret (gateway.auth.token or gateway.auth.password); clients may send it in either connect auth field. Use token/password for direct exposure, and trusted-proxy only behind hardened identity-aware proxies.

gateway.auth.allowTailscale.label: Gateway Auth Allow Tailscale Identity
gateway.auth.allowTailscale.help: Allows trusted Tailscale identity paths to satisfy gateway auth checks when configured. Use this only when your tailnet identity posture is strong and operator workflows depend on it.

gateway.auth.identityScopes.label: Gateway Identity Scope Grants
gateway.auth.identityScopes.help: Maps verified trusted-proxy or Tailscale identities to connection-only operator scope grants. Email keys match case-insensitively; grants augment device scopes before the connection scope cap is applied.

gateway.auth.rateLimit.label: Gateway Auth Rate Limit
gateway.auth.rateLimit.help: Login/auth attempt throttling controls to reduce credential brute-force risk at the gateway boundary. Keep enabled in exposed environments and tune thresholds to your traffic baseline.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.label: Gateway Trusted Proxy Auth
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.help: Trusted-proxy auth header mapping for upstream identity providers that inject user claims. Use only with known proxy CIDRs and strict header allowlists to prevent spoofed identity headers.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.label: Cloudflare Access OIDC GitHub Identity
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.help: Optional verified GitHub identity from a selected Cloudflare Access OIDC provider. Requires the standard Access email and assertion headers. Missing claims keep email-only profiles; existing profile roles and co-author preferences are preserved.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.delegation.label: Enterprise Browser Delegation
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.delegation.help: Accept revision-scoped OCE browser identity and scope grants through the private trusted proxy. Delegated profiles do not use email aliases or device grants.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.delegation.cre.label: Delegation Credential File
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.delegation.cre.help: Absolute path to a private file containing the revision's 32-byte credential as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters. File replacement or removal invalidates existing grants.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.label: Cloudflare Access Issuer
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.help: Exact HTTPS origin of the trusted Cloudflare Access team, such as https://example.cloudflareaccess.com, without a trailing slash. Claims from other issuers do not supply GitHub identity.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.label: Cloudflare Access OIDC Provider ID
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.help: Exact Access identity-provider ID for the trusted OIDC integration. A provider display name or a matching claim name alone does not establish trust.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.label: GitHub Account ID Claim
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.cloudflareAcce.help: Exact forwarded OIDC claim whose value is a verified positive decimal-string GitHub account ID. Configure Access to forward it, then inspect the authenticated Access identity response. OpenClaw reads oidc_fields, or custom when oidc_fields is absent. Never use an unverified user-editable claim.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.label: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.help: Optional policy for automatically approving new browser and native UI operator devices and same-key scope upgrades after trusted-proxy authentication. Grants are capped by deviceAutoApprove.scopes and the proxy's x-openclaw-scopes header when present.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.label: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval Enabled
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.help: Automatically approves new browser and native UI operator devices and same-key scope upgrades after the reverse proxy authenticates an allowed user. Default: false. Enable only when the proxy identity boundary is strong enough to replace manual device pairing.

gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.label: Trusted Proxy Device Auto-Approval Scopes
gateway.auth.trustedProxy.deviceAutoAppr.help: Maximum scopes granted to auto-approved operator devices. Defaults to operator.read, operator.write, operator.approvals, and operator.questions. Requested scopes are capped to this list; requests without scopes receive this list. When unset, auto-approval also adds operator.questions for older UI clients; an explicit list is never widened. Explicitly listing operator.admin lets every proxy-authenticated user auto-approve full admin and makes scope-less requests receive full admin automatically; it also triggers a critical security audit finding and Gateway startup warning.

gateway.roles.label: Gateway Operator Roles
gateway.roles.help: Named operator-role definitions for team Gateways. Setting gateway.roles.default enables profile-bound enforcement of session access, sandbox isolation, agents, and operator scopes. Definitions without a default are a catalog only and preserve the behavior of a Gateway without gateway.roles.

gateway.roles.default.label: Default Operator Role (Enables Enforcement)
gateway.roles.default.help: Optional default that enables named-role enforcement and applies to authenticated profiles without a valid explicit or GitHub login assignment. Its name must match a configured definition. Omitting it leaves named-role enforcement off, even when definitions exist.

gateway.roles.assignments.label: Operator Role Assignments
gateway.roles.assignments.help: Optional declarative role assignments for authenticated profiles. A valid explicit assignment made with users.setRole takes precedence over these mappings, followed by the default role.

gateway.roles.assignments.byGithubLogin.label: Operator Roles by GitHub Login
gateway.roles.assignments.byGithubLogin.help: Requires gateway.roles.default, even for an empty mapping. Maps cached GitHub identity logins to configured role names, matching case-insensitively after trimming. Invalid logins, duplicate normalized logins, and unknown roles are rejected. Profiles without a cached GitHub identity use their explicit assignment or default role.

gateway.roles.assignments.byGithubLogin..label: GitHub Login Operator Role
gateway.roles.assignments.byGithubLogin..help: Configured role name for this GitHub login. Applies when the profile has a matching cached GitHub identity and no valid explicit role assignment. Changes hot-apply when config reload is enabled.

gateway.roles.definitions.label: Operator Role Definitions
gateway.roles.definitions.help: Nonempty administrator-named role catalog bundling session-sharing, sandbox-isolation, agent-access, and operator-scope policies. Definitions alone do not enable enforcement; set gateway.roles.default to apply named roles to authenticated profiles.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.label: Operator Role Definition
gateway.roles.definitions.*.help: One named operator role. Every definition must explicitly provide its session-sharing policy, allowed session and run agents, and operator-scope ceiling, and can require sandbox isolation for newly created sessions and a plugin access policy.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.label: Operator Role Session Access
gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.help: Session-sharing permissions granted to this role for sessions created by other authenticated people; a person's own sessions remain owner-accessible.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.oth.label: Operator Role Access to Other Sessions
gateway.roles.definitions.*.sessions.oth.help: Access to other people's sessions: "none" hides them even with explicit session membership, "invited" requires explicit membership, "view" allows reading, "suggest" permits the suggestion flow, and "write" permits participation without membership. Explicit session membership can raise "view" or "suggest" access for a specific session. Session creators and connections holding operator.admin retain their session access. A creator or admin can invite an explicitly configured "invited" profile with a selected human @mention; connection scopes and draft/incognito restrictions still apply.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.sandbox.label: Operator Role Sandbox Isolation
gateway.roles.definitions.*.sandbox.help: Execution isolation for newly created sessions: "inherit" (default) uses the agent policy; "required" permanently requires a sandbox, even when the agent sandbox mode is off, and blocks execution if the backend is unavailable.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.agents.label: Operator Role Allowed Agents
gateway.roles.definitions.*.agents.help: Agents available when this role creates sessions or starts runs: set "*" to allow every agent, list agent IDs to allow only those agents, or use an empty list to disable both.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy.label: Operator Role Model Policy
gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy.help: Optional model ceiling for this role's requests and descendants. An empty object allows only the source agent's configured primary and fallback models; omitting the policy leaves model access unchanged. Model aliases resolve before enforcement, and denied models cannot be used by retries or fallbacks. With config reload enabled, changes confined to existing roles' model policies apply when committed without restarting permitted work. Other role changes hot-apply and reconnect clients with current authority.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy..label: Operator Role Model Source Agent
gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy..help: Agent whose primary, fallbacks, and model aliases supply this role's model policy. Defaults to the configured system/default agent or the sole agent. Set this explicitly when a multi-agent Gateway has no ambient owner.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy..label: Operator Role Allowed Models
gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy..help: Optional replacement allowlist of model references, configured aliases, or trailing prefix wildcards such as "provider/*" or "provider/family-*". Omitted uses the source agent primary and fallbacks; an empty list denies all models. The first permitted source model remains Default, followed by explicit allowed models.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy..label: Operator Role Excluded Models
gateway.roles.definitions.*.modelPolicy..help: Model references, source-agent aliases, or trailing prefix wildcards excluded from this role. A pattern such as "provider/family-*" excludes future members of that family too. Exclusions match resolved model identities and take precedence over allowed and source-agent models.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.scopes.label: Operator Role Scope Ceiling
gateway.roles.definitions.*.scopes.help: Closed list of operator scopes granted as this role's maximum connection authority. Requested, paired, identity-granted, and upgraded scopes are intersected with this list.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.workerProfil.label: Operator Role Worker Profiles
gateway.roles.definitions.*.workerProfil.help: Cloud worker profiles this role may explicitly dispatch its own sessions to. Omitted or empty denies cloud dispatch; administrators retain access. Setup and moves to cloud profiles remain administrator-only.

gateway.roles.definitions.*.accessPolicy.label: Operator Role Access Policy Plugin
gateway.roles.definitions.*.accessPolicy.help: Optional exact plugin ID whose Gateway access policy must authorize this role. Access is denied when the plugin is missing, disabled, fails to load, or supplies no current authority. Unavailable plugin IDs remain valid configuration so independent staff roles and the Gateway owner can repair access. Omitting this field adds no plugin dependency.

gateway.trustedProxies.label: Gateway Trusted Proxy CIDRs
gateway.trustedProxies.help: CIDR/IP allowlist of upstream proxies permitted to provide forwarded client identity headers. Keep this list narrow so untrusted hops cannot impersonate users.

gateway.allowRealIpFallback.label: Gateway Allow x-real-ip Fallback
gateway.allowRealIpFallback.help: Enables x-real-ip fallback when x-forwarded-for is missing in proxy scenarios. Keep disabled unless your ingress stack requires this compatibility behavior.

gateway.tools.label: Gateway Tool Exposure Policy
gateway.tools.help: Gateway-level tool exposure allow/deny policy that can restrict runtime tool availability independent of agent/tool profiles. Use this for coarse emergency controls and production hardening.

gateway.tools.allow.label: Gateway Tool Allowlist
gateway.tools.allow.help: Explicit gateway-level tool allowlist when you want a narrow set of tools available at runtime. Use this for locked-down environments where tool scope must be tightly controlled.

gateway.tools.deny.label: Gateway Tool Denylist
gateway.tools.deny.help: Explicit gateway-level tool denylist to block risky tools even if lower-level policies allow them. Use deny rules for emergency response and defense-in-depth hardening.

gateway.tailscale.label: Gateway Tailscale
gateway.tailscale.help: Tailscale integration settings for Serve/Funnel exposure and lifecycle handling on gateway start/exit. Keep off unless your deployment intentionally relies on Tailscale ingress.

gateway.tailscale.mode.label: Gateway Tailscale Mode
gateway.tailscale.mode.help: Tailscale publish mode: "off", "serve", or "funnel" for private or public exposure paths. Use "serve" for tailnet-only access and "funnel" only when public internet reachability is required.

gateway.tailscale.preserveFunnel.label: Gateway Tailscale External Funnel Migration Guard
gateway.tailscale.preserveFunnel.help: Deprecated migration guard for mode='serve'. If an external Funnel still targets the ordinary Gateway listener, OpenClaw leaves exposure unchanged and warns that only plugin-authenticated webhooks remain usable until password auth is configured and mode is migrated to 'funnel'.

gateway.remote.label: Remote Gateway
gateway.remote.help: Remote gateway connection settings for direct or SSH transport when this instance proxies to another runtime host. Use remote mode only when split-host operation is intentionally configured.

gateway.remote.transport.label: Remote Gateway Transport
gateway.remote.transport.help: Remote connection transport: "direct" uses configured URL connectivity, while "ssh" tunnels through SSH. Use SSH when you need encrypted tunnel semantics without exposing remote ports.

gateway.reload.label: Config Reload
gateway.reload.help: Live config-reload policy for how edits are applied and when full restarts are triggered. Keep hybrid behavior for safest operational updates unless debugging reload internals.

gateway.tls.label: Gateway TLS
gateway.tls.help: TLS certificate and key settings for terminating HTTPS directly in the gateway process. Use explicit certificates in production and avoid plaintext exposure on untrusted networks.

gateway.tls.enabled.label: Gateway TLS Enabled
gateway.tls.enabled.help: Enables TLS termination at the gateway listener so clients connect over HTTPS/WSS directly. Keep enabled for direct internet exposure or any untrusted network boundary.

gateway.tls.autoGenerate.label: Gateway TLS Auto-Generate Cert
gateway.tls.autoGenerate.help: Auto-generates a local TLS certificate/key pair when explicit files are not configured. Use only for local/dev setups and replace with real certificates for production traffic.

gateway.tls.certPath.label: Gateway TLS Certificate Path
gateway.tls.certPath.help: Filesystem path to the TLS certificate file used by the gateway when TLS is enabled. Use managed certificate paths and keep renewal automation aligned with this location.

gateway.tls.keyPath.label: Gateway TLS Key Path
gateway.tls.keyPath.help: Filesystem path to the TLS private key file used by the gateway when TLS is enabled. Keep this key file permission-restricted and rotate per your security policy.

gateway.tls.caPath.label: Gateway TLS CA Path
gateway.tls.caPath.help: Optional CA bundle path for client verification or custom trust-chain requirements at the gateway edge. Use this when private PKI or custom certificate chains are part of deployment.

gateway.http.label: Gateway HTTP API
gateway.http.help: Gateway HTTP API configuration grouping endpoint toggles and transport-facing API exposure controls. Keep only required endpoints enabled to limit what remote callers can access.

gateway.http.endpoints.label: Gateway HTTP Endpoints
gateway.http.endpoints.help: HTTP endpoint feature toggles under the gateway API surface for compatibility routes and optional integrations. Enable endpoints intentionally and monitor access patterns after rollout.

gateway.http.securityHeaders.label: Gateway HTTP Security Headers
gateway.http.securityHeaders.help: Optional HTTP response security headers applied by the gateway process itself. Prefer setting these at your reverse proxy when TLS terminates there.

gateway.http.securityHeaders.strictTrans.label: Strict Transport Security Header
gateway.http.securityHeaders.strictTrans.help: Value for the Strict-Transport-Security response header. Set only on HTTPS origins that you fully control; use false to explicitly disable.

gateway.remote.url.label: Remote Gateway URL
gateway.remote.url.help: Remote Gateway WebSocket URL (ws:// or wss://).

gateway.remote.sshTarget.label: Remote Gateway SSH Target
gateway.remote.sshTarget.help: Remote gateway over SSH (tunnels the gateway port to localhost). Format: user@host or user@host:port.

gateway.remote.sshIdentity.label: Remote Gateway SSH Identity
gateway.remote.sshIdentity.help: Optional SSH identity file path (passed to ssh -i).

gateway.remote.sshHostKeyPolicy.label: Remote Gateway SSH Host-Key Policy
gateway.remote.sshHostKeyPolicy.help: macOS SSH host-key verification policy. "strict" requires an already trusted host key; "openssh" explicitly delegates to effective OpenSSH configuration.

gateway.remote.token.label: Remote Gateway Token
gateway.remote.token.help: Shared secret sent in the token field to authenticate this client to a remote gateway. The server's gateway.auth.mode selects its configured secret; either client token or password field is accepted. Store via secret/env substitution and rotate alongside remote gateway auth changes.

gateway.remote.password.label: Remote Gateway Password
gateway.remote.password.help: Shared secret sent in the password field to authenticate this client to a remote gateway. The server's gateway.auth.mode selects its configured secret; either client token or password field is accepted. Keep this secret managed externally and avoid plaintext values in committed config.

gateway.remote.edgeAuth.label: Remote Gateway Edge Auth Headers
gateway.remote.edgeAuth.help: Secret-backed HTTP headers presented to an identity-aware proxy in front of the configured remote Gateway. Headers are sent only to the exact gateway.remote.url origin over WSS and never follow redirects.

gateway.remote.tlsFingerprint.label: Remote Gateway TLS Fingerprint
gateway.remote.tlsFingerprint.help: Expected sha256 TLS fingerprint for the remote gateway (pin to avoid MITM).

gateway.auth.token.label: Gateway Token
gateway.auth.token.help: Shared secret selected by gateway.auth.mode=token, the default for new local onboarding. Clients may send it in either auth.token or auth.password. Non-loopback binds require an enabled authentication mode.

gateway.auth.password.label: Gateway Password
gateway.auth.password.help: Shared secret selected by gateway.auth.mode=password. Clients may send it in either auth.token or auth.password. Password mode is required for Tailscale Funnel.

tools.allow.label: Tool Allowlist
tools.allow.help: Absolute tool allowlist that replaces profile-derived defaults for strict environments. Use this only when you intentionally run a tightly curated subset of tool capabilities.

tools.deny.label: Tool Denylist
tools.deny.help: Global tool denylist that blocks listed tools even when profile or provider rules would allow them. Use deny rules for emergency lockouts and long-term defense-in-depth.

tools.web.label: Web Tools
tools.web.help: Web-tool policy grouping for search/fetch providers, limits, and fallback behavior tuning. Keep enabled settings aligned with API key availability and outbound networking policy.

tools.exec.label: Exec Tool
tools.exec.help: Exec-tool policy grouping for shell execution host, security mode, approval behavior, and runtime bindings. Keep conservative defaults in production and tighten elevated execution paths.

tools.openclaw.label: OpenClaw Delegation
tools.openclaw.help: Approval policy for persistent changes delegated to the OpenClaw system agent.

tools.openclaw.autoApproveChanges.label: Auto-approve Delegated Changes
tools.openclaw.autoApproveChanges.help: Standing authorization for permitted delegated administration, including configuration that can execute code on the Gateway host. True authorizes changes without individual approval, even when direct execution tools are denied; false always requires approval. Omitted uses explicit Full Access or independently proven unrestricted Gateway execution. Filesystem, sandbox, operation, and current-run restrictions still apply.

agents.entries.*.tools.openclaw.label: Agent OpenClaw Delegation
agents.entries.*.tools.openclaw.help: Per-agent approval policy for changes delegated to the OpenClaw system agent.

agents.entries.*.tools.openclaw.autoAppr.label: Agent Auto-approve Delegated Changes
agents.entries.*.tools.openclaw.autoAppr.help: Overrides tools.openclaw.autoApproveChanges for this agent. True is a standing delegated-administration grant that can enable Gateway-host code execution; false requires individual approval, including in Full Access. Omitted inherits the global setting, then the requesting run's effective authority. Filesystem, sandbox, and operation restrictions still apply.

tools.github.label: GitHub CLI Identity and Git Author
tools.github.help: Managed local GitHub CLI profile and optional Git author for agent tools. Omit this object to preserve the Gateway runtime user's native account and author; repository remote credentials are never overridden.

tools.github.profileId.label: GitHub Profile Version
tools.github.profileId.help: Opaque generated profile version used to switch managed credentials atomically.

tools.github.kind.label: GitHub Credential Kind
tools.github.kind.help: Marks a managed OAuth profile whose rotating refresh credential is owned by the Gateway. Omitted profiles use a personal access token.

tools.github.gitAuthor.name.label: Git Author Name
tools.github.gitAuthor.name.help: Optional process-local Git author and committer name.

tools.github.gitAuthor.email.label: Git Author Email
