tools.github.gitAuthor.email.help: Optional process-local Git author and committer email.

agents.entries.*.tools.github.label: Agent GitHub CLI Identity Override
agents.entries.*.tools.github.help: Complete managed GitHub CLI identity and Git author override for this agent. Omit it to inherit the system identity.

agents.entries.*.tools.github.allowInSan.label: Allow Agent GitHub Identity in Sandbox
agents.entries.*.tools.github.allowInSan.help: Allows this agent's managed GitHub credentials and Git author inside its own Docker or Podman sandbox (default: false). Shared scope refuses identity injection; other backends reject provisioning. Security audit warns while enabled.

tools.media.image.enabled.label: Enable Image Understanding
tools.media.image.enabled.help: Enable image understanding so attached or referenced images can be interpreted into textual context. Disable if you need text-only operation or want to avoid image-processing cost.

tools.media.image.preferredModel.label: Preferred Image Understanding Model
tools.media.image.preferredModel.help: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for image understanding before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.image.maxBytes.label: Image Understanding Max Bytes
tools.media.image.maxBytes.help: Default image input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to match provider payload limits and deployment bandwidth.

tools.media.image.maxChars.label: Image Understanding Max Chars
tools.media.image.maxChars.help: Default maximum image description length. Use a lower value for compact context or a higher value for detailed OCR and scene analysis.

tools.media.image.prompt.label: Image Understanding Prompt
tools.media.image.prompt.help: Default image-understanding prompt when an entry does not override it. Use a fixed prompt when consumers rely on stable descriptions.

tools.media.image.timeoutSeconds.label: Image Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.media.image.timeoutSeconds.help: Default timeout for image-understanding requests. Increase it for large images or slower local vision models.

tools.media.image.scope.label: Image Understanding Scope
tools.media.image.scope.help: Restrict image understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow in busy or untrusted channels to control processing.

tools.media.image.attachments.label: Image Understanding Attachment Policy
tools.media.image.attachments.help: Choose which matching image attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-image analysis is intentional.

tools.media.models.label: Media Understanding Shared Models
tools.media.models.help: Media-understanding model list. Use image, audio, or video capability tags on every entry so each pipeline selects only compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.concurrency.label: Media Understanding Concurrency
tools.media.concurrency.help: Maximum number of concurrent media understanding operations per turn across image, audio, and video tasks. Lower this in resource-constrained deployments to prevent CPU/network saturation.

tools.media.audio.enabled.label: Enable Audio Understanding
tools.media.audio.enabled.help: Enable audio understanding so voice notes or audio clips can be transcribed for agent context.

tools.media.audio.preferredModel.label: Preferred Audio Understanding Model
tools.media.audio.preferredModel.help: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for audio transcription before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.audio.maxBytes.label: Audio Understanding Max Bytes
tools.media.audio.maxBytes.help: Default audio input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to the largest recording your providers and network should accept.

tools.media.audio.maxChars.label: Audio Understanding Max Chars
tools.media.audio.maxChars.help: Default maximum transcript length for configured and auto-detected models. Use a lower value to keep long voice notes from expanding agent context.

tools.media.audio.prompt.label: Audio Understanding Prompt
tools.media.audio.prompt.help: Default audio transcription prompt when a model entry does not override it. Keep the instruction stable when downstream workflows rely on transcript style.

tools.media.audio.timeoutSeconds.label: Audio Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.media.audio.timeoutSeconds.help: Default timeout for audio understanding requests. Increase it for long recordings or slower local transcription models.

tools.media.audio.language.label: Audio Understanding Language
tools.media.audio.language.help: Default language hint for audio transcription providers. Set it when the primary spoken language is known and provider detection is unreliable.

tools.media.audio.scope.label: Audio Understanding Scope
tools.media.audio.scope.help: Restrict audio understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow where automatic transcription is sensitive or expensive.

tools.media.audio.attachments.label: Audio Understanding Attachment Policy
tools.media.audio.attachments.help: Choose which matching audio attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-attachment transcription is intentional.

tools.media.audio.echoTranscript.label: Echo Transcript to Chat
tools.media.audio.echoTranscript.help: Echo the audio transcript to the originating chat before agent processing. Enable this when users need to verify what the system heard.

tools.media.audio.echoFormat.label: Transcript Echo Format
tools.media.audio.echoFormat.help: Format the echoed transcript with a {transcript} placeholder. Keep the placeholder intact so delivery includes the transcript.

tools.media.video.enabled.label: Enable Video Understanding
tools.media.video.enabled.help: Enable video understanding so clips can be summarized into text for downstream reasoning and responses. Disable when processing video is out of policy or too expensive for your deployment.

tools.media.video.preferredModel.label: Preferred Video Understanding Model
tools.media.video.preferredModel.help: Prefer one capability-tagged tools.media.models entry for video understanding before the remaining compatible fallbacks.

tools.media.video.maxBytes.label: Video Understanding Max Bytes
tools.media.video.maxBytes.help: Default video input size limit for configured and auto-detected models. Set this to match provider payload limits and deployment bandwidth.

tools.media.video.maxChars.label: Video Understanding Max Chars
tools.media.video.maxChars.help: Default maximum video description length. Use a lower value for compact context or a higher value for detailed scene summaries.

tools.media.video.prompt.label: Video Understanding Prompt
tools.media.video.prompt.help: Default video-understanding prompt when an entry does not override it. Use a fixed prompt when consumers rely on stable summaries.

tools.media.video.timeoutSeconds.label: Video Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.media.video.timeoutSeconds.help: Default timeout for video-understanding requests. Increase it for longer clips or slower local analysis models.

tools.media.video.scope.label: Video Understanding Scope
tools.media.video.scope.help: Restrict video understanding by channel, chat type, or source key. Keep this narrow in busy or untrusted channels to control processing.

tools.media.video.attachments.label: Video Understanding Attachment Policy
tools.media.video.attachments.help: Choose which matching video attachments are processed. Use first-only handling unless multi-video analysis is intentional.

tools.links.enabled.label: Enable Link Understanding
tools.links.enabled.help: Enable automatic link understanding pre-processing so URLs can be summarized before agent reasoning. Keep enabled for richer context, and disable when strict minimal processing is required.

tools.links.maxLinks.label: Link Understanding Max Links
tools.links.maxLinks.help: Maximum number of links expanded per turn during link understanding. Use lower values to control latency/cost in chatty threads and higher values when multi-link context is critical.

tools.links.timeoutSeconds.label: Link Understanding Timeout (sec)
tools.links.timeoutSeconds.help: Per-link understanding timeout budget in seconds before unresolved links are skipped. Keep this bounded to avoid long stalls when external sites are slow or unreachable.

tools.links.models.label: Link Understanding Models
tools.links.models.help: Preferred model list for link understanding tasks, evaluated in order as fallbacks when supported. Use lightweight models first for routine summarization and heavier models only when needed.

tools.links.scope.label: Link Understanding Scope
tools.links.scope.help: Controls when link understanding runs relative to conversation context and message type. Keep scope conservative to avoid unnecessary fetches on messages where links are not actionable.

tools.profile.label: Tool Profile
tools.profile.help: Global tool profile name used to select a predefined tool policy baseline before applying allow/deny overrides. Use this for consistent environment posture across agents and keep profile names stable.

tools.alsoAllow.label: Tool Allowlist Additions
tools.alsoAllow.help: Extra tool allowlist entries merged on top of the selected tool profile and default policy. Keep this list small and explicit so audits can quickly identify intentional policy exceptions.

agents.entries.*.tools.profile.label: Agent Tool Profile
agents.entries.*.tools.profile.help: Per-agent override for tool profile selection when one agent needs a different capability baseline. Use this sparingly so policy differences across agents stay intentional and reviewable.

agents.entries.*.tools.alsoAllow.label: Agent Tool Allowlist Additions
agents.entries.*.tools.alsoAllow.help: Per-agent additive allowlist for tools on top of global and profile policy. Keep narrow to avoid accidental privilege expansion on specialized agents.

agents.entries.*.tools.codeMode.label: Agent Code Mode
agents.entries.*.tools.codeMode.help: Per-agent Code Mode options. Explicit enabled overrides the shared model and global activation defaults; an agent-specific model codeMode override wins. Other options merge over tools.codeMode without changing activation.

agents.entries.*.tools.swarm.label: Agent Swarm
agents.entries.*.tools.swarm.help: Per-agent swarm override. Values merge over the top-level tools.swarm configuration.

tools.byProvider.label: Tool Policy by Provider
tools.byProvider.help: Per-provider tool allow/deny overrides keyed by channel/provider ID to tailor capabilities by surface. Use this when one provider needs stricter controls than global tool policy. exec.mode sets a restrict-only host exec ceiling for turns on that provider or provider/model (it never drops mandatory approvals or loosens a stricter mode), so mode "auto" puts only that model's exec misses behind the exec reviewer.

agents.entries.*.tools.byProvider.label: Agent Tool Policy by Provider
agents.entries.*.tools.byProvider.help: Per-agent provider-specific tool policy overrides for channel-scoped capability control. Use this when a single agent needs tighter restrictions on one provider than others.

agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.label: Agent Cross-Context Messaging (Same Provider)
agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.help: Per-agent message guard for sending to other conversations on the same provider. Set both this and allowAcrossProviders to false for current-conversation-only public agents.

agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.label: Agent Cross-Context Messaging (Across Providers)
agents.entries.*.tools.message.crossCont.help: Per-agent override for sending across providers. Inherits the global setting (default: true). Set false to block cross-provider messaging for this agent.

agents.entries.*.tools.message.actions.a.label: Agent Message Action Allowlist
agents.entries.*.tools.message.actions.a.help: Per-agent message action allowlist for the message tool. Set to a minimal list such as ["send"] for public sandbox agents so read, edit, delete, reaction, and other provider-specific message actions stay hidden and blocked.

tools.exec.applyPatch.enabled.label: Enable apply_patch
tools.exec.applyPatch.enabled.help: Enable or disable apply_patch for OpenAI and OpenAI Codex models when allowed by tool policy (default: true).

tools.exec.applyPatch.workspaceOnly.label: apply_patch Workspace-Only
tools.exec.applyPatch.workspaceOnly.help: Restrict host apply_patch paths to the workspace directory (default: false). Set true for workspace-only access; required roots and session restrictions still apply.

tools.exec.applyPatch.allowModels.label: apply_patch Model Allowlist
tools.exec.applyPatch.allowModels.help: Optional allowlist of model ids (e.g. "gpt-5.4" or "openai/gpt-5.4").

tools.loopDetection.enabled.label: Tool Repeat Guard
tools.loopDetection.enabled.help: Controls the tool repeat guard. The guard adds a redirect note on the third identical consecutive tool call and ends the turn at the twentieth. Omit or set true to keep it on; set false to disable it.

tools.fs.workspaceOnly.label: Workspace-only FS tools
tools.fs.workspaceOnly.help: Restrict filesystem tools (read/write/edit/apply_patch) to the workspace directory (default: false).

tools.sessions.visibility.label: Session Tools Visibility
tools.sessions.visibility.help: Controls which sessions can be targeted by sessions_list/sessions_history/sessions_search/sessions_send/session_status. ("all" default = any session on the Gateway, including other agents and users; "agent" = any session in the current agent id; "self" = only current; "tree" = current session + spawned subagent sessions). Cross-agent access is on by default and scoped by tools.agentToAgent; use narrower visibility to restrict reads and ordinary sends. Explicit agents.entries.<id>.tools.agentToAgent.send destinations can permit sends without widening reads.

tools.sessions.allowThreadTargets.label: Allow Thread Send Targets
tools.sessions.allowThreadTargets.help: Allow sessions_send to target thread- or topic-scoped chat sessions such as Telegram forum topics or Slack/Discord threads (default: false). The target runs in that session; anything it sends with the message tool lands in the human-facing thread.

tools.exec.notifyOnExit.label: Exec Notify On Exit
tools.exec.notifyOnExit.help: When true (default), backgrounded exec sessions on exit and node exec lifecycle events enqueue a follow-up for the originating session.

tools.exec.notifyOnExitEmptySuccess.label: Exec Notify On Empty Success
tools.exec.notifyOnExitEmptySuccess.help: When true (default), successful backgrounded exec exits with empty output still wake the originating session, so a silent waiter reports back. Set false to keep silent successes quiet; the agent then collects them with process poll.

tools.exec.approvalRunningNoticeMs.label: Exec Approval Running Notice (ms)
tools.exec.approvalRunningNoticeMs.help: Delay in milliseconds before showing an in-progress notice after an exec approval is granted. Increase to reduce flicker for fast commands, or lower for quicker operator feedback.

tools.exec.host.label: Exec Target
tools.exec.host.help: Selects execution target strategy for shell commands. Use "auto" for runtime-aware behavior (sandbox when available, otherwise gateway), or pin sandbox/gateway/node explicitly when you need a fixed surface.

tools.exec.mode.label: Exec Mode
tools.exec.mode.help: Normalized exec policy selector. Use "auto" for classifier-reviewed approval misses, "ask" for human-reviewed misses, "allowlist" for commands approved by fixed rules, or "full" for trusted local operation.

tools.exec.reviewer.label: Exec Reviewer
tools.exec.reviewer.help: Model-backed exec reviewer used by auto mode before human approval fallback. Configure a narrow model override here when you want exec review isolated from the main agent model.

tools.exec.reviewer.model.label: Exec Reviewer Model
tools.exec.reviewer.model.help: Optional provider/model override for the exec reviewer agent. Omit to reuse the configured primary model for the target agent.

tools.exec.reviewer.thinking.label: Exec Reviewer Thinking
tools.exec.reviewer.thinking.help: Optional reasoning effort for OpenClaw model-backed approval reviews: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, or max. Omit to preserve provider defaults. Supported levels are normalized for the selected model. Does not configure native Codex Guardian.

tools.exec.reviewer.fastMode.label: Exec Reviewer Fast Mode
tools.exec.reviewer.fastMode.help: Optional Fast mode for OpenClaw approval reviews: true requests priority processing on supported OpenAI Responses and ChatGPT/OAuth routes; false requests standard processing. Omit to preserve provider defaults. Fast mode may cost more and is subject to provider availability. Does not configure native Codex Guardian.

tools.exec.reviewer.timeoutMs.label: Exec Reviewer Timeout (ms)
tools.exec.reviewer.timeoutMs.help: Per-stage exec reviewer timeout in milliseconds for model preparation and completion before falling back to human approval (default: 30000).

tools.exec.node.label: Exec Node Binding
tools.exec.node.help: Node binding configuration for exec tooling when command execution is delegated through connected nodes. Use explicit node binding only when multi-node routing is required.

tools.updatePlan.label: Enable Structured Plan Tool
tools.updatePlan.help: Unified `progress_card` status tool for durable plans and narrative notes in parent sessions. Enabled by default; set false to opt out. Always unavailable to subagents.

tools.toolSearch.label: Tool Search
tools.toolSearch.help: Compact large OpenClaw, MCP, and client tool catalogs. OpenClaw runtimes use structured Tool Search automatically when unset; engaged Code Mode takes precedence and Codex uses its native search. Set false to disable it, true for structured search, or use the object form to choose a mode.

tools.toolSearch.enabled.label: Enable Tool Search
tools.toolSearch.enabled.help: Enables Tool Search. When on, OpenClaw hides large tool catalogs behind structured search/describe/call tools during embedded runtime runs.

tools.toolSearch.mode.label: Tool Search Surface
tools.toolSearch.mode.help: Choose the model-facing surface: "tools" (default) exposes structured search/describe/call tools; "directory" keeps a bounded tool directory visible, exposes a bounded set of likely or required schemas, and defers the rest behind search/describe/call.

tools.toolSearch.include.label: Tool Search Include Selectors
tools.toolSearch.include.help: Presentation selectors for catalog-eligible, policy-approved tools. Omitted selects all eligible tools; [] selects none. Fields within a selector are ANDed; selectors are ORed. Unselected tools remain directly callable. Does not affect independent Code Mode or Codex-native search.

tools.toolSearch.include[].source.label: Included Tool Source
tools.toolSearch.include[].source.help: Tool origin: "openclaw" for core and non-MCP plugins, "mcp" for registered MCP tools, or "client" for client-supplied tools. Qualify names with a source to avoid matching lookalikes.

tools.toolSearch.include[].name.label: Included Tool Name
tools.toolSearch.include[].name.help: Registered tool name or * glob, using tool-policy normalization (including aliases). Name-only selectors match across sources. No regex support or tool-group expansion.

tools.toolSearch.exclude.label: Tool Search Exclude Selectors
tools.toolSearch.exclude.help: Tools to keep directly visible instead of cataloging. Uses the same selectors as include; exclusion wins. Omitted or [] excludes nothing. Does not grant permissions or override direct-only and runtime-required tools.

tools.toolSearch.exclude[].source.label: Excluded Tool Source
tools.toolSearch.exclude[].source.help: Origin to exclude from cataloging: "openclaw", "mcp", or "client". ANDed with name when both are present.

tools.toolSearch.exclude[].name.label: Excluded Tool Name
tools.toolSearch.exclude[].name.help: Registered tool name or * glob to keep direct, using tool-policy normalization. Name-only selectors match across sources; use source qualification to avoid unintended matches.

tools.toolSearch.searchDefaultLimit.label: Tool Search Default Results
tools.toolSearch.searchDefaultLimit.help: Default number of Tool Search results returned when the model omits a limit. Runtime clamps this to `maxSearchLimit`.

tools.toolSearch.maxSearchLimit.label: Tool Search Max Results
tools.toolSearch.maxSearchLimit.help: Maximum number of Tool Search results a model can request. Runtime clamps values to the supported 1..50 range.

tools.codeMode.label: Code Mode
tools.codeMode.help: Generic OpenClaw Code Mode. When omitted globally, defaults to `"auto"`; an authored object without `enabled` remains off. Engaged agent runs expose only `exec` and `wait` to the model and access normal tools through the catalog bridge.

tools.codeMode.enabled.label: Enable Code Mode
tools.codeMode.enabled.help: Global OpenClaw Code Mode activation. A completely absent global setting defaults to `"auto"`; an authored object without `enabled` remains off. `"auto"` engages catalog-preferred models, while `true` engages tool-capable runs. Agent and model activation overrides take precedence. An engaged run is blocked if the runtime is unavailable instead of exposing the full tool list.

tools.codeMode.executor.label: Code Mode Executor
tools.codeMode.executor.help: JavaScript executor: "node" (default) uses Node vm for trusted code and is not a security sandbox; "quickjs" uses the bundled QuickJS WASM plugin for hardened guest execution. Tool permissions apply to both. Code Mode cannot run if the selected executor is unavailable.

tools.codeMode.mode.label: Code Mode Surface
tools.codeMode.mode.help: Model-facing surface. Only "only" is supported: expose code-mode `exec` and `wait` and hide normal tools.

tools.codeMode.timeoutMs.label: Code Mode Timeout
tools.codeMode.timeoutMs.help: Maximum milliseconds for one code-mode `exec` or `wait` call.

tools.codeMode.memoryLimitBytes.label: Code Mode Memory Limit
tools.codeMode.memoryLimitBytes.help: QuickJS guest heap limit or best-effort Node worker V8 heap budget in bytes. Node runtime overhead and minimum engine allocations affect the effective budget; external buffers and process RSS are excluded. This is not a security guarantee.

tools.codeMode.maxOutputBytes.label: Code Mode Output Limit
tools.codeMode.maxOutputBytes.help: Maximum serialized bytes returned through code-mode output.

tools.codeMode.maxSnapshotBytes.label: Code Mode Snapshot Limit
tools.codeMode.maxSnapshotBytes.help: Maximum serialized bytes retained for one suspended QuickJS snapshot.

tools.codeMode.maxPendingToolCalls.label: Code Mode Pending Tool Limit
tools.codeMode.maxPendingToolCalls.help: Maximum concurrent nested tool calls a code-mode VM can start before it must resume later.

tools.codeMode.snapshotTtlSeconds.label: Code Mode Snapshot TTL
tools.codeMode.snapshotTtlSeconds.help: How long suspended Code Mode runs can be resumed with `wait` before they expire.

tools.codeMode.searchDefaultLimit.label: Code Mode Default Search Results
tools.codeMode.searchDefaultLimit.help: Default number of hidden catalog search results returned by `catalog.search` inside code mode.

tools.codeMode.maxSearchLimit.label: Code Mode Max Search Results
tools.codeMode.maxSearchLimit.help: Maximum number of hidden catalog search results a code-mode program can request.

tools.swarm.label: Swarm
tools.swarm.help: Collector-mode subagent orchestration. Enabled by default; set false to opt out. Tool permissions still apply to agents_wait and swarm spawn options.

tools.swarm.enabled.label: Enable Swarm
tools.swarm.enabled.help: Enables collector-mode subagents and agents_wait. Default is on; set false to opt out.

tools.swarm.maxConcurrent.label: Swarm Concurrent Children per Group
tools.swarm.maxConcurrent.help: Maximum running collector children in each swarm group's separate execution lane (default: 32), independent of ordinary subagent concurrency. Each running child uses one model stream and one Code Mode worker isolate. Group admission limits still apply.

tools.swarm.maxChildrenPerGroup.label: Swarm Live Children per Group
tools.swarm.maxChildrenPerGroup.help: Maximum live collector children per swarm group.

tools.swarm.maxTotalPerGroup.label: Swarm Total Children per Group
tools.swarm.maxTotalPerGroup.help: Maximum lifetime collector spawns per swarm group.

tools.swarm.waitTimeoutSecondsMax.label: Swarm Maximum Wait Timeout
tools.swarm.waitTimeoutSecondsMax.help: Maximum timeout accepted by agents_wait, in seconds.

tools.swarm.defaultAgentId.label: Swarm Default Agent
tools.swarm.defaultAgentId.help: Default target agent for swarm spawns that omit agentId. The subagent allowlist still applies.

tools.elevated.label: Elevated Tool Access
tools.elevated.help: Elevated tool access controls for privileged command surfaces that should only be reachable from trusted senders. Keep disabled unless operator workflows explicitly require elevated actions.

tools.elevated.enabled.label: Enable Elevated Tool Access
tools.elevated.enabled.help: Enables elevated tool execution path when sender and policy checks pass. Keep disabled in public/shared channels and enable only for trusted owner-operated contexts.

tools.elevated.allowFrom.label: Elevated Tool Allow Rules
tools.elevated.allowFrom.help: Sender allow rules for elevated tools, usually keyed by channel/provider identity formats. Use narrow, explicit identities so elevated commands cannot be triggered by unintended users.

tools.subagents.label: Subagent Tool Policy
tools.subagents.help: Tool policy wrapper for spawned subagents to restrict or expand tool availability compared to parent defaults. Use this to keep delegated agent capabilities scoped to task intent.

tools.subagents.tools.label: Subagent Tool Allow/Deny Policy
tools.subagents.tools.help: Allow/deny tool policy applied to spawned subagent runtimes. Keep this narrower than parent scope. Parent-owned tools such as progress_card are always denied, including through allow/alsoAllow.

tools.sandbox.label: Sandbox Tool Policy
tools.sandbox.help: Tool policy wrapper for sandboxed agent executions so sandbox runs can have distinct capability boundaries. Use this to enforce stronger safety in sandbox contexts.

tools.sandbox.tools.label: Sandbox Tool Allow/Deny Policy
tools.sandbox.tools.help: Allow/deny tool policy applied when agents run in sandboxed execution environments. Keep policies minimal so sandbox tasks cannot escalate into unnecessary external actions.

tools.exec.pathPrepend.label: Exec PATH Prepend
tools.exec.pathPrepend.help: Directories to prepend to PATH for exec runs (gateway/sandbox).

tools.exec.safeBins.label: Exec Safe Bins
tools.exec.safeBins.help: Allow stdin-only safe binaries to run without explicit allowlist entries.

tools.exec.strictInlineEval.label: Require Inline-Eval Approval
tools.exec.strictInlineEval.help: Require explicit approval for interpreter inline-eval forms such as `python -c`, `node -e`, `ruby -e`, or `osascript -e`. Prevents silent allowlist reuse and downgrades allow-always to ask-each-time for those forms.

tools.exec.commandHighlighting.label: Exec Command Highlighting
tools.exec.commandHighlighting.help: Show parser-derived command highlights in exec approval prompts (default: false). Enable this to render highlighted command text without changing exec approval policy.

tools.exec.grantExpiryDays.label: Standing Grant Expiry (Days)
tools.exec.grantExpiryDays.help: Default lifetime, in days (1-3650), for standing grants minted by allow-always on automation approvals. Unset keeps grants valid until revoked or the owning automation changes. Terms freeze at mint, so changing this affects only future grants.

tools.exec.safeBinTrustedDirs.label: Exec Safe Bin Trusted Dirs
tools.exec.safeBinTrustedDirs.help: Additional explicit directories trusted for safe-bin path checks (PATH entries are never auto-trusted).

tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.label: Exec Safe Bin Profiles
tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.help: Optional per-binary safe-bin profiles (positional limits + allowed/denied flags).

approvals.exec.label: Exec Approval Forwarding
approvals.exec.help: Groups exec-approval forwarding behavior including enablement, routing mode, filters, and explicit targets. Configure here when approval prompts must reach operational channels instead of only the origin thread.

approvals.exec.enabled.label: Forward Exec Approvals
approvals.exec.enabled.help: Enables forwarding of exec approval requests to configured delivery destinations (default: false). Keep disabled in low-risk setups and enable only when human approval responders need channel-visible prompts.

approvals.exec.mode.label: Approval Forwarding Mode
approvals.exec.mode.help: Controls where approval prompts are sent: "session" uses origin chat, "targets" uses configured targets, and "both" sends to both paths. Use "session" as baseline and expand only when operational workflow requires redundancy.

approvals.exec.agentFilter.label: Approval Agent Filter
approvals.exec.agentFilter.help: Optional allowlist of agent IDs eligible for forwarded approvals, for example `["primary", "ops-agent"]`. Use this to avoid notifying channels for unrelated agents.

approvals.exec.sessionFilter.label: Approval Session Filter
approvals.exec.sessionFilter.help: Optional session-key filters matched as substring or regex-style patterns, for example `["discord:", "^agent:ops:"]`. Use narrow patterns so only intended approval contexts are forwarded to shared destinations.

approvals.exec.targets.label: Approval Forwarding Targets
approvals.exec.targets.help: Explicit delivery targets used when forwarding mode includes targets, each with channel and destination details. Keep target lists least-privilege and validate each destination before enabling broad forwarding.

approvals.exec.targets[].channel.label: Approval Target Channel
approvals.exec.targets[].channel.help: Channel/provider ID used for forwarded approval delivery, such as discord, slack, or a plugin channel id. Use valid channel IDs only so approvals do not silently fail due to unknown routes.

approvals.exec.targets[].to.label: Approval Target Destination
approvals.exec.targets[].to.help: Destination identifier inside the target channel (channel ID, user ID, or thread root depending on provider). Verify semantics per provider because destination format differs across channel integrations.

approvals.exec.targets[].accountId.label: Approval Target Account ID
approvals.exec.targets[].accountId.help: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups when approvals must route through a specific account context. Use this only when the target channel has multiple configured identities.

approvals.exec.targets[].threadId.label: Approval Target Thread ID
approvals.exec.targets[].threadId.help: Optional thread/topic target for channels that support threaded delivery of forwarded approvals. Use this to keep approval traffic contained in operational threads instead of main channels.

approvals.plugin.label: Plugin Approval Forwarding
approvals.plugin.help: Groups plugin-approval forwarding behavior including enablement, routing mode, filters, and explicit targets. Independent of exec approval forwarding. Configure here when plugin approval prompts must reach operational channels.

approvals.plugin.enabled.label: Forward Plugin Approvals
approvals.plugin.enabled.help: Enables forwarding of plugin approval requests to configured delivery destinations (default: false). Independent of approvals.exec.enabled.

approvals.plugin.mode.label: Plugin Approval Forwarding Mode
approvals.plugin.mode.help: Controls where plugin approval prompts are sent: "session" uses origin chat, "targets" uses configured targets, and "both" sends to both paths.

approvals.plugin.agentFilter.label: Plugin Approval Agent Filter
approvals.plugin.agentFilter.help: Optional allowlist of agent IDs eligible for forwarded plugin approvals, for example `["primary", "ops-agent"]`. Use this to select which agents' approval requests are forwarded.

approvals.plugin.sessionFilter.label: Plugin Approval Session Filter
approvals.plugin.sessionFilter.help: Optional session-key filters matched as substring or regex-style patterns, for example `["discord:", "^agent:ops:"]`. Use narrow patterns so only intended approval contexts are forwarded.

approvals.plugin.targets.label: Plugin Approval Forwarding Targets
approvals.plugin.targets.help: Explicit delivery targets used when plugin approval forwarding mode includes targets, each with channel and destination details.

approvals.plugin.targets[].channel.label: Plugin Approval Target Channel
approvals.plugin.targets[].channel.help: Channel/provider ID used for forwarded plugin approval delivery, such as discord, slack, or a plugin channel id.

approvals.plugin.targets[].to.label: Plugin Approval Target Destination
approvals.plugin.targets[].to.help: Destination identifier inside the target channel (channel ID, user ID, or thread root depending on provider).

approvals.plugin.targets[].accountId.label: Plugin Approval Target Account ID
approvals.plugin.targets[].accountId.help: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups when plugin approvals must route through a specific account context.

approvals.plugin.targets[].threadId.label: Plugin Approval Target Thread ID
approvals.plugin.targets[].threadId.help: Optional thread/topic target for channels that support threaded delivery of forwarded plugin approvals.

approvals.plugin.slack.label: Slack Plugin Reviewers
approvals.plugin.slack.help: Slack reviewer policy for plugin approvals. Omit the default approvers list to retain account allowFrom/defaultTo authorization; set it to [] to deny Slack decisions by default.

approvals.plugin.slack.approvers.label: Default Slack Plugin Reviewers
approvals.plugin.slack.approvers.help: Default Slack plugin reviewers as raw U/W user IDs within the selected Slack account, or workspace-qualified team:<team-id>:user:<user-id> values. Plugin and tool lists override this list for their own requests.

approvals.plugin.slack.plugins.label: Slack Plugin Reviewer Overrides
approvals.plugin.slack.plugins.help: Reviewer overrides keyed by the selected native tool plugin ID. Tool keys encode the raw tool name.

tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinPr.label: Allow Cross-Context (Same Provider)
tools.message.crossContext.allowWithinPr.help: Allow sends to other channels within the same provider (default: true).

tools.message.crossContext.allowAcrossPr.label: Allow Cross-Context (Across Providers)
tools.message.crossContext.allowAcrossPr.help: Allow sends across different providers (default: true). Set false to block cross-provider messaging.

tools.message.crossContext.marker.enable.label: Cross-Context Marker
tools.message.crossContext.marker.enable.help: Add a visible origin marker when sending cross-context (default: true).

tools.message.actions.allow.label: Message Action Allowlist
tools.message.actions.allow.help: Global message action allowlist for the message tool. Use only when the whole runtime should expose and accept a reduced action set; prefer per-agent allowlists for public or sandboxed agents.

tools.web.search.enabled.label: Enable Web Search Tool
tools.web.search.enabled.help: Enable managed web_search and optional Codex-native search for eligible models.

tools.web.search.provider.label: Web Search Provider
tools.web.search.provider.help: Search provider id. Auto-detected from available API keys if omitted.

tools.web.search.timeoutSeconds.label: Web Search Timeout (sec)
tools.web.search.timeoutSeconds.help: Timeout in seconds for web_search requests.

tools.web.search.cacheTtlMinutes.label: Web Search Cache TTL (min)
tools.web.search.cacheTtlMinutes.help: Cache TTL in minutes for web_search results.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.enabled.label: Enable Native Codex Web Search
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.enabled.help: Enable native Codex web search for Codex-capable models.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.mode.label: Codex Web Search Mode
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.mode.help: Native Codex web search preference: "cached" (default; unrestricted Codex turns resolve it to live) or "live".

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.allowedDoma.label: Codex Allowed Domains
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.allowedDoma.help: Domain allowlist for native Codex web_search. On native-hosted-search turns, it also gates managed web_fetch; managed-provider turns are unchanged.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.contextSize.label: Codex Search Context Size
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.contextSize.help: Native Codex search context size hint: "low", "medium", or "high".

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User Country
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate country sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User Region
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate region/state sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User City
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate city sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.label: Codex User Timezone
tools.web.search.openaiCodex.userLocatio.help: Approximate timezone sent to native Codex web search.

tools.web.fetch.enabled.label: Enable Web Fetch Tool
tools.web.fetch.enabled.help: Enable the web_fetch tool (lightweight HTTP fetch).

tools.web.fetch.maxCharsCap.label: Web Fetch Hard Max Chars
tools.web.fetch.maxCharsCap.help: Hard cap for web_fetch maxChars (applies to config and tool calls).

tools.web.fetch.timeoutSeconds.label: Web Fetch Timeout (sec)
tools.web.fetch.timeoutSeconds.help: Timeout in seconds for web_fetch requests.

tools.web.fetch.cacheTtlMinutes.label: Web Fetch Cache TTL (min)
tools.web.fetch.cacheTtlMinutes.help: Cache TTL in minutes for web_fetch results.

tools.web.fetch.userAgent.label: Web Fetch User-Agent
tools.web.fetch.userAgent.help: Override User-Agent header for web_fetch requests.

tools.web.fetch.headers.label: Web Fetch Request Headers
tools.web.fetch.headers.help: Extra request headers sent with direct web_fetch requests, for example gateway routing or authentication headers. Every configured value is treated as sensitive and redacted from exposed config and debug captures. Values are plain strings, support ${VAR} substitution and the global $${VAR} literal escape, and are sent to model-chosen URLs. Entries are validated when the request is built rather than at config load, so a bad name or unsendable value is dropped and logged instead of disabling the surface; Accept, Accept-Language, User-Agent, and framing headers such as Transfer-Encoding are dropped too. Use tools.web.fetch.userAgent to change the user agent. Cross-origin redirects retain only the guarded-fetch safe header allowlist, and changing the headers actually sent partitions the fetch cache.

tools.web.fetch.readability.label: Web Fetch Readability Extraction
tools.web.fetch.readability.help: Use Readability to extract main content from HTML (fallbacks to basic HTML cleanup).

tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy.label: Web Fetch Trusted Env Proxy
tools.web.fetch.useTrustedEnvProxy.help: Route web_fetch through a trusted HTTP(S) env proxy and let the proxy resolve DNS. Enable only when that proxy is operator-controlled and enforces outbound policy after DNS resolution.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.label: Web Fetch SSRF Policy
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.help: Scoped SSRF policy overrides for web_fetch. Keep this narrow and opt in only for known local-network proxy environments.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAl.label: Web Fetch Dangerously Allow Private Network
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAl.help: Allows web_fetch access to private and internal network targets. Keep disabled unless model-selected URLs are trusted in this deployment.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostna.label: Web Fetch Allowed Hostnames
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowedHostna.help: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed for web_fetch, including otherwise blocked targets. Keep the list minimal.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostna.label: Web Fetch Blocked Hostnames
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.blockedHostna.help: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules on every web_fetch redirect. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowRfc2544B.label: Web Fetch Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowRfc2544B.help: Allow RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15) for fake-IP proxy compatibility such as Clash or Surge.

tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowIpv6Uniq.label: Web Fetch Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy.allowIpv6Uniq.help: Allow IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7) for trusted fake-IP proxy compatibility such as sing-box, Clash, or Surge.

mcp.apps.label: MCP Apps
mcp.apps.help: MCP Apps UI support. When enabled, configured MCP servers may provide interactive HTML views for their tool results.

mcp.apps.enabled.label: MCP Apps Enabled
mcp.apps.enabled.help: Opt-in MCP Apps rendering and app-to-server bridge. Keep disabled unless you trust the configured MCP servers that provide app UI resources.

mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin.label: MCP Apps Sandbox Origin
mcp.apps.sandboxOrigin.help: Optional dedicated public HTTP(S) origin for MCP Apps. Use this behind a reverse proxy or TLS terminator and proxy it only to the configured MCP Apps sandbox port. It must differ from the web app origin and must not serve authenticated content.

mcp.apps.sandboxPort.label: MCP Apps Sandbox Port
mcp.apps.sandboxPort.help: Dedicated MCP Apps sandbox listener port. Defaults to the Gateway port plus one. Set an unused port when another local service or Gateway profile already owns that port.

gateway.push.label: Gateway Push Delivery
gateway.push.help: Push-delivery settings used by the gateway when it needs to wake or notify paired devices. Configure relay-backed APNs here for official iOS builds; direct APNs auth remains env-based for local/manual builds.

gateway.push.apns.label: Gateway APNs Delivery
gateway.push.apns.help: APNs delivery settings for iOS devices paired to this gateway. Use relay settings for official App Store builds that register through the external push relay.

gateway.push.apns.relay.label: Gateway APNs Relay
gateway.push.apns.relay.help: External relay settings for relay-backed APNs sends. The gateway uses the hosted OpenClaw relay by default, or this custom relay for push.test, wake nudges, and reconnect wakes after a paired official iOS build publishes a relay-backed registration.

gateway.push.apns.relay.baseUrl.label: Gateway APNs Relay Base URL
gateway.push.apns.relay.baseUrl.help: Optional custom base HTTPS URL for the external APNs relay service used by official App Store iOS builds. Keep this aligned with the relay URL baked into the iOS build so registration and send traffic hit the same deployment.

gateway.push.apns.relay.timeoutMs.label: Gateway APNs Relay Timeout (ms)
gateway.push.apns.relay.timeoutMs.help: Timeout in milliseconds for relay send requests from the gateway to the APNs relay (default: 10000). Increase for slower relays or networks, or lower to fail wake attempts faster.

gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.label: OpenAI Chat Completions Image Limits
gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.help: Image fetch/validation controls for OpenAI-compatible `image_url` parts.

gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.label: OpenAI Chat Completions Allow Image URLs
gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.help: Allow server-side URL fetches for `image_url` parts (default: false; data URIs remain supported). Set this to `false` to disable URL fetching entirely.

gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.label: OpenAI Chat Completions Image URL Allowlist
gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.help: Optional hostname allowlist for `image_url` URL fetches; supports exact hosts and `*.example.com` wildcards. Empty or omitted lists mean no hostname allowlist restriction.

gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.label: OpenAI Chat Completions Image MIME Allowlist
gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.help: Allowed MIME types for `image_url` parts (case-insensitive list).

gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.label: OpenAI Chat Completions Image Max Bytes
OpenAI Chat Completions Image Max Redirects
gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.help: Max HTTP redirects allowed when fetching `image_url` URLs (default: 3).

gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.label: OpenAI Chat Completions Image Timeout (ms)
gateway.http.endpoints.chatCompletions.i.help: Timeout in milliseconds for `image_url` URL fetches (default: 10000).

gateway.reload.mode.label: Config Reload Mode
gateway.reload.mode.help: Controls how config edits are applied: "off" ignores live edits and "hybrid" applies hot-safe changes then restarts when required.

gateway.nodes.browser.mode.label: Gateway Node Browser Mode
gateway.nodes.browser.mode.help: Node browser routing ("auto" = prefer the host browser, use a single connected browser node when local capability is unavailable; "manual" = require an explicit node selection or configured pin; "off" = disable node routing).

gateway.nodes.browser.node.label: Gateway Node Browser Pin
gateway.nodes.browser.node.help: Pin browser routing to a specific node id or name (optional).

gateway.nodes.pairing.label: Gateway Node Pairing
gateway.nodes.pairing.help: Node pairing policy settings. SSH-verified auto-approval is enabled by default; CIDR auto-approval stays disabled unless explicit trusted CIDR/IP allowlists are configured.

gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveLocal.label: Gateway Node Pairing Auto-Approve Local
gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveLocal.help: Silently approve trusted local pairing and access upgrades (default: true); set false to trade convenience for explicit approval of every device.

gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveCidrs.label: Gateway Node Pairing Auto-Approve CIDRs
gateway.nodes.pairing.autoApproveCidrs.help: Opt-in CIDR/IP allowlist for auto-approving first-time node-role device pairing with no requested scopes. Disabled when unset. Operator, browser, web app, and any role, scope, metadata, or public-key upgrade pairing still require manual approval.

gateway.nodes.pairing.sshVerify.label: Gateway Node Pairing SSH Verification
gateway.nodes.pairing.sshVerify.help: SSH-verified auto-approval for first-time node-role device pairing (default: enabled). The gateway SSHes back to the pairing host (BatchMode, strict host keys) and approves only when the remote `openclaw node identity` output matches the pending device key. Set false to disable SSH verification (independent of autoApproveCidrs, which stays active); for manual-only pairing also unset autoApproveCidrs. Pass an object to override user/identity/timeoutMs/cidrs.

gateway.nodes.pluginTools.label: Gateway Node Plugin Tools
gateway.nodes.pluginTools.help: Controls whether paired nodes may publish agent-visible plugin tool descriptors.

gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled.label: Gateway Node Plugin Tools Enabled
gateway.nodes.pluginTools.enabled.help: Accept agent-visible plugin tool descriptors published by paired nodes (default: true). Set false to ignore and remove all node-published plugin tools.

gateway.nodes.allowSkills.label: Gateway Node Skills Enabled
gateway.nodes.allowSkills.help: Accept skills published by paired nodes while they are connected (default: true). Set false to ignore node-published skills.

gateway.nodes.commands.allow.label: Gateway Node Allowlist (Extra Commands)
gateway.nodes.commands.allow.help: Extra node.invoke commands to allow beyond the gateway defaults (array of command strings). Enabling dangerous commands here is a security-sensitive override and is flagged by `openclaw security audit`.

gateway.nodes.commands.deny.label: Gateway Node Denylist
gateway.nodes.commands.deny.help: Node command names to block even if present in node claims or default allowlist (exact command-name matching only, e.g. `system.run`; does not inspect shell text inside that command).

nodeHost.autoUpdate.label: Node Automatic Updates
nodeHost.autoUpdate.help: Controls automatic updates of the separate runtime for packaged headless node hosts. Checks hourly and waits for all node work to finish before restarting; automatic restarts are at least 12 hours apart.

nodeHost.autoUpdate.enabled.label: Node Automatic Updates Enabled
nodeHost.autoUpdate.enabled.help: Enable automatic stable or beta updates for long-running packaged headless nodes (default: true). Set false to opt out. Also disabled by update.checkOnStart=false or OPENCLAW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1; source checkouts, native apps, private workers, dev, and extended-stable do not auto-apply.

nodeHost.agentRuns.label: Node Agent Runs
nodeHost.agentRuns.help: Opt in to approval-gated native agent turns on this headless node host. Disabled by default.

nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.label: Node Claude Agent Runs
nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.help: Controls whether this headless node host may advertise Claude CLI agent turns to the gateway.

nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled.label: Node Claude Agent Runs Enabled
nodeHost.agentRuns.claude.enabled.help: Advertise paired-node Claude session continuation when the local claude binary is available (default: false). Runs still require node exec approval.

nodeHost.workerRuns.label: Node Worker Runs
nodeHost.workerRuns.help: Opt in to full OpenClaw worker session hosting from Gateway-managed bundles. Disabled by default.

nodeHost.workerRuns.enabled.label: Node Worker Runs Enabled
nodeHost.workerRuns.enabled.help: Allow this paired node to host sessions from exact bundles installed by its Gateway (default: false).

nodeHost.workerRuns.folders.label: Node Worker Session Folders
nodeHost.workerRuns.folders.help: Optional directory roots restricting in-place sessions to those roots and their subdirectories. Unset allows any existing directory except filesystem roots and private worker storage; [] disables device-folder sessions. Use absolute or ~/ paths. Existing files stay on the device; session deletion never removes these folders. Requires workerRuns.enabled.

nodeHost.workerRuns.capacity.label: Node Worker Run Capacity
nodeHost.workerRuns.capacity.help: Maximum concurrent worker sessions hosted by this node (default: the number of available CPU cores). Must be an integer from 1 through 1024.

nodeHost.workerRuns.isolation.label: Node Worker Run Isolation
nodeHost.workerRuns.isolation.help: Select the worker-session process boundary: "none" runs directly on the node host (default); "container" requires a working Docker-compatible engine and never falls back to host execution.

nodeHost.workerRuns.containerImage.label: Node Worker Run Container Image
nodeHost.workerRuns.containerImage.help: Optional Node 24.22.1+ or 26.12.1+ image for container-isolated workers (default: "node:24.22.1-slim"). Use a digest-pinned, private-registry, or preloaded image when needed; missing images are pulled on first use.

nodeHost.browserProxy.label: Node Browser Proxy
nodeHost.browserProxy.help: Groups browser-proxy settings for exposing local browser control through node routing. Enable only when remote node workflows need your local browser profiles.

nodeHost.browserProxy.enabled.label: Node Browser Proxy Enabled
nodeHost.browserProxy.enabled.help: Expose the local browser control server through node proxy routing so remote clients can use this host's browser capabilities. Keep disabled unless remote automation explicitly depends on it.

nodeHost.browserProxy.allowProfiles.label: Node Browser Proxy Allowed Profiles
nodeHost.browserProxy.allowProfiles.help: Optional allowlist of browser profile names exposed through node proxy routing. Leave empty to preserve the default full profile surface, including profile create/delete routes. When set, OpenClaw enforces least-privilege profile access and blocks persistent profile create/delete through the proxy.

nodeHost.mcp.label: Node Host MCP
nodeHost.mcp.help: Use MCP servers started by the headless node host and published to its paired gateway as agent tools. Restart the node host after changing this section.

nodeHost.mcp.servers.label: Node Host MCP Servers
nodeHost.mcp.servers.help: Named MCP server definitions local to this node. Uses the same server shape as mcp.servers; OAuth servers are not supported by the node host.

nodeHost.skills.label: Node Host Skills
nodeHost.skills.help: Use this section to publish skills installed in ~/.openclaw/skills from the headless node host. Restart the node host after changing skill files.

nodeHost.skills.enabled.label: Node Host Skills Enabled
nodeHost.skills.enabled.help: Scan and publish node-hosted skills after connecting (default: true). Set false to disable node skill publication.

attachments.label: Attachments
attachments.help: Top-level retention behavior shared across providers and tools that persist media. Use ttlHours when general staged media needs bounded cleanup.

attachments.ttlHours.label: Attachment Retention TTL (hours)
attachments.ttlHours.help: Optional retention window in hours for persisted media handled by the general mtime sweep. Leave unset to disable that sweep, or set values like 24 (1 day) or 168 (7 days) to periodically remove older staged media. Managed outgoing media (chat-generated attachments) is excluded and follows its own SQLite- and chat-aware retention.

bindings[].type.label: Binding Type
bindings[].type.help: Binding kind. Use "route" (or omit for legacy route entries) for normal routing, and "acp" for persistent ACP conversation bindings.

bindings[].agentId.label: Binding Agent ID
bindings[].agentId.help: Target agent ID that receives traffic when the corresponding binding match rule is satisfied. Use valid configured agent IDs only so routing does not fail at runtime.

bindings[].session.label: Binding Session
bindings[].session.help: Optional route session overrides for conversations matched by this binding. Use this when a narrow route should keep the same agent but isolate session continuity differently.

bindings[].session.dmScope.label: Binding Session DM Scope
bindings[].session.dmScope.help: Optional DM session scope override for this route binding. For example, keep global session.dmScope="main" while using "per-account-channel-peer" for selected direct peers.

bindings[].session.groupScope.label: Binding Session Group Scope
bindings[].session.groupScope.help: Optional group/channel session scope override for this route binding. "per-group" keeps matched rooms separate and ambiently watched by the agent main session regardless of dmScope; "main" merges their context into main and needs no watch.

bindings[].match.label: Binding Match Rule
bindings[].match.help: Match rule object for deciding when a binding applies, including channel and optional account/peer constraints. Keep rules narrow to avoid accidental agent takeover across contexts.

bindings[].match.channel.label: Binding Channel
bindings[].match.channel.help: Channel/provider identifier this binding applies to, such as `telegram`, `discord`, or a plugin channel ID. Use the configured channel key exactly so binding evaluation works reliably.

bindings[].match.accountId.label: Binding Account ID
bindings[].match.accountId.help: Optional account selector for multi-account channel setups so the binding applies only to one identity. Use this when account scoping is required for the route and leave unset otherwise.

bindings[].match.peer.label: Binding Peer Match
bindings[].match.peer.help: Optional peer matcher for specific conversations including peer kind and peer id. Use this when only one direct/group/channel target should be pinned to an agent.

bindings[].match.peer.kind.label: Binding Peer Kind
bindings[].match.peer.kind.help: Peer conversation type: "direct", "group", "channel", or legacy "dm" (deprecated alias for direct). Prefer "direct" for new configs and keep kind aligned with channel semantics.

bindings[].match.peer.id.label: Binding Peer ID
bindings[].match.peer.id.help: Conversation identifier used with peer matching, such as a chat ID, channel ID, or group ID from the provider. Keep this exact to avoid silent non-matches.

bindings[].match.guildId.label: Binding Guild ID
bindings[].match.guildId.help: Optional Discord-style guild/server ID constraint for binding evaluation in multi-server deployments. Use this when the same peer identifiers can appear across different guilds.

bindings[].match.teamId.label: Binding Team ID
bindings[].match.teamId.help: Optional team/workspace ID constraint used by providers that scope chats under teams. Add this when you need bindings isolated to one workspace context.

bindings[].match.roles.label: Binding Roles
bindings[].match.roles.help: Optional role-based filter list used by providers that attach roles to chat context. Use this to route privileged or operational role traffic to specialized agents.

bindings[].acp.label: ACP Binding Overrides
bindings[].acp.help: Optional per-binding ACP overrides for bindings[].type=acp. This layer overrides agents.entries.*.runtime.acp defaults for the matched conversation.

bindings[].acp.mode.label: ACP Binding Mode
bindings[].acp.mode.help: ACP session mode override for this binding (persistent or oneshot).

bindings[].acp.label.label: ACP Binding Label
bindings[].acp.label.help: Human-friendly label for ACP status/diagnostics in this bound conversation.

bindings[].acp.cwd.label: ACP Binding Working Directory
bindings[].acp.cwd.help: Working directory override for ACP sessions created from this binding.

bindings[].acp.backend.label: ACP Binding Backend
bindings[].acp.backend.help: ACP backend override for this binding (falls back to agent runtime ACP backend, then global acp.backend).

broadcast.strategy.label: Agent Group Strategy
broadcast.strategy.help: Participant execution order: "parallel" (default) runs agents concurrently, while "sequential" runs them in configured order. Each round completes before the next begins.

broadcast.*.label: Agent Group Participants and Options
broadcast.*.help: Use a channel-qualified peer ID (for example "telegram:-100123") to configure an array of agent IDs or a strict object with agents, mentionGating, maxRounds, and maxTurns. Qualified entries take precedence over legacy WhatsApp peer keys and allow at most 16 agents.

broadcast.*.agents.label: Agent Group Participants
broadcast.*.agents.help: Participant agent IDs from agents.entries (maximum: 16). Each participant uses its own session for this channel, account, conversation, and thread.

broadcast.*.mentionGating.label: Agent Group Mention Selection
broadcast.*.mentionGating.help: Select only explicitly @mentioned participants when any match; otherwise run all participants (default: true). Bare names or emoji do not select participants. Channel allowlists and admission rules still apply.

broadcast.*.maxRounds.label: Agent Group Maximum Rounds
broadcast.*.maxRounds.help: Maximum rounds per inbound message, including the initial round (integer: 1–4, default: 1). Follow-up rounds share bounded, attributed sibling replies and stop when every participant passes.

broadcast.*.maxTurns.label: Agent Group Maximum Turns
broadcast.*.maxTurns.help: Maximum participant turns per inbound message across all rounds (integer: 1–32, default: agents.length). Slots are reserved before parallel dispatch; this bounds agent turns, not physical message chunks or tool sends. Budgets do not resume after restart.

skills.load.extraDirs.label: Extra Skill Directories
skills.load.extraDirs.help: Additional shared skill roots to scan at lowest precedence. Use this for sibling repos or shared skill packs that should be available without copying them into the OpenClaw workspace.

skills.load.allowSymlinkTargets.label: Allowed Skill Symlink Targets
skills.load.allowSymlinkTargets.help: Trusted real target roots that skill symlinks may resolve into when they sit outside their configured source root. Keep this narrow, such as a sibling repo skills directory.

skills.load.watch.label: Watch Skills
skills.load.watch.help: Enable filesystem-triggered skill discovery with a safety rescan every 30 minutes for missed events. Disabling this leaves explicit OpenClaw skill changes, relevant configuration changes, and Gateway startup refreshing skills immediately. Existing sessions use changed snapshots on their next agent turn.

agents.defaults.skills.label: Skills
agents.defaults.skills.help: Optional default skill allowlist inherited by agents that omit agents.entries.*.skills. Omit for unrestricted skills, set [] to give inheriting agents no skills, and remember explicit agents.entries.*.skills replaces this default instead of merging with it.

agents.defaults.subagents.delegationMode.label: Sub-agent Delegation Mode
agents.defaults.subagents.delegationMode.help: Prompt-only sub-agent delegation strength. Defaults to "prefer" in each agent's main session and "suggest" elsewhere; "prefer" strongly instructs the agent to delegate non-trivial work via sessions_spawn.

agents.entries.*.subagents.delegationMod.label: Sub-agent Delegation Mode
agents.entries.*.subagents.delegationMod.help: Per-agent override for sub-agent delegation strength. Omit to use "prefer" in this agent's main session and "suggest" elsewhere; explicit "prefer" or "suggest" always wins.

agents.defaults.workspace.label: Workspace
agents.defaults.workspace.help: Default agent workspace for bootstrap and memory files. Also used as the working directory when agents.defaults.cwd is unset. Set this explicitly when running from wrappers so path resolution stays consistent.

agents.defaults.workspaceFileMode.label: New Memory File Mode
agents.defaults.workspaceFileMode.help: New memory-core DREAMS.md, MEMORY.md, and memory/dreaming report permissions: "0600", "0620", "0640", or "0660". Unset keeps exact 0600; configured modes respect the writing host's umask. Existing files, daily memory, session corpus, and private state are unchanged. Directory traversal and default ACLs must be provisioned separately.

agents.entries.*.workspaceFileMode.label: New Memory File Mode
agents.entries.*.workspaceFileMode.help: Overrides agents.defaults.workspaceFileMode for this agent's newly created human-readable memory outputs. Existing file permissions are preserved; the writing host applies its own umask.

agents.defaults.cwd.label: Working Directory
agents.defaults.cwd.help: Working directory for agent reply runs, separate from workspace bootstrap and memory files. Agent-specific cwd and session-spawned cwd take precedence. Supports ~ and relative paths; a distinct cwd requires an unsandboxed run.

agents.defaults.repoRoot.label: Repo Root
agents.defaults.repoRoot.help: Optional repository root shown in the system prompt runtime line (overrides auto-detect).

agents.defaults.skipBootstrap.label: Skip Workspace Bootstrap Creation
agents.defaults.skipBootstrap.help: Skips automatic creation of workspace bootstrap files, not injection of existing files. For the embedded runtime, set agents.defaults.contextInjection to "never" to disable injection unless overridden per agent.

agents.defaults.skipOptionalBootstrapFil.label: Skipped Optional Bootstrap Files
agents.defaults.skipOptionalBootstrapFil.help: Optional bootstrap files that should not be created in agent workspaces. Valid values: SOUL.md, USER.md, IDENTITY.md (HEARTBEAT.md is accepted but a no-op).

agents.defaults.contextInjection.label: Context Injection
agents.defaults.contextInjection.help: Controls workspace bootstrap-file injection in the embedded runtime: "always" uses normal injection (default), "continuation-skip" skips eligible continuation turns after a recorded full-bootstrap turn, and "never" disables injection. Does not control CLI-backed prompt preparation.

agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars.label: Bootstrap Max Chars
agents.defaults.bootstrapMaxChars.help: Max characters of each workspace bootstrap file injected into the system prompt before truncation (default: 20000).

agents.defaults.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.label: Bootstrap Total Max Chars
agents.defaults.bootstrapTotalMaxChars.help: Max total characters across all injected workspace bootstrap files (default: 60000).

agents.defaults.experimental.label: Experimental Agent Flags
agents.defaults.experimental.help: Experimental agent-default flags. Keep these off unless you are intentionally testing a preview surface.

agents.defaults.experimental.localModelL.label: Enable Lean Local Model Mode (Experimental)
agents.defaults.experimental.localModelL.help: Advanced troubleshooting override that restricts optional tools such as browser, automations, and message. Off by default; supported local runtimes use automatic Tool Search without this restriction. Explicit tool allows and required delivery tools are preserved.

agents.defaults.startupContext.label: Startup Context
agents.defaults.startupContext.help: Runtime-owned first-turn prelude for bare "/new" and "/reset". Use this to control whether recent daily memory files are preloaded into the first prompt instead of asking the model to decide what to read.

agents.defaults.startupContext.enabled.label: Enable Startup Context
agents.defaults.startupContext.enabled.help: Enable the startup-context prelude for bare session resets (default: true). Disable this to fall back to prompt-only behavior with no runtime-loaded daily memory.

agents.defaults.startupContext.applyOn.label: Startup Context Apply On
agents.defaults.startupContext.applyOn.help: Chooses which bare reset commands get startup context: include "new", "reset", or both (default: ["new","reset"]).

agents.defaults.startupContext.dailyMemo.label: Startup Context Daily Memory Days
agents.defaults.startupContext.dailyMemo.help: Number of dated memory files to load counting backward from today in the configured user timezone (default: 2 for today + yesterday).

agents.defaults.startupContext.maxFileBy.label: Startup Context Max File Bytes
agents.defaults.startupContext.maxFileBy.help: Maximum bytes allowed per daily memory file when building startup context (default: 16384). Files over this boundary-safe read limit are skipped.

agents.defaults.startupContext.maxFileCh.label: Startup Context Max File Chars
agents.defaults.startupContext.maxFileCh.help: Maximum characters retained from each loaded daily memory file in the startup prelude (default: 1200).

agents.defaults.startupContext.maxTotalC.label: Startup Context Max Total Chars
agents.defaults.startupContext.maxTotalC.help: Maximum total characters retained across all loaded daily memory files in the startup prelude (default: 2800). Additional files are truncated from the prelude once this cap is reached.

memory.search.label: Memory Search
memory.search.help: Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

memory.search.enabled.label: Enable Memory Search
memory.search.enabled.help: Master toggle for memory search indexing and retrieval behavior on this agent profile. Keep enabled for semantic recall, and disable when you want fully stateless responses.

memory.search.rememberAcrossConversation.label: Remember Across Conversations
memory.search.rememberAcrossConversation.help: Use relevant context from this agent's other private conversations through protected chat recall. Defaults on only when global session.dmScope is unset or "main" and no binding overrides DM scope; any configured DM isolation defaults it off. An explicit true or false always wins.

memory.search.sources.label: Memory Search Sources
memory.search.sources.help: Chooses which sources are indexed: "memory" reads MEMORY.md + memory files, and "sessions" includes chat history. Keep ["memory"] unless you need recall from prior chats.

memory.search.extraPaths.label: Extra Memory Paths
memory.search.extraPaths.help: Adds extra directories or .md files to the memory index beyond default memory files. Entries may be path strings or objects with a root-relative glob pattern. When multimodal memory is enabled, matching image/audio files under these paths are also eligible for indexing.

memory.search.extraPaths.*.path.label: Extra Memory Path
memory.search.extraPaths.*.path.help: Sets the extra memory directory or file. Relative paths resolve from the agent workspace; direct file entries are indexed exactly.

memory.search.extraPaths.*.pattern.label: Extra Memory Path Pattern
memory.search.extraPaths.*.pattern.help: Limits a directory entry to supported files matching this root-relative glob, for example "runbooks/**/*.md". Omit it to scan all supported files recursively.

memory.search.extraPaths.*.evergreen.label: Evergreen Extra Memory Path
memory.search.extraPaths.*.evergreen.help: Keeps matching extra-path reference files out of filesystem-mtime temporal decay. This changes recency ranking only; it does not make the content trusted, promote it, or change source provenance.

memory.search.multimodal.label: Memory Search Multimodal
memory.search.multimodal.help: Optional multimodal memory settings for indexing image and audio files from configured extra paths. Keep this off unless your embedding model explicitly supports cross-modal embeddings, and set `memory.search.fallback` to "none" while it is enabled. Matching files are uploaded to the configured remote embedding provider during indexing.

memory.search.multimodal.enabled.label: Enable Memory Search Multimodal
memory.search.multimodal.enabled.help: Enables image/audio memory indexing from extraPaths. This currently requires Gemini embedding-2, keeps the default memory roots Markdown-only, disables memory-search fallback providers, and uploads matching binary content to the configured remote embedding provider.

memory.search.multimodal.modalities.label: Memory Search Multimodal Modalities
memory.search.multimodal.modalities.help: Selects which multimodal file types are indexed from extraPaths: "image", "audio", or "all". Keep this narrow to avoid indexing large binary corpora unintentionally.

memory.search.multimodal.maxFileBytes.label: Memory Search Multimodal Max File Bytes
memory.search.multimodal.maxFileBytes.help: Sets the maximum bytes allowed per multimodal file before it is skipped during memory indexing. Use this to cap upload cost and indexing latency, or raise it for short high-quality audio clips.

memory.search.experimental.sessionMemory.label: Memory Search Session Index (Experimental)
memory.search.experimental.sessionMemory.help: Indexes chat history into memory search. Keep this advanced override when root and per-agent recall inheritance differ.

memory.search.provider.label: Memory Search Provider
memory.search.provider.help: Selects the embedding backend used to build/query memory vectors. Defaults to "openai"; set "openai-compatible", "gemini", "voyage", "mistral", "bedrock", "deepinfra", "github-copilot", "lmstudio", "ollama", or "local" when you want a different backend.

memory.search.remote.baseUrl.label: Remote Embedding Base URL
memory.search.remote.baseUrl.help: Overrides the embedding API endpoint, such as an OpenAI-compatible proxy or custom Gemini base URL. Use this only when routing through your own gateway or vendor endpoint; keep provider defaults otherwise.

memory.search.remote.apiKey.label: Remote Embedding API Key
memory.search.remote.apiKey.help: Supplies a dedicated API key for remote embedding calls used by memory indexing and query-time embeddings. Use this when memory embeddings should use different credentials than global defaults or environment variables.

memory.search.remote.headers.label: Remote Embedding Headers
memory.search.remote.headers.help: Adds custom HTTP headers to remote embedding requests, merged with provider defaults. Use this for proxy auth and tenant routing headers, and keep values minimal to avoid leaking sensitive metadata.

memory.search.remote.batch.enabled.label: Remote Batch Embedding Enabled
memory.search.remote.batch.enabled.help: Enables provider batch APIs for embedding jobs when supported (OpenAI/Gemini), improving throughput on larger index runs. Keep this enabled unless debugging provider batch failures or running very small workloads.

memory.search.model.label: Memory Search Model
memory.search.model.help: Embedding model override used by the selected memory provider when a non-default model is required. Set this only when you need explicit recall quality/cost tuning beyond provider defaults.

memory.search.inputFormat.label: Memory Search Input Format
memory.search.inputFormat.help: Optional paired literal text prefixes for embedding queries and documents, such as { query: "query: ", document: "passage: " }. Replaces automatic model formatting, including for model aliases. Both strings are required; spaces and newlines are preserved, and empty strings select raw text. A non-empty queryInstruction takes precedence for queries. Changing the document prefix requires a reindex.

memory.search.inputFormat.query.label: Memory Search Query Prefix
memory.search.inputFormat.query.help: Literal prefix for query embeddings. Used unless a non-empty queryInstruction is set; an empty string disables automatic query formatting.

memory.search.inputFormat.document.label: Memory Search Document Prefix
memory.search.inputFormat.document.help: Literal prefix for document embeddings. An empty string selects raw document text. Changing this prefix changes index and embedding-cache identity and requires a reindex.

memory.search.inputType.label: Memory Search Input Type
memory.search.inputType.help: Use this optional provider-specific `input_type` value only when the same label should apply to both query and document embedding requests. For asymmetric providers, prefer queryInputType and documentInputType.

memory.search.queryInputType.label: Memory Search Query Input Type
memory.search.queryInputType.help: Optional provider-specific `input_type` value for query-time memory embeddings. Use this with OpenAI-compatible asymmetric embedding endpoints that require a query label.

memory.search.queryInstruction.label: Memory Search Query Instruction
memory.search.queryInstruction.help: Optional literal prefix for query embeddings, such as "search_query: ". Include required spaces or newlines. Non-empty values replace inputFormat.query and automatic query formatting; unset or empty values use inputFormat.query when set, otherwise provider defaults. Documents and index identity are unchanged, so no reindex is needed. An empty per-agent override clears the inherited instruction.

memory.search.documentInputType.label: Memory Search Document Input Type
memory.search.documentInputType.help: Optional provider-specific `input_type` value for document and indexing memory embeddings. Use this with OpenAI-compatible asymmetric embedding endpoints that require a passage or document label.

memory.search.outputDimensionality.label: Memory Search Output Dimensionality
memory.search.outputDimensionality.help: Provider-specific output vector size override for memory embeddings. Gemini models support 128-3072 dimensions and recommend 768, 1536, or 3072; Bedrock families such as Titan V2, Cohere V4, and Nova expose their own allowed sizes. OpenAI-compatible endpoints receive it as `dimensions` and must return vectors of exactly that size. Managed local GGUF embeddings truncate and normalize locally. Expect a full reindex when you change it because stored vector dimensions must stay consistent.

memory.search.fallback.label: Memory Search Fallback
memory.search.fallback.help: Backup provider used when primary embeddings fail: "openai", "gemini", "voyage", "mistral", "bedrock", "lmstudio", "ollama", "local", or "none". Set a real fallback for production reliability; use "none" only if you prefer explicit failures.

memory.search.local.modelPath.label: Local Embedding Model Path
memory.search.local.modelPath.help: Specifies the local embedding model source for local memory search, such as a GGUF file path or `hf:` URI. Use this only when provider is `local`, and verify model compatibility before large index rebuilds.

memory.search.store.vector.enabled.label: Memory Search Vector Index
memory.search.store.vector.enabled.help: Controls the sqlite-vec semantic index. Keep this advanced override when root and per-agent vector policies differ.

memory.search.store.vector.extensionPath.label: Memory Search Vector Extension Path
memory.search.store.vector.extensionPath.help: Overrides the auto-discovered sqlite-vec extension library path (`.dylib`, `.so`, or `.dll`). Use this when your runtime cannot find sqlite-vec automatically or you pin a known-good build.

memory.search.query.maxResults.label: Memory Search Max Results
memory.search.query.maxResults.help: Maximum number of memory hits returned from search before downstream reranking and prompt injection. Raise for broader recall, or lower for tighter prompts and faster responses.

memory.search.query.minScore.label: Memory Search Min Score
memory.search.query.minScore.help: Minimum relevance score threshold for including memory results in final recall output. Increase to reduce weak/noisy matches, or lower when you need more permissive retrieval.

memory.search.cache.enabled.label: Memory Search Embedding Cache
memory.search.cache.enabled.help: Caches computed chunk embeddings in SQLite so reindexing and incremental updates run faster (default: true). Keep this enabled unless investigating cache correctness or minimizing disk usage.

memory.citations.label: Memory Citations Mode
memory.citations.help: Controls citation visibility in replies: "auto" shows citations when useful, "on" always shows them, and "off" hides them. Keep "auto" for a balanced signal-to-noise default.

auth.profiles.label: Auth Profiles
auth.profiles.help: Named auth profiles (provider + mode + optional email).

auth.order.label: Auth Profile Order
auth.order.help: Ordered auth profile IDs per provider (used for automatic failover).

acp.enabled.label: ACP Enabled
acp.enabled.help: Global ACP feature gate. Keep disabled unless ACP runtime + policy are configured.

acp.dispatch.enabled.label: ACP Dispatch Enabled
acp.dispatch.enabled.help: Independent dispatch gate for ACP session turns (default: true). Set false to keep ACP commands available while blocking ACP turn execution.

acp.backend.label: ACP Backend
acp.backend.help: Default ACP runtime backend id (for example: acpx). Must match a registered ACP runtime plugin backend.

acp.fallbacks.label: ACP Fallback Backends
acp.fallbacks.help: Ordered list of fallback ACP backend ids tried when the primary backend fails with UNAVAILABLE (for example: rate-limit / quota exhausted). Each entry must match a registered ACP runtime plugin backend.

acp.defaultAgent.label: ACP Default Agent
acp.defaultAgent.help: Fallback ACP target agent id used when ACP spawns do not specify an explicit target.

acp.allowedAgents.label: ACP Allowed Agents
acp.allowedAgents.help: Allowlist of ACP target agent ids permitted for ACP runtime sessions. Empty means no additional allowlist restriction.

acp.stream.label: ACP Stream
acp.stream.help: ACP streaming projection controls for chunk sizing, metadata visibility, and deduped delivery behavior.

acp.stream.repeatSuppression.label: ACP Stream Repeat Suppression
