acp.stream.repeatSuppression.help: When true (default), suppress repeated ACP status/tool projection lines in a turn while keeping raw ACP events unchanged.

acp.stream.deliveryMode.label: ACP Stream Delivery Mode
acp.stream.deliveryMode.help: ACP delivery style: live streams projected output incrementally, final_only buffers all projected ACP output until terminal turn events.

acp.stream.tagVisibility.label: ACP Stream Tag Visibility
acp.stream.tagVisibility.help: Per-sessionUpdate visibility overrides for ACP projection (for example usage_update, available_commands_update).

acp.runtime.installCommand.label: ACP Runtime Install Command
acp.runtime.installCommand.help: Optional operator install/setup command shown by `/acp install` and `/acp doctor` when ACP backend wiring is missing.

models.mode.label: Model Catalog Mode
models.mode.help: Controls provider catalog behavior: "merge" keeps built-ins and overlays your custom providers, while "replace" uses only your configured providers. In "merge", matching provider IDs preserve non-empty agent models.json baseUrl values, while apiKey values are preserved only when the provider is not SecretRef-managed in current config/auth-profile context; SecretRef-managed providers refresh apiKey from current source markers, and matching model contextWindow/maxTokens use the higher value between explicit and implicit entries.

models.usage.cacheTtlMs.label: Provider Usage Cache TTL (ms)
models.usage.cacheTtlMs.help: Reuse provider usage snapshots for this many milliseconds (default: 60000). Applies to ordinary and post-run reads; 0 disables reuse. Does not enable idle polling.

models.catalogRefresh.label: Model Catalog Refresh
models.catalogRefresh.help: Controls background updates to the bundled model catalog. Remote rows can update model metadata but cannot change provider endpoints or headers.

models.catalogRefresh.enabled.label: Model Catalog Refresh Enabled
models.catalogRefresh.enabled.help: Fetch hosted model catalog updates in the background (default: true). Set to false to disable all remote model catalog traffic.

models.catalogRefresh.url.label: Model Catalog Refresh URL
models.catalogRefresh.url.help: Override the hosted model catalog URL for a self-hosted HTTPS mirror (localhost HTTP is allowed for testing). A running Gateway stops using the previous source's catalog and adopts the mirror's at its next catalog check, without restarting.

models.providers.label: Model Providers
models.providers.help: Model endpoint configurations keyed by provider ID. Choose a new ID, such as gpu-a or my-lab, for an independent custom endpoint. Built-in and extension-owned IDs and aliases retain their integration semantics; configuring one overlays that integration. The ID does not select the wire protocol: api does. Multiple custom IDs may use the same adapter with different base URLs, credentials, and models. Use a distinct ID for an independent server rather than repurposing openai merely because it is OpenAI-compatible. Custom entries must include baseUrl and models.

models.providers.*.name.label: Model Provider Display Name
models.providers.*.name.help: Optional display name shown in provider settings and model pickers. Does not change the provider ID, model references, credentials, or routing.

models.providers.*.icon.label: Model Provider Icon
models.providers.*.icon.help: Optional provider artwork: a local file, public HTTPS image URL, or bundled icon. PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF sources are limited to 2 MiB and 4096 pixels per side and served as a sanitized static PNG. Relative file paths resolve from the active configuration file directory. Invalid artwork falls back to the provider brand or display-name initial.

models.providers.*.icon.source.label: Model Provider Icon Source
models.providers.*.icon.source.help: Artwork source: file for a Gateway-local image, url for a public HTTPS image, or builtin for an icon bundled with the web app.

models.providers.*.icon.path.label: Model Provider Icon File
models.providers.*.icon.path.help: Gateway-local PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF path. Relative paths resolve from the directory containing the active configuration file; ~/ expands to the Gateway user's home directory. Only this configured image is exposed through the scoped provider asset route.

models.providers.*.icon.url.label: Model Provider Icon URL
models.providers.*.icon.url.help: Public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF URL without embedded credentials or a fragment. The Gateway fetches and sanitizes the image with private-network and redirect protections; the browser never contacts this URL directly.

models.providers.*.icon.name.label: Model Provider Bundled Icon
models.providers.*.icon.name.help: Bundled web app icon name, such as server. An unknown name falls back to the provider's built-in brand or display-name initial.

models.providers.*.baseUrl.label: Model Provider Base URL
models.providers.*.baseUrl.help: Base URL for the provider endpoint used to serve model requests for that provider entry. Use HTTPS endpoints and keep URLs environment-specific through config templating where needed.

models.providers.*.apiKey.label: Model Provider API Key
models.providers.*.apiKey.help: Provider credential used for API-key based authentication when the provider requires direct key auth. Use secret/env substitution and avoid storing real keys in committed config files.

models.providers.*.auth.label: Model Provider Auth Mode
models.providers.*.auth.help: Selects provider auth style: "api-key" for API key auth, "token" for bearer token auth, "oauth" for OAuth credentials, "aws-sdk" for AWS credential resolution, and "none" for custom openai-completions endpoints that do not enforce auth. Explicit "none" skips credentials and sends no Authorization header; other effective adapters are rejected. "native-command" delegates credentials to an explicitly configured Codex runtime for a custom HTTPS Responses provider; it cannot be combined with API keys, profiles, or request overrides.

models.providers.*.api.label: Model Provider API Adapter
models.providers.*.api.help: Wire protocol adapter, independent of the provider ID. Chat Completions: openai-completions; Responses: openai-responses; Messages: anthropic-messages. Choose other adapters from the allowed values to match your upstream protocol.

models.providers.*.maxTokens.label: Model Provider Max Tokens
models.providers.*.maxTokens.help: Default maximum output token budget applied to models under this provider when a model entry does not set maxTokens.

models.providers.*.timeoutSeconds.label: Model Provider Request Timeout
models.providers.*.timeoutSeconds.help: Optional per-provider model request timeout in seconds. Provider-level request settings affect explicit provider-owned model rows; they do not create implicit models. For custom providers, set it alongside the provider baseUrl and models. Applies to provider HTTP fetches, including connect, headers, body, and total request abort handling, and also raises the LLM idle/stream watchdog ceiling for this provider above the implicit ~120s default. Use this for slow local or self-hosted model servers, or for cloud providers that buffer reasoning tokens silently on the wire (Gemini preview, large-tool-payload Claude/Opus), instead of changing global agent timeouts.

models.providers.*.region.label: Model Provider Region
models.providers.*.region.help: Optional provider deployment/API region interpreted by providers that expose regional endpoints. Use provider docs for supported values; baseUrl overrides usually take precedence when both are set.

models.providers.*.injectNumCtxForOpenAI.label: Model Provider Inject num_ctx (OpenAI Compat)
models.providers.*.injectNumCtxForOpenAI.help: Controls whether OpenClaw injects `options.num_ctx` for Ollama providers configured with the OpenAI-compatible adapter (`openai-completions`). Default is true. Set false only if your proxy/upstream rejects unknown `options` payload fields.

models.providers.*.params.label: Model Provider Runtime Parameters
models.providers.*.params.help: Provider-specific runtime parameters interpreted by provider plugins. Keep keys documented by the provider, and prefer explicit provider docs over ad hoc shared assumptions.

models.providers.*.headers.label: Model Provider Headers
models.providers.*.headers.help: Static HTTP headers merged into provider requests for tenant routing, proxy auth, or custom gateway requirements. Use this sparingly and keep sensitive header values in secrets.

models.providers.*.authHeader.label: Model Provider Authorization Header
models.providers.*.authHeader.help: When true, credentials are sent via the HTTP Authorization header even if alternate auth is possible. Use this only when your provider or proxy explicitly requires Authorization forwarding.

models.providers.*.agentRuntime.label: Model Provider Runtime
models.providers.*.agentRuntime.help: Optional low-level agent runtime policy for this provider. Use provider/model runtime policy instead of agent-wide runtime pins; omitted/default lets OpenClaw choose the runtime for the selected provider.

models.providers.*.agentRuntime.id.label: Model Provider Runtime ID
models.providers.*.agentRuntime.id.help: Provider agent runtime id: "openclaw", "auto", a registered plugin harness id such as "codex", or a supported CLI backend alias such as "claude-cli". OpenAI on the official endpoint defaults to the Codex harness when omitted.

models.providers.*.localService.label: Model Provider Local Service
models.providers.*.localService.help: Optional on-demand local model server process for this provider. OpenClaw checks healthUrl, starts the command when needed, waits for readiness, and then sends the model request.

models.providers.*.remote.label: Model Provider Hosted Watchdog Timing
models.providers.*.remote.help: Watchdog-only hosted timing override for local relays in front of hosted APIs. When true, the LLM idle and first-event watchdogs use hosted timing even with a local baseUrl, provider ID, localService, or local auth marker. Absent or false preserves locality detection. Explicit timeoutSeconds and run or agent budgets keep their precedence.

models.providers.*.localService.command.label: Model Provider Local Service Command
models.providers.*.localService.command.help: Absolute executable path for the local model server process. Keep this path explicit so provider startup is predictable and does not depend on shell PATH lookup.

models.providers.*.localService.args.label: Model Provider Local Service Arguments
models.providers.*.localService.args.help: Argument list passed to the local model server command without shell expansion.

models.providers.*.localService.cwd.label: Model Provider Local Service Working Directory
models.providers.*.localService.cwd.help: Working directory for the local model server process.

models.providers.*.localService.env.label: Model Provider Local Service Environment
models.providers.*.localService.env.help: Additional environment variables for the local model server process. Values that look secret are redacted from config snapshots.

models.providers.*.localService.healthUr.label: Model Provider Local Service Health URL
models.providers.*.localService.healthUr.help: Readiness URL checked before model requests. If omitted, OpenClaw uses the provider baseUrl with /models appended.

models.providers.*.localService.readyTim.label: Model Provider Local Service Ready Timeout
models.providers.*.localService.readyTim.help: Maximum milliseconds to wait for the local model server readiness check after starting the process.

models.providers.*.localService.idleStop.label: Model Provider Local Service Idle Stop
models.providers.*.localService.idleStop.help: Milliseconds to keep an OpenClaw-started local model server alive after the last request finishes. Set 0 to keep it alive until OpenClaw exits.

models.providers.*.request.label: Model Provider Request Overrides
models.providers.*.request.help: Optional request overrides for model-provider requests, including extra headers, auth overrides, proxy routing, TLS client settings, and optional allowPrivateNetwork for trusted self-hosted endpoints. Use these only when your upstream or enterprise network path requires transport customization.

models.providers.*.request.headers.label: Model Provider Request Headers
models.providers.*.request.headers.help: Extra headers merged into provider requests after default attribution and auth resolution.

models.providers.*.request.auth.label: Model Provider Request Auth Override
models.providers.*.request.auth.help: Override provider request authentication behavior for this provider.

models.providers.*.request.auth.token.label: Model Provider Request Bearer Token
models.providers.*.request.auth.token.help: Bearer token used when auth mode is authorization-bearer.

models.providers.*.request.auth.headerNa.label: Model Provider Request Auth Header Name
models.providers.*.request.auth.headerNa.help: Custom auth header name used when auth mode is header.

models.providers.*.request.auth.value.label: Model Provider Request Auth Header Value
models.providers.*.request.auth.value.help: Custom auth header value used when auth mode is header.

models.providers.*.request.auth.prefix.label: Model Provider Request Auth Header Prefix
models.providers.*.request.auth.prefix.help: Optional prefix prepended to request.auth.value when auth mode is header.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.label: Model Provider Request Proxy
models.providers.*.request.proxy.help: Optional proxy override for model-provider requests. Use "env-proxy" to honor environment proxy settings or "explicit-proxy" to route through a specific proxy URL.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.mode.label: Model Provider Request Proxy Mode
models.providers.*.request.proxy.mode.help: Proxy override mode for model-provider requests: "env-proxy" or "explicit-proxy".

models.providers.*.request.proxy.url.label: Model Provider Request Proxy URL
models.providers.*.request.proxy.url.help: Explicit proxy URL used when request.proxy.mode is explicit-proxy. Credentials embedded in the URL are treated as sensitive and redacted from snapshots.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.label: Model Provider Request Proxy TLS
models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.help: Optional TLS settings used when connecting to the configured proxy.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.ca.label: Model Provider Request Proxy TLS CA
models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.ca.help: Custom CA bundle used to verify the proxy TLS certificate chain.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.cer.label: Model Provider Request Proxy TLS Cert
models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.cer.help: Client TLS certificate presented to the proxy when mutual TLS is required.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.key.label: Model Provider Request Proxy TLS Key
models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.key.help: Private key paired with request.proxy.tls.cert for proxy mutual TLS.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.pas.label: Model Provider Request Proxy TLS Passphrase
models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.pas.help: Optional passphrase used to decrypt request.proxy.tls.key.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.ser.label: Model Provider Request Proxy TLS Server Name
models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.ser.help: Optional SNI/server-name override used when establishing TLS to the proxy.

models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.ins.label: Model Provider Request Proxy TLS Skip Verify
models.providers.*.request.proxy.tls.ins.help: Skips proxy TLS certificate verification. Use only for controlled development environments.

models.providers.*.request.tls.label: Model Provider Request TLS
models.providers.*.request.tls.help: Optional TLS settings used when connecting directly to the upstream model endpoint.

models.providers.*.request.tls.ca.label: Model Provider Request TLS CA
models.providers.*.request.tls.ca.help: Custom CA bundle used to verify the upstream TLS certificate chain.

models.providers.*.request.tls.cert.label: Model Provider Request TLS Cert
models.providers.*.request.tls.cert.help: Client TLS certificate presented to the upstream endpoint when mutual TLS is required.

models.providers.*.request.tls.key.label: Model Provider Request TLS Key
models.providers.*.request.tls.key.help: Private key paired with request.tls.cert for upstream mutual TLS.

models.providers.*.request.tls.passphras.label: Model Provider Request TLS Passphrase
models.providers.*.request.tls.passphras.help: Optional passphrase used to decrypt request.tls.key.

models.providers.*.request.tls.serverNam.label: Model Provider Request TLS Server Name
models.providers.*.request.tls.serverNam.help: Optional SNI/server-name override used when establishing upstream TLS.

models.providers.*.request.tls.insecureS.label: Model Provider Request TLS Skip Verify
models.providers.*.request.tls.insecureS.help: Skips upstream TLS certificate verification. Use only for controlled development environments.

models.providers.*.request.allowPrivateN.label: Model Provider Request Allow Private Network
models.providers.*.request.allowPrivateN.help: When true, allow model-provider HTTP requests to private, CGNAT, or similar ranges through the provider HTTP fetch guard (fetchWithSsrFGuard). Custom/local provider base URLs already trust the exact configured origin, except metadata, link-local, and local-use NAT64 (64:ff9b:1::/48) origins; set this to false to opt out of that trust. OpenAI Responses WebSocket reuses request for headers/TLS but does not use that fetch SSRF path. Use true only for operator-controlled self-hosted endpoints that must reach private origins outside the configured baseUrl origin.

models.providers.*.models.label: Model Provider Model List
models.providers.*.models.help: Declared model list for a provider including identifiers, metadata, provider-specific params, and optional compatibility/cost hints. Keep IDs exact to provider catalog values so selection and fallback resolve correctly.

models.providers.*.models[].agentRuntime.label: Model Runtime
models.providers.*.models[].agentRuntime.help: Optional low-level agent runtime policy for this specific model. Model runtime policy overrides the provider runtime policy.

models.providers.*.models[].agentRuntime.label: Model Runtime ID
models.providers.*.models[].agentRuntime.help: Model agent runtime id: "openclaw", "auto", a registered plugin harness id such as "codex", or a supported CLI backend alias such as "claude-cli".

models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.label: Model Media Input
models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.help: Optional model media capability metadata used by tools to choose conservative image compression defaults.

models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.label: Model Image Input
models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.help: Optional image input limits for this model, such as maximum side length, maximum pixels, and preferred compression side.

models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.label: Model Image Max Bytes
models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.help: Maximum encoded image payload size accepted by the provider for this model.

models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.label: Model Image Max Pixels
models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.help: Maximum image pixel count accepted by the provider for this model.

models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.label: Model Image Max Side
models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.help: Maximum image width or height accepted by the provider for this model.

models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.label: Model Image Preferred Side
models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.help: Preferred image resize side for balanced compression. Leave unset to use OpenClaw's conservative default.

models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.label: Model Image Token Mode
models.providers.*.models[].mediaInput.i.help: Provider image token accounting style: "tile", "detail", or "provider".

proxy.enabled.label: Managed Proxy Enabled
proxy.enabled.help: Explicit managed-proxy override. URL presence enables routing by default; set false to ignore configured or environment proxy URLs without deleting them.

proxy.proxyUrl.label: Managed Proxy URL
proxy.proxyUrl.help: Managed forward proxy URL. Use http:// for a plain CONNECT proxy or https:// when the connection to the proxy endpoint itself must use TLS.

proxy.tls.label: Managed Proxy TLS
proxy.tls.help: TLS settings used when connecting to the managed proxy endpoint. These settings apply to proxy TLS, not destination TLS after CONNECT.

proxy.tls.caFile.label: Managed Proxy TLS CA File
proxy.tls.caFile.help: Filesystem path to a custom CA bundle used to verify an HTTPS managed proxy endpoint certificate.

proxy.loopbackMode.label: Managed Proxy Loopback Mode
proxy.loopbackMode.help: Controls Gateway loopback control-plane routing while managed proxy mode is active: "gateway-only", "proxy", or "block".

agents.entries.*.models.label: Agent Model Overrides
agents.entries.*.models.help: Per-agent model catalog overrides keyed by full provider/model IDs.

agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.label: Agent Model Policy
agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.help: Per-agent model override policy. An explicit allow list replaces the default policy for this agent.

agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.allow.label: Allowed Agent Models
agents.entries.*.modelPolicy.allow.help: Allowed model override refs for this agent. Accepts aliases, full "provider/model" refs, and trailing prefix wildcards such as "provider/*", "provider/namespace/*" or "provider/family-*"; empty permits any model.

agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.label: Agent Model Runtime
agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.help: Optional per-model runtime policy for this agent. Use this for agent-specific model exceptions instead of setting a whole-agent runtime.

agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.i.label: Agent Model Runtime ID
agents.entries.*.models.*.agentRuntime.i.help: Per-agent model runtime id: "openclaw", "auto", a registered plugin harness id such as "codex", or a supported CLI backend alias such as "claude-cli".

agents.entries.*.nativeRuntimeConsent.label: Remembered native runtime permissions
agents.entries.*.nativeRuntimeConsent.help: Harness IDs allowed to use their native permissions for this agent. New chats use Full access with sandbox off. Remove an ID to revoke remembered consent immediately; explicit per-chat consent is unchanged. Required sandbox and workspace boundaries still apply.

agents.entries.*.models.*.codeMode.label: Code Mode
agents.entries.*.models.*.codeMode.help: OpenClaw Code Mode for this agent and exact provider/model: On forces it on, Off disables it, and Default inherits the agent activation setting, then the shared model override, then tools.codeMode.enabled. This does not change the selected runtime or Codex native Code Mode.

agents.defaults.models.label: Models
agents.defaults.models.help: Configured model catalog and per-model settings. Entries provide aliases, params, runtime metadata, and Code Mode overrides; they do not restrict model overrides.

agents.defaults.modelSelectionScope.label: Model Selection Scope
agents.defaults.modelSelectionScope.help: Scope for chat commands and Gateway session model updates without an explicit scope: "session" (default) changes only the current session, "agent" also updates that agent's primary, and "global" also updates the shared agents.defaults.model fallback. Explicit scope flags take precedence; configured-default writes require owner/admin authority. Telegram callback pickers and the embedded local TUI stay session-only.

agents.defaults.modelPolicy.label: Model Policy
agents.defaults.modelPolicy.help: Explicit policy for model overrides. Omit it or leave allow empty to permit any model.

agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow.label: Allowed Models
agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow.help: Allowed model override refs. Accepts aliases, full "provider/model" refs, and trailing prefix wildcards such as "openai/*", "clawrouter/anthropic/*" or "openai/gpt-*". Empty permits any model.

agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.label: Default Agent Model Runtime
agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.help: Optional per-model runtime policy for the default agent. Use this for model-specific runtime exceptions instead of setting a whole-agent runtime.

agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id.label: Default Agent Model Runtime ID
agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id.help: Default-agent model runtime id: "openclaw", "auto", a registered plugin harness id such as "codex", or a supported CLI backend alias such as "claude-cli".

agents.defaults.models.*.codeMode.label: Code Mode
agents.defaults.models.*.codeMode.help: OpenClaw Code Mode for this exact provider/model: On forces it on, Off disables it, and Default inherits tools.codeMode.enabled. Agent-specific activation settings take precedence. This does not change the selected runtime or Codex native Code Mode.

agents.defaults.model.fallbacks.label: Model Fallbacks
agents.defaults.model.fallbacks.help: Ordered fallback models (provider/model). Used when the primary model fails.

agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.cyberFailo.label: Cyber Policy Failover
agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.cyberFailo.help: Automatic same-model Daybreak escalation for replay-safe OpenAI cyber-policy refusals in the embedded runtime, subject to existing access and policy checks.

agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.cyberFailo.label: Cyber Policy Failover Mode
agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.cyberFailo.help: Enable automatic escalation ("auto", default) or keep provider refusals terminal ("off").

agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.cyberFailo.label: Cyber Policy Failover Cooloff
agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.cyberFailo.help: How long unavailable Daybreak access for the active model is skipped for the current session.

agents.defaults.utilityModel.label: Utility Model
agents.defaults.utilityModel.help: Optional lower-cost model (provider/model, alias, or { primary, fallbacks }) for short internal tasks such as generated titles and progress narration. Utility fallbacks use the same retry, alias resolution, and model-selection policy as configured model fallbacks, independently of model.fallbacks. Unset derives the primary provider's declared small model when available (otherwise the primary model); set to an empty string to disable utility routing.

agents.defaults.utilityModel.fallbacks.label: Utility Model Fallbacks
agents.defaults.utilityModel.fallbacks.help: Ordered utility fallback models (provider/model or alias), independent of the main model fallback list.

agents.entries.*.utilityModel.label: Agent Utility Model
agents.entries.*.utilityModel.help: Per-agent utility model string or { primary, fallbacks }. Unset inherits agents.defaults.utilityModel. An explicit primary without fallbacks clears inherited fallbacks; an empty string disables utility routing.

agents.entries.*.utilityModel.primary.label: Agent Primary Utility Model
agents.entries.*.utilityModel.primary.help: Per-agent utility primary. Omit to inherit the default utility primary.

agents.entries.*.utilityModel.fallbacks.label: Agent Utility Model Fallbacks
agents.entries.*.utilityModel.fallbacks.help: Ordered per-agent utility fallback models. An empty list clears inherited utility fallbacks.

agents.defaults.decisionModel.label: Decision Model
agents.defaults.decisionModel.help: Optional provider/model for typed choices, scores, and boolean probabilities. Unset or empty disables decision calls. Supporting plugins send bounded task evidence to this provider; chat and utility models are unchanged.

agents.defaults.experimental.decisionAss.label: Decision Assistance (Experimental)
agents.defaults.experimental.decisionAss.help: Global opt-in for experimental assistance from the owning agent’s configured Decision model (default: false; requires explicit true). The effective decisionModel can be inherited from global defaults or selected per agent; an empty per-agent value disables assistance. Supported uses may send selected data to that provider and incur provider charges. See the Decision assistance documentation for supported uses, setup, and data handling. This setting does not gate explicit decision_evaluate calls, select providers, or grant actions.

agents.defaults.experimental.usageRanked.label: Usage-ranked Tool Index (Experimental)
agents.defaults.experimental.usageRanked.help: Opt in to usage-ranked Code Mode, Tool Search, and MCP tool directory prompt indexes in the embedded OpenClaw runtime (default: false). Stores only tool IDs, decayed scores, and timestamps in operator-owned agent storage for 90 days; excludes incognito sessions. Rankings stay frozen until a prompt-prefix boundary. Does not change tool permissions or Codex. Inspect, import past usage, or reset with openclaw tools usage.

agents.entries.*.decisionModel.label: Agent Decision Model
agents.entries.*.decisionModel.help: Per-agent decision model. Unset inherits agents.defaults.decisionModel; an empty string disables decision calls for this agent.

agents.defaults.imageModel.primary.label: Image Model
agents.defaults.imageModel.primary.help: Optional image model (provider/model) used when the primary model lacks image input.

agents.defaults.mediaModels.image.primar.label: Image Generation Model
agents.defaults.mediaModels.image.primar.help: Optional image-generation model (provider/model) used by the shared image generation capability.

agents.defaults.mediaModels.image.timeou.label: Image Generation Timeout (ms)
agents.defaults.mediaModels.image.timeou.help: Default provider request timeout in milliseconds for image_generate calls. Per-call timeoutMs overrides this.

agents.defaults.mediaModels.video.primar.label: Video Generation Model
agents.defaults.mediaModels.video.primar.help: Optional video-generation model (provider/model) used by the shared video generation capability.

agents.defaults.mediaModels.video.timeou.label: Video Generation Timeout (ms)
agents.defaults.mediaModels.video.timeou.help: Default provider request timeout in milliseconds for video_generate calls. Per-call timeoutMs overrides this, and this value overrides provider-authored defaults.

agents.defaults.mediaModels.music.primar.label: Music Generation Model
agents.defaults.mediaModels.music.primar.help: Optional music-generation model (provider/model) used by the shared music generation capability.

agents.defaults.voiceModel.primary.label: Voice Model
agents.defaults.voiceModel.primary.help: Optional voice model (provider/model) used by speech, transcription, and realtime voice capabilities.

agents.defaults.voiceModel.timeoutMs.label: Voice Timeout (ms)
agents.defaults.voiceModel.timeoutMs.help: Default provider request timeout in milliseconds for voice model operations when the caller supports timeouts.

agents.defaults.pdfModel.primary.label: PDF Model
agents.defaults.pdfModel.primary.help: Optional PDF model (provider/model) for the PDF analysis tool. Defaults to imageModel, then session model.

agents.defaults.pdfMaxMb.label: PDF Max Size (MB)
agents.defaults.pdfMaxMb.help: Maximum PDF file size in megabytes for the PDF tool (default: 10).

agents.defaults.pdfMaxPages.label: PDF Max Pages
agents.defaults.pdfMaxPages.help: Maximum number of PDF pages to process for the PDF tool (default: 20).

agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx.label: Image Max Dimension (px)
agents.defaults.imageMaxDimensionPx.help: Max image side length in pixels when sanitizing chat and tool-result image payloads (default: 1200).

agents.defaults.imageQuality.label: Image Quality
agents.defaults.imageQuality.help: Image-tool media compression preference: "auto" adapts to provider/model limits and image count, "efficient" saves tokens and bytes, "balanced" keeps the current middle ground, and "high" preserves more detail for screenshots and document images.

agents.defaults.humanDelay.minMs.label: Human Delay Min (ms)
agents.defaults.humanDelay.minMs.help: Minimum delay in ms for custom humanDelay (default: 800).

agents.defaults.humanDelay.maxMs.label: Human Delay Max (ms)
agents.defaults.humanDelay.maxMs.help: Maximum delay in ms for custom humanDelay (default: 2500).

agents.defaults.typingMode.label: Typing Mode
agents.defaults.typingMode.help: Controls when typing starts for agents: "never", "instant", "thinking", or "message". Per-agent typingMode overrides this default.

agents.defaults.typingIntervalSeconds.label: Typing Interval (Seconds)
agents.defaults.typingIntervalSeconds.help: Controls typing-indicator keepalive cadence in seconds for every agent. Increase it to reduce update frequency across all typing-capable channels.

agents.entries.*.typingMode.label: Agent Typing Mode
agents.entries.*.typingMode.help: Overrides the default typing start policy for one agent without changing other agents.

agents.entries.*.sandbox.browser.network.label: Agent Sandbox Browser Network
agents.entries.*.sandbox.browser.network.help: Per-agent override for the sandbox browser Docker network. Use a bridge network; "none" is unsupported because browser control requires published CDP ports.

agents.entries.*.sandbox.browser.cdpSour.label: Agent Sandbox Browser CDP Source Range
agents.entries.*.sandbox.browser.cdpSour.help: Per-agent override for CDP source CIDR allowlist.

agents.entries.*.sandbox.docker.dangerou.label: Agent Sandbox Docker Allow Container Namespace Join
agents.entries.*.sandbox.docker.dangerou.help: Per-agent DANGEROUS override for container namespace joins in sandbox Docker network mode.

agents.entries.*.sandbox.docker.gpus.label: Agent Sandbox Docker GPUs
agents.entries.*.sandbox.docker.gpus.help: Per-agent Docker GPU passthrough override for sandbox containers.

agents.defaults.compaction.label: Compaction
agents.defaults.compaction.help: Compaction behavior for when context nears token limits, including strategy and pre-compaction memory flush behavior. Use this when long-running sessions need stable continuity under tight context windows.

agents.defaults.compaction.enabled.label: Embedded Auto-Compaction
agents.defaults.compaction.enabled.help: Enable embedded proactive auto-compaction (default: true). Set false to stop threshold-driven embedded compaction while preserving OpenClaw overflow recovery, preflight compaction, and manual /compact.

agents.defaults.compaction.mode.label: Compaction Mode
agents.defaults.compaction.mode.help: Compaction strategy mode: "safeguard" (the effective default when unset) applies guardrails to preserve recent context, while "default" uses baseline summarization without them. Set "default" only if safeguard summarization causes problems for your provider.

agents.defaults.compaction.provider.label: Compaction Provider
agents.defaults.compaction.provider.help: Id of a registered compaction provider plugin used for summarization. When set and the provider is registered, its summarize() method is called instead of the built-in summary request. Falls back to built-in on provider failure. Leave unset to use the default built-in summarization.

agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel.label: Compaction Thinking Level
agents.defaults.compaction.thinkingLevel.help: Thinking level used only for embedded OpenClaw compaction summaries: "off", "minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "adaptive", "max", "ultra", or "inherit". Defaults to the provider compaction preference, otherwise "low"; native local Ollama prefers "off". Set "inherit" to reuse the session level. Explicit settings override provider defaults, and the selected level is clamped to the actual compaction model/runtime. Native Codex app-server compaction ignores this setting because its compact request has no per-operation thinking override, and OpenClaw logs a warning.

agents.defaults.compaction.keepRecentTok.label: Compaction Keep Recent Tokens
agents.defaults.compaction.keepRecentTok.help: Minimum token budget preserved from the most recent conversation window during compaction. Use higher values to protect immediate context continuity and lower values to keep more long-tail history.

agents.defaults.compaction.maxSummaryCha.label: Compaction Summary Max Characters
agents.defaults.compaction.maxSummaryCha.help: Maximum characters in a persisted client-side compaction summary (default: 16000; range: 1000–200000). Larger summaries retain more generated context but increase replay cost on later requests. The active model token budget can require a smaller summary. Does not control provider-native compaction.

agents.entries.*.compaction.label: Agent Compaction
agents.entries.*.compaction.help: Per-agent client-side compaction overrides. Omitted settings inherit agents.defaults.compaction.

agents.entries.*.compaction.maxSummaryCh.label: Agent Compaction Summary Max Characters
agents.entries.*.compaction.maxSummaryCh.help: Per-agent persisted client-side summary character ceiling (1000–200000), overriding agents.defaults.compaction.maxSummaryChars. The active model token budget may require a smaller summary.

agents.defaults.compaction.identifierPol.label: Compaction Identifier Policy
agents.defaults.compaction.identifierPol.help: Identifier-preservation policy for compaction summaries: "strict" prepends built-in opaque-identifier retention guidance (default), while "off" disables this prefix.

agents.defaults.compaction.recentTurnsPr.label: Compaction Preserve Recent Turns
agents.defaults.compaction.recentTurnsPr.help: Number of most recent user/assistant turns kept verbatim outside safeguard summarization (default: 3). Raise this to preserve exact recent dialogue context, or lower it to maximize compaction savings.

agents.defaults.compaction.qualityGuard.label: Compaction Quality Guard
agents.defaults.compaction.qualityGuard.help: Quality-audit retry settings for safeguard compaction summaries. Safeguard mode enables this by default; set enabled: false to skip summary audits and regeneration.

agents.defaults.compaction.qualityGuard..label: Compaction Quality Guard Enabled
agents.defaults.compaction.qualityGuard..help: Enables summary quality audits and regeneration retries for safeguard compaction. Default: true in safeguard mode.

agents.defaults.compaction.qualityGuard..label: Compaction Quality Guard Max Retries
agents.defaults.compaction.qualityGuard..help: Maximum number of regeneration retries after a failed safeguard summary quality audit. Use small values to bound extra latency and token cost.

agents.defaults.compaction.midTurnPreche.label: Compaction Mid-turn Precheck
agents.defaults.compaction.midTurnPreche.help: Optional estimated-pressure threshold between tool rounds using the compaction reserve. Provider-measured threshold maintenance and hard context-window admission run independently, reusing safe truncation or compaction recovery.

agents.defaults.compaction.midTurnPreche.label: Compaction Mid-turn Precheck Enabled
agents.defaults.compaction.midTurnPreche.help: Enable the optional estimated-pressure threshold between tool rounds. Default: false. Measured threshold maintenance and the hard context-window check remain active when this is disabled.

agents.defaults.compaction.postIndexSync.label: Compaction Post-Index Sync
agents.defaults.compaction.postIndexSync.help: Controls post-compaction session memory reindex mode: "off", "async", or "await" (default: "async"). Use "await" for strongest freshness, "async" for lower compaction latency, and "off" only when session-memory sync is handled elsewhere.

agents.defaults.compaction.postCompactio.label: Post-Compaction Context Sections
agents.defaults.compaction.postCompactio.help: Opt-in AGENTS.md H2/H3 section names re-injected after compaction. Leave unset or set [] to disable reinjection. Explicitly set ["Session Startup", "Red Lines"] to enable the legacy default pair.

agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSecond.label: Compaction Timeout (Seconds)
agents.defaults.compaction.timeoutSecond.help: Seconds a built-in compaction model request may go without progress (default: 180). Each request start and each streamed output token refreshes the window, so a slow request that keeps streaming is not cut off; the complete compaction stops after 10 windows. Plugin-owned compaction receives one window unless the engine explicitly declares onProgress in info.acceptedHostParams and reports progress; the same 10-window ceiling applies.

agents.defaults.compaction.model.label: Compaction Model Override
agents.defaults.compaction.model.help: Optional provider/model or configured bare alias used only for compaction summarization. Bare aliases resolve before dispatch; a configured literal model ID wins if it collides with an alias. Leave unset to keep using the primary agent model.

agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTran.label: Compaction Active Chat Size Threshold
agents.defaults.compaction.maxActiveTran.help: Byte threshold for preflight local compaction in the built-in runtime (bytes or strings like "20mb"). For Codex app-server, bounds fresh-thread history seeds instead: one host summary attempt only when unsummarized history would be omitted, never on ordinary turns or after native /compact. Set to 0 or leave unset to disable. Native rollout-size and token fuses are unchanged.

agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser.label: Compaction Notify User
agents.defaults.compaction.notifyUser.help: When enabled, sends brief context-maintenance notices to the user: when compaction starts and completes (for example, '🧹 Compacting context...' and '🧹 Compaction complete'), and when a pre-compaction memory flush is exhausted so the reply continues in a degraded state (for example, '⚠️ Memory maintenance temporarily failed; continuing your reply.'). Disabled by default to keep context maintenance silent and non-intrusive.

agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.label: Compaction Memory Flush
agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.help: Pre-compaction memory flush settings that run an agentic memory write with the active session model and its normal fallback chain before heavy compaction. Keep enabled for long sessions so salient context is persisted before aggressive trimming.

agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.e.label: Compaction Memory Flush Enabled
agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.e.help: Enables pre-compaction memory flush before the runtime performs stronger history reduction near token limits. Keep enabled unless you intentionally disable memory side effects in constrained environments.

agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.s.label: Compaction Memory Flush Soft Threshold
agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.s.help: Threshold distance to compaction (in tokens) that triggers pre-compaction memory flush execution. Use earlier thresholds for safer persistence, or tighter thresholds for lower flush frequency.

agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.f.label: Compaction Memory Flush Chat Size Threshold
agents.defaults.compaction.memoryFlush.f.help: Forces pre-compaction memory flush when the model-visible chat history reaches this threshold (bytes or strings like "2mb"). After compaction, this includes the retained tail and subsequent turns rather than discarded history. Use this to prevent long-session hangs even when token counters are stale; set to 0 to disable.

agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.label: Embedded OpenClaw
agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.help: Embedded OpenClaw runner hardening controls for how workspace-local agent settings are trusted and applied in OpenClaw sessions.

agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.projectSet.label: Embedded OpenClaw Project Settings Policy
agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.projectSet.help: How embedded OpenClaw handles workspace-local `.openclaw/settings.json`: "sanitize" (default) strips shellPath/shellCommandPrefix, "ignore" disables project settings entirely, and "trusted" applies project settings as-is.

agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.executionC.label: Embedded OpenClaw Execution Contract
agents.defaults.embeddedAgent.executionC.help: Embedded OpenClaw execution contract: "default" keeps the standard runner behavior, while "strict-agentic" enables structured plan tracking and non-visible turn recovery for supported OpenAI/OpenAI Codex GPT-5-family runs.

agents.entries.*.embeddedAgent.label: Agent Embedded OpenClaw
agents.entries.*.embeddedAgent.help: Optional per-agent embedded OpenClaw overrides. Use this to opt specific agents into stricter GPT-5 execution behavior without changing the global default.

agents.entries.*.embeddedAgent.execution.label: Agent Embedded OpenClaw Execution Contract
agents.entries.*.embeddedAgent.execution.help: Optional per-agent embedded OpenClaw execution contract override. Set "strict-agentic" to enable structured plan tracking and non-visible turn recovery for that agent on supported OpenAI/OpenAI Codex GPT-5-family runs, or "default" to inherit the standard runner behavior.

agents.defaults.systemAgent.label: System Agent Target
agents.defaults.systemAgent.help: Target settings for ambient OpenClaw system-agent and Custodian inference plus selected unscoped operator reads.

agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId.label: System Agent Owner
agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId.help: Agent whose model and credentials own ambient system-agent and Custodian consults. Also used when models.list, models.authStatus, skills.status, doctor.memory.status, or an infer CLI command that resolves agent-owned model or auth state omits agentId or --agent; explicit request agentId always wins.

agents.defaults.authInheritance.label: Auth Inheritance Target
agents.defaults.authInheritance.help: Upgrade compatibility owner for the inherited credential store until credentials are relocated per agent.

agents.defaults.authInheritance.agentId.label: Auth Inheritance Owner
agents.defaults.authInheritance.agentId.help: Agent whose legacy credential store remains the inheritance source after default-marker retirement. Written automatically during upgrade when the former owner was not main.

agents.defaults.sessionStore.label: Legacy Session Store Target
agents.defaults.sessionStore.help: Upgrade compatibility owner for retired main-agent rows and fixed legacy session stores.

agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId.label: Legacy Session Store Owner
agents.defaults.sessionStore.agentId.help: Agent that owns retired main-agent rows or unscoped rows in a fixed legacy session store after default-marker retirement. Written automatically during upgrade when the former owner was not main or the sole agent.

agents.defaults.sandbox.browser.network.label: Sandbox Browser Network
agents.defaults.sandbox.browser.network.help: Docker network for sandbox browser containers (default: openclaw-sandbox-browser). Use the dedicated default or a custom bridge network; "none" is unsupported because browser control requires published CDP ports.

agents.defaults.sandbox.browser.cdpSourc.label: Sandbox Browser CDP Source Port Range
agents.defaults.sandbox.browser.cdpSourc.help: Optional CIDR allowlist for container-edge CDP ingress (for example 172.21.0.1/32).

agents.defaults.sandbox.docker.dangerous.label: Sandbox Docker Allow Container Namespace Join
agents.defaults.sandbox.docker.dangerous.help: DANGEROUS break-glass override that allows sandbox Docker network mode container:<id>. This joins another container namespace and weakens sandbox isolation.

agents.defaults.sandbox.docker.gpus.label: Sandbox Docker GPUs
agents.defaults.sandbox.docker.gpus.help: Optional Docker GPU passthrough value passed to --gpus, for example "all" or "device=GPU-uuid". Requires a compatible host runtime such as NVIDIA Container Toolkit.

commands.native.label: Native Commands
commands.native.help: Registers native slash/menu commands with channels that support command registration (Discord, Slack, Telegram). Keep enabled for discoverability unless you intentionally run text-only command workflows.

commands.nativeSkills.label: Native Skill Commands
commands.nativeSkills.help: Registers native skill commands so users can invoke skills directly from provider command menus where supported. Keep aligned with your skill policy so exposed commands match what operators expect.

commands.text.label: Text Commands
commands.text.help: Enables text-command parsing in chat input in addition to native command surfaces where available. Keep this enabled for compatibility across channels that do not support native command registration.

commands.bash.label: Allow Bash Chat Command
commands.bash.help: Allow bash chat command (`!`; `/bash` alias) to run host shell commands (default: false; requires tools.elevated).

commands.bashForegroundMs.label: Bash Foreground Window (ms)
commands.bashForegroundMs.help: How long bash waits before backgrounding (default: 2000; 0 backgrounds immediately).

commands.config.label: Allow /config
commands.config.help: Allow /config chat command to read/write config on disk (default: false).

commands.mcp.label: Allow /mcp
commands.mcp.help: Allow /mcp chat command to manage OpenClaw MCP server config under mcp.servers (default: false).

commands.plugins.label: Allow /plugins
commands.plugins.help: Allow /plugins chat command to list discovered plugins and toggle plugin enablement in config (default: false).

commands.debug.label: Allow /debug
commands.debug.help: Allow /debug chat command for runtime-only overrides (default: false).

commands.restart.label: Allow Restart
commands.restart.help: Allow /restart, /update, and external SIGUSR2 restart requests (default: true).

commands.ownerAllowFrom.label: Command Owners
commands.ownerAllowFrom.help: Explicit owner allowlist for owner-scoped commands. Use channel-native IDs (optionally prefixed like "whatsapp:+15551234567"). '*' is ignored.

commands.allowFrom.label: Command Elevated Access Rules
commands.allowFrom.help: Defines elevated command allow rules by channel and sender for owner-level command surfaces. Use narrow provider-specific identities so privileged commands are not exposed to broad chat audiences.

mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs.label: MCP Session Idle TTL (ms)
mcp.sessionIdleTtlMs.help: Optional idle eviction for OpenClaw session MCP runtimes in milliseconds. Unset or 0 keeps runtimes alive until session cleanup or Gateway shutdown. Positive values round down; active leases and pending acquisitions prevent eviction. Run-owned runtimes still retire when their one-shot run ends.

mcp.servers.label: MCP Servers
mcp.servers.help: Named MCP server definitions. OpenClaw stores them in its own config and runtime adapters decide which transports are supported at execution time.

mcp.servers.*.oauth.identity.label: MCP OAuth Identity
mcp.servers.*.oauth.identity.help: OAuth credential ownership for this server. Omit this field or use "shared" for operator-managed credentials; use "per-requester" to let each authenticated sender connect their own account.

mcp.servers.*.oauth.authProfileId.label: MCP OAuth Auth Profile
mcp.servers.*.oauth.authProfileId.help: Refresh-capable auth profile id used to inject the current bearer token into this remote MCP server. When set, OpenClaw resolves and refreshes the profile at runtime and does not project refresh material downstream.

mcp.servers.*.codex.label: Codex MCP Projection
mcp.servers.*.codex.help: OpenClaw projection metadata for Codex app-server threads only. It does not affect ACP sessions or generic Codex harness config. Omit this block to keep the server available to every Codex app-server agent with Codex's default MCP approval behavior.

mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.label: MCP Tool Selection
mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.help: Per-server MCP tool selection. Use include to expose only selected MCP tool names, or exclude to hide selected MCP tool names. Entries accept exact names and simple '*' globs.

mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.include.label: Included MCP Tools
mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.include.help: Exact MCP tool names or simple '*' globs to expose from this server. When omitted, all server tools remain eligible unless excluded.

mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.exclude.label: Excluded MCP Tools
mcp.servers.*.toolFilter.exclude.help: Exact MCP tool names or simple '*' globs to hide from this server.

mcp.servers.*.codex.agents.label: Codex MCP Agents
mcp.servers.*.codex.agents.help: Optional non-empty OpenClaw agent ids that should receive this MCP server in Codex app-server thread config. Lists with no valid agent IDs grant no access; when omitted, the server is projected for all Codex app-server agents.

mcp.servers.*.codex.defaultToolsApproval.label: Codex MCP Tool Approval
mcp.servers.*.codex.defaultToolsApproval.help: Optional Codex MCP tool approval mode for this server: "auto", "prompt", or "approve". Use only for MCP servers you intentionally trust.

mcp.servers.*.codex.default_tools_approv.label: Codex MCP Tool Approval
mcp.servers.*.codex.default_tools_approv.help: Codex-native spelling for the same per-server MCP tool approval mode. Prefer defaultToolsApprovalMode in OpenClaw config.

ui.seamColor.label: Accent Color
ui.seamColor.help: Primary accent color used by UI surfaces for emphasis, badges, and visual identity cues. Use high-contrast values that remain readable across light/dark themes.

ui.prefs.accent.label: User Accent Color
ui.prefs.accent.help: Web app accent: #RRGGBB for a custom color, or 'theme' for the selected theme’s palette. Overrides ui.seamColor; clear it to inherit the configured accent color or theme default.

ui.prefs.locale.label: Interface language
ui.prefs.locale.help: Language for the web app, as a supported locale id such as en, de, or zh-CN. Leave unset to follow the browser or system language. Set it from Settings → Appearance → Language. It does not set the assistant's timezone (agents.defaults.userTimezone).

tui.label: Terminal UI
tui.help: Terminal UI display settings. Use this section for terminal-only presentation preferences without changing Gateway or other UI behavior.

tui.footer.label: Terminal UI Footer
tui.footer.help: Terminal UI footer display settings. Keep optional context compact so session, model, goal, and token information stay readable.

agents.entries.*.subagents.delegateTools.label: Delegated Tool Targets
agents.entries.*.subagents.delegateTools.help: Exact configured native target agents that may omit this requester agent’s tools.deny at spawn. Requires allowAgents independently. Deny-only handoffs preserve all nonlocal restrictions; restrictive initial profiles/allowlists or unsupported transports refuse the handoff instead of widening them. Same-target native helpers preserve their own additional ceilings. Sender-restricted and ACP requests never use this grant. Revocation restores the original requester snapshot.

agents.entries.*.tools.agentToAgent.label: Agent Outbound Messaging
agents.entries.*.tools.agentToAgent.help: Outbound-only agent messaging policy. Explicit send destinations do not grant session reads or status access, and remain bounded by global agent-to-agent participation and sandbox restrictions.

agents.entries.*.tools.agentToAgent.send.label: Agent Send Destination Allowlist
agents.entries.*.tools.agentToAgent.send.help: Agent ids or * patterns this agent may contact with sessions_send, even with narrow tools.sessions.visibility. Omitted inherits visibility; [] denies ordinary cross-agent sends. Global tools.agentToAgent and sandbox limits still apply. Does not grant list, history, search, status, or watch access; replies belong only to the sent turn. Requester-owned child session access is unchanged.

tools.agentToAgent.label: Agent-to-Agent Tool Access
tools.agentToAgent.help: Policy for cross-agent session tool calls: sends, list, history, search, and status reads (default: enabled). Use allow to restrict agent pairs; enabled=false blocks ordinary cross-agent access. Requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under tree or all visibility. For strict separation, set tools.sessions.visibility to agent or self (tree still admits requester-owned native/ACP children), or use separate gateways.

tools.agentToAgent.enabled.label: Enable Agent-to-Agent Tool
tools.agentToAgent.enabled.help: Enables cross-agent session tool access (default: true); omitted or empty allow permits every agent pair. Set false to block ordinary cross-agent access; requester-owned native subagent and ACP child sessions stay reachable under tree or all visibility. For strict separation, set tools.sessions.visibility to agent or self (tree still admits requester-owned native/ACP children), or use separate gateways.

tools.agentToAgent.allow.label: Agent-to-Agent Target Allowlist
tools.agentToAgent.allow.help: Agent ids or * patterns that may take part in cross-agent calls; the requesting and target agent must both match. Cross-agent access is on by default, and omitted or empty allow permits every pair. Set an explicit list to restrict access; blank entries deny.

session.scope.label: Session Scope
session.scope.help: Sets base session grouping strategy: "per-sender" isolates by sender and "global" shares one session per channel context. Keep "per-sender" for safer multi-user behavior unless deliberate shared context is required.

session.dmScope.label: DM Session Scope
session.dmScope.help: DM session scoping: "main" keeps continuity, while "per-peer", "per-channel-peer", and "per-account-channel-peer" increase isolation. Use isolated modes for shared inboxes or multi-account deployments.

session.groupScope.label: Group Session Scope
session.groupScope.help: Group/channel session scoping: "per-group" keeps rooms separate while the agent main session ambiently watches them, independently of dmScope; "main" merges room context into main and needs no watch. Use "main" only for trusted rooms.

session.notifyOnCreate.label: Notify Home on Session Creation
session.notifyOnCreate.help: Queue a system notice in the owning agent's Home session when a session is created (default: true). Notices include available title and creator metadata and are read on the next Home turn or scheduled automation. Set false to disable; drafts, incognito, internal sessions, and scheduled cron runs are excluded.

session.identityLinks.label: Session Identity Links
session.identityLinks.help: Maps shared identities to provider-prefixed peer IDs so equivalent users resolve to one DM thread (example: telegram:123456). Use this when the same human appears across multiple channels or accounts.

session.resetTriggers.label: Session Reset Triggers
session.resetTriggers.help: Lists message triggers that force a session reset when matched in inbound content. Use sparingly for explicit reset phrases so context is not dropped unexpectedly during normal conversation.

session.reset.label: Session Reset Policy
session.reset.help: Defines the default reset policy object used when no type-specific or channel-specific override applies. By default sessions do not reset automatically; use daily or idle schedules to opt in, while /new and /reset remain available at any time.

session.reset.mode.label: Session Reset Mode
session.reset.mode.help: Selects reset strategy: "none" disables automatic reset (the default), "daily" resets at a configured hour, and "idle" resets after inactivity. /new and /reset remain available in every mode.

session.reset.atHour.label: Session Daily Reset Hour
session.reset.atHour.help: Sets local-hour boundary (0-23) for daily reset mode so sessions roll over at predictable times. Use with mode=daily and align to operator timezone expectations for human-readable behavior.

session.reset.idleMinutes.label: Session Reset Idle Minutes
session.reset.idleMinutes.help: Sets inactivity window before reset for idle mode and can also act as secondary guard with daily mode. Use larger values to preserve continuity or smaller values for fresher short-lived threads.

session.resetByType.label: Session Reset by Chat Type
session.resetByType.help: Overrides reset behavior by chat type (direct, group, thread) when defaults are not sufficient. Use this when group/thread traffic needs different reset cadence than direct messages.

session.resetByType.direct.label: Session Reset (Direct)
session.resetByType.direct.help: Defines reset policy for direct chats and supersedes the base session.reset configuration for that type. Use this as the current direct-message override instead of the legacy dm alias.

session.resetByType.group.label: Session Reset (Group)
session.resetByType.group.help: Defines reset policy for group chat sessions where continuity and noise patterns differ from DMs. Use shorter idle windows for busy groups if context drift becomes a problem.

session.resetByType.thread.label: Session Reset (Thread)
session.resetByType.thread.help: Defines reset policy for thread-scoped sessions, including focused channel thread workflows. Use this when thread sessions should expire faster or slower than other chat types.

session.resetByChannel.label: Session Reset by Channel
session.resetByChannel.help: Provides channel-specific reset overrides keyed by provider/channel id for fine-grained behavior control. Use this only when one channel needs exceptional reset behavior beyond type-level policies.

session.store.label: Session Store Path
session.store.help: Sets the session storage file path used to persist session records across restarts. Use an explicit path only when you need custom disk layout, backup routing, or mounted-volume storage.

session.mainKey.label: Session Main Key
session.mainKey.help: Accepted but ignored: the per-agent main session suffix is always "main". Omit this field; global session scope uses "global" instead.

session.communication.label: Session Communication Defaults
session.communication.help: Defaults for new messages between sessions. Each direction accepts always, ask, or never and defaults to always. Sessions inherit these values until a human selects an override; existing access restrictions still apply.

session.communication.send.label: Send Messages to Other Sessions
session.communication.send.help: Default for initiating messages to other sessions: always permits, ask requires human approval before sending, and never blocks. Requested replies and authorized delegated-task communication keep their existing authority.

session.communication.receive.label: Receive Messages from Other Sessions
session.communication.receive.help: Default for accepting new messages from other sessions: always permits, ask requires human approval before model input or new work, and never blocks. This does not change history visibility or human access.

session.sendPolicy.label: Session Send Policy
session.sendPolicy.help: Controls session delivery using allow/deny rules evaluated against channel, chatType, and key prefixes. This is separate from incoming and outgoing peer-message admission; use session.communication for those defaults.

session.sendPolicy.default.label: Session Send Policy Default Action
session.sendPolicy.default.help: Sets fallback action when no sendPolicy rule matches: "allow" or "deny". Keep "allow" for simpler setups, or choose "deny" when you require explicit allow rules for every destination.

session.sendPolicy.rules.label: Session Send Policy Rules
session.sendPolicy.rules.help: Ordered allow/deny rules evaluated before the default action, for example `{ action: "deny", match: { channel: "discord" } }`. Put most specific rules first so broad rules do not shadow exceptions.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].action.label: Session Send Rule Action
session.sendPolicy.rules[].action.help: Defines rule decision as "allow" or "deny" when the corresponding match criteria are satisfied. Use deny-first ordering when enforcing strict boundaries with explicit allow exceptions.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.label: Session Send Rule Match
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.help: Defines optional rule match conditions that can combine channel, chatType, and key-prefix constraints. Keep matches narrow so policy intent stays readable and debugging remains straightforward.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.channel.label: Session Send Rule Channel
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.channel.help: Matches rule application to a specific channel/provider id (for example discord, telegram, slack). Use this when one channel should permit or deny delivery independently of others.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.chatTyp.label: Session Send Rule Chat Type
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.chatTyp.help: Matches rule application to chat type (direct, group, thread) so behavior varies by conversation form. Use this when DM and group destinations require different safety boundaries.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.keyPref.label: Session Send Rule Key Prefix
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.keyPref.help: Matches a normalized session-key prefix after internal key normalization steps in policy consumers. Use this for general prefix controls, and prefer rawKeyPrefix when exact full-key matching is required.

session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.rawKeyP.label: Session Send Rule Raw Key Prefix
session.sendPolicy.rules[].match.rawKeyP.help: Matches the raw, unnormalized session-key prefix for exact full-key policy targeting. Use this when normalized keyPrefix is too broad and you need agent-prefixed or transport-specific precision.

session.threadBindings.label: Session Thread Bindings
session.threadBindings.help: Shared defaults for thread-bound session spawning and routing across supported channels. Configure global defaults here and override per channel only when behavior differs.

session.threadBindings.enabled.label: Thread Binding Enabled
session.threadBindings.enabled.help: Global master switch for thread-bound session spawning, routing, and delivery. Disable to turn off thread binding globally.

session.threadBindings.idleHours.label: Thread Binding Idle Timeout (hours)
session.threadBindings.idleHours.help: Default inactivity window in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables idle expiry). Default: 24.

session.threadBindings.maxAgeHours.label: Thread Binding Max Age (hours)
session.threadBindings.maxAgeHours.help: Optional hard max age in hours for thread-bound sessions across providers/channels (0 disables hard cap). Default: 0.

session.threadBindings.spawnSessions.label: Thread-Bound Session Spawns
session.threadBindings.spawnSessions.help: Global default gate for creating thread-bound work sessions from sessions_spawn and ACP thread spawns. Default: true when thread bindings are enabled.

session.threadBindings.defaultSpawnConte.label: Thread Spawn Context
session.threadBindings.defaultSpawnConte.help: Default native subagent context for thread-bound spawns. Use "fork" to start from the requester chat or "isolated" for a clean child. Default: "fork".

session.sharing.label: Session Sharing Modes
session.sharing.help: Controls which collaboration modes session owners and administrators may select. Omitted booleans default to enabled; set a mode false to remove it from the picker and reject new selections.

session.sharing.readOnly.label: Allow Read-only Sessions
session.sharing.readOnly.help: Allows sessions to be made read-only for non-participants. Default: true.

session.sharing.suggest.label: Allow Suggest Sessions
session.sharing.suggest.help: Allows suggest visibility. In this phase it enforces the same admission policy as read-only; suggestion queues are configured by a later feature. Default: true.

session.sharing.drafts.label: Allow Draft Sessions
session.sharing.drafts.help: Allows draft visibility, which hides sessions from non-owner, non-admin operators. Default: true.

session.maintenance.label: Session Maintenance
session.maintenance.help: Automatic session-store maintenance controls for app-session archiving, pruning age, entry caps, reset archive retention, and disk budget cleanup. Start in warn mode to observe impact, then enforce once thresholds are tuned.

session.maintenance.coldStorage.label: Chat Cold Storage
session.maintenance.coldStorage.help: Moves inactive chats into compressed JSONL archives while retaining session metadata. Archive files become required history and must be included in backups. Changes apply without restarting the Gateway.

session.maintenance.coldStorage.enabled.label: Automatically Archive Old Chats
session.maintenance.coldStorage.enabled.help: Enables background chat archival (default true). Set false to disable future extraction. A worker checks for eligible chats every minute. This archive policy is separate from deletion and disk-budget cleanup.

session.maintenance.coldStorage.afterDay.label: Archive After Inactive Days
session.maintenance.coldStorage.afterDay.help: Archive chats after this many inactive days (positive integer, default 30). Active work is protected; changing the cutoff takes effect on the next worker pass without a Gateway restart.

session.maintenance.mode.label: Session Maintenance Mode
session.maintenance.mode.help: Determines whether pruning and disk-budget policies are only reported ("warn") or actively applied ("enforce"). Keep "warn" during rollout and switch to "enforce" after validating safe thresholds. Cold storage is enabled by default and has its own opt-out setting.

session.maintenance.pruneAfter.label: Session Prune After
session.maintenance.pruneAfter.help: Archives eligible durable conversations and removes disposable automation entries older than this duration (default `30d`; for example `12h`). Archived conversations retain their history and can be restored; protected or routable conversations remain active.

session.maintenance.archiveDashboardAfte.label: Archive Inactive Dashboard Sessions After
session.maintenance.archiveDashboardAfte.help: Archives inactive sessions started in the OpenClaw app after this duration (for example `7d`) so they remain available without crowding the active session list. Set `false` or `0` to disable this automatic archiving.

session.maintenance.maxEntries.label: Session Max Entries
session.maintenance.maxEntries.help: Caps unarchived session entries (default 5000). Eligible durable overflow conversations are archived with their history; disposable automation entries are removed. Existing archives do not consume the cap. Protected active entries still count and can keep the store above the limit.

session.maintenance.preserveRecent.label: Preserve Recent Sessions
session.maintenance.preserveRecent.help: Protects interactive sessions active within this duration (for example `7d`) from automatic age, count, and disk-budget history eviction. Unset or `false` keeps the normal oldest-first policy. Synthetic model-run, cron, hook, heartbeat, ACP, and sub-agent rows remain eligible for bounded cleanup.

session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetentio.label: Session Reset Archive Retention
session.maintenance.resetArchiveRetentio.help: Age-based retention for archived chats (`*.reset.<timestamp>` and `*.deleted.<timestamp>`). Defaults to keeping archives until the disk budget evicts them oldest-first; set a duration (for example `30d`) to opt into wall-clock deletion, or `false` to disable it explicitly.

session.maintenance.maxDiskBytes.label: Session Max Disk Budget
session.maintenance.maxDiskBytes.help: Per-agent physical disk budget covering SQLite main/WAL and counted session-directory artifacts (for example `500mb`). Defaults to `10gb`; protected data can keep usage above the target. When exceeded, warn mode reports pressure and enforce mode removes old reset/delete artifacts, unreferenced history, then cap-created archives. Manual, age-retention, app-session, recovery, and legacy archives remain protected. Set `false`, `0`, or `"0"` to disable.

session.maintenance.highWaterBytes.label: Session Disk High-water Target
session.maintenance.highWaterBytes.help: Target size after disk-budget cleanup (high-water mark). Defaults to 80% of maxDiskBytes; set explicitly for tighter reclaim behavior on constrained disks. A value that resolves to zero falls back to the default; negative values are invalid. Disable the budget with maxDiskBytes instead.

cron.enabled.label: Automations Enabled
cron.enabled.help: Enables automation execution for stored schedules managed by the gateway. Keep enabled for normal reminder/automation flows, and disable only to pause all automation execution without deleting jobs.

cron.defaultTools.label: Automation Default Tools
cron.defaultTools.help: Tools added when the automations tool creates or explicitly revises a nonempty toolsAllow list, before creator-policy checks and approval. Unset adds nothing. Use toolsAllowMode: "exact" on that request to opt out; [] remains tool-less. Existing jobs and unrelated edits are unchanged.

cron.skipMissedJobs.label: Skip Missed Recurring Automations
cron.skipMissedJobs.help: Skips missed recurring cron/every slots at Gateway startup and schedules their next future occurrence instead of catching up. Default: false. Enable to avoid stale reminders after downtime; one-shot at jobs still catch up.

cron.webhookToken.label: Automations Webhook Bearer Token
cron.webhookToken.help: Bearer token attached to automation webhook POST deliveries when webhook mode is used. Prefer secret/env substitution and rotate this token regularly if shared webhook endpoints are internet-reachable.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.label: Automations Webhook SSRF Policy
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.help: SSRF policy applied to every outbound automation webhook. Private, loopback, link-local, and internal targets stay blocked unless this policy explicitly allows them. Keep unset for strict delivery.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowP.label: Automations Webhook Dangerously Allow Private Network
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowP.help: Allows automation webhooks to private and internal network targets. Keep disabled unless every configured webhook destination is trusted.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.label: Automations Webhook Allowed Hostnames
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowedHostnames.help: Exact hostnames or IP literals allowed for automation webhook delivery, including otherwise blocked targets. Keep the list minimal.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.label: Automations Webhook Blocked Hostnames
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.blockedHostnames.help: Hostname patterns denied before DNS and allow rules for automation webhook delivery. Supports exact hosts and "*.example.com" for subdomains only; add "example.com" separately to block the apex. Empty or unset adds no denials.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Bench.label: Automations Webhook Allow RFC 2544 Benchmark Range
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowRfc2544Bench.help: Allows automation webhooks to RFC 2544 benchmark-range IPs (198.18.0.0/15). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLo.label: Automations Webhook Allow IPv6 Unique Local Range
cron.webhookSsrfPolicy.allowIpv6UniqueLo.help: Allows automation webhooks to IPv6 Unique Local Addresses (fc00::/7). Use only with trusted fake-IP proxy environments.

cron.delivery.label: Automations Default Delivery
cron.delivery.help: Gateway-wide default announce destination for automations that name no route of their own (no channel other than `last`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`, or owner targeting). It replaces the remembered session route at run time and never applies to `none` or `webhook` delivery. A `cron.creators.<profileId>.delivery` or `cron.agents.<agentId>.delivery` default wins over this one.

cron.delivery.channel.label: Automations Default Delivery Channel
cron.delivery.channel.help: Channel for the default destination, such as `telegram`. Omit to use `last` resolution against the default recipient.

cron.delivery.to.label: Automations Default Delivery Recipient
cron.delivery.to.help: Recipient for the default destination, in the channel's target syntax (for example a Telegram chat id such as `-100123456789`).

cron.delivery.threadId.label: Automations Default Delivery Thread
cron.delivery.threadId.help: Optional thread or forum topic for the default destination, such as a Telegram topic id.

cron.delivery.accountId.label: Automations Default Delivery Account
cron.delivery.accountId.help: Optional channel account for the default destination when the channel has several accounts.

cron.agents.label: Automations Per-agent Defaults
cron.agents.help: Per-agent automation defaults keyed by agent id. Each automation uses the entry for its effective agent (its agentId, else the agent in its session key, else the default agent).

cron.agents.*.delivery.label: Agent Automations Default Delivery
cron.agents.*.delivery.help: Default announce destination for this agent's automations that name no route. Replaces `cron.delivery` whole for this agent; fields are not merged. A creator default for the job's human creator wins over it.

cron.agents.*.failureAlert.label: Agent Automations Failure Alert Route
cron.agents.*.failureAlert.help: Default failure-alert route (`mode`, `channel`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`) for this agent's automations. Replaces the `cron.failureAlert` route fields whole; `enabled`, `after`, `cooldownMs`, and `includeSkipped` stay Gateway-wide.

cron.creators.label: Automations Per-creator Defaults
cron.creators.help: Per-creator automation defaults keyed by the Gateway profile id of the human who created the automation. Applies only when the automation records a human profile creator (directly, or as the profile that delegated creation to an agent); legacy automations and channel-only, unknown, agent, or system creators use no creator entry. Keys match exactly.

cron.creators.*.delivery.label: Creator Automations Default Delivery
cron.creators.*.delivery.help: Default announce destination for this person's automations that name no route. Wins over `cron.agents.<agentId>.delivery` and `cron.delivery`; replaces them whole.

cron.creators.*.failureAlert.label: Creator Automations Failure Alert Route
cron.creators.*.failureAlert.help: Default failure-alert route (`mode`, `channel`, `to`, `threadId`, `accountId`) for this person's automations. Wins over the owner agent's route and replaces the `cron.failureAlert` route fields whole; `enabled`, `after`, `cooldownMs`, and `includeSkipped` stay Gateway-wide.

cron.sessionRetention.label: Automations Session Retention
cron.sessionRetention.help: Controls how long completed automation run sessions are kept before pruning (`24h`, `7d`, `1h30m`, or `false` to disable pruning; a zero duration such as `0h` also disables; default: `24h`). Use shorter retention to reduce storage growth on high-frequency schedules.

transcripts.enabled.label: Transcripts Enabled
transcripts.enabled.help: Enables durable automatic meeting notes, the transcripts agent tool, and configured auto-start sources. Default: true. Set false to disable persistence and the tool; explicit meeting transcribe mode retains its bounded live tail.

transcripts.autoStart.label: Transcripts Auto-start Sources
transcripts.autoStart.help: Live transcript sources managed automatically from gateway startup. Each entry is enabled by being present; remove an entry to disable that source. Sources capture continuously unless whenOccupied is enabled.

transcripts.autoStart[].providerId.label: Transcript Source Provider ID
transcripts.autoStart[].providerId.help: Transcript source provider id, such as a Discord voice or future Slack huddle provider. Use the exact id exposed by the provider plugin.

transcripts.autoStart[].sessionId.label: Transcript Session ID
transcripts.autoStart[].sessionId.help: Optional fixed transcript session id for this auto-start source. Ignored when whenOccupied is true. Leave unset for generated ids unless you need a stable daily selector and can avoid same-day collisions.

transcripts.autoStart[].whenOccupied.label: Transcript Capture When Occupied
